title: Missing CSS for new built-in citeproc in Pandoc 2.11
Pandoc 2.11.2 now default to ATX header
description:
This is a change in the [new 2.11.2 release](https://pandoc.org/releases.html#pandoc-2.11.2-2020-11-19). 
> Default to using ATX (##-style) headings for Markdown output (#6662, Aner Lucero). Previously we used Setext (underlined) headings by default for levels 1–2.
>
> Add option --markdown-headings=atx|setext, and deprecate --atx-headers (#6662, Aner Lucero).

That means `rmarkdown::md_document` won't output the same now with Pandoc 2.11.2
``` r
tmp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".Rmd")
xfun::write_utf8(c(
  "# Header 1",
  "",
  "## Header 2",
  "",
  "Some content"), tmp_file
)

# Pandoc 2.7.3
rmarkdown::find_pandoc(dir = "C:/Users/chris/Logiciel/pandoc/pandoc-2.7.3", cache = FALSE)
#> $version
#> [1] '2.7.3'
#> 
#> $dir
#> [1] "C:/Users/chris/Logiciel/pandoc/pandoc-2.7.3"

res <- rmarkdown::render(tmp_file, "md_document")
#> processing file: file9c046df1eed.Rmd
#> output file: file9c046df1eed.knit.md
#> "C:/Users/chris/Logiciel/pandoc/pandoc-2.7.3/pandoc" +RTS -K512m -RTS file9c046df1eed.utf8.md --to markdown_strict --from markdown+autolink_bare_uris+tex_math_single_backslash --output file9c046df1eed.md --standalone
#> 
#> Output created: file9c046df1eed.md
xfun::file_string(res)
#> Header 1
#> ========
#> 
#> Header 2
#> --------
#> 
#> Some content

# Pandoc 2.11.2
rmarkdown::find_pandoc(version = "2.11.2", cache = FALSE)
#> $version
#> [1] '2.11.2'
#> 
#> $dir
#> [1] "C:/Users/chris/scoop/shims"

res <- rmarkdown::render(tmp_file, "md_document")
#> processing file: file9c046df1eed.Rmd
#> output file: file9c046df1eed.knit.md
#> "C:/Users/chris/scoop/shims/pandoc" +RTS -K512m -RTS file9c046df1eed.utf8.md --to markdown_strict --from markdown+autolink_bare_uris+tex_math_single_backslash --output file9c046df1eed.md --standalone
#> 
#> Output created: file9c046df1eed.md
xfun::file_string(res)
#> # Header 1
#> 
#> ## Header 2
#> 
#> Some content


res <- rmarkdown::render(tmp_file, "md_document", 
                         output_options = list(pandoc_args = "--markdown-headings=setext"))
#> processing file: file9c046df1eed.Rmd
#> output file: file9c046df1eed.knit.md
#> "C:/Users/chris/scoop/shims/pandoc" +RTS -K512m -RTS file9c046df1eed.utf8.md --to markdown_strict --from markdown+autolink_bare_uris+tex_math_single_backslash --output file9c046df1eed.md --standalone --markdown-headings=setext
#> 
#> Output created: file9c046df1eed.md
xfun::file_string(res)
#> Header 1
#> ========
#> 
#> Header 2
#> --------
#> 
#> Some content
```


We need to 

* either communicate the the default has change and use pandoc default
* or add `"--markdown-headings=setext"` argument to have the default behavioir of `md_document()`.
* Make sure `--atx-headers` is not more used with pandoc 2.11.2+

title: Incorrect format for HTML tables
description:
Here is a minimal reprex
````md
---
title: "table format"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
knitr::kable(iris, "html")
```
````

This is caused by the change in https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/pull/1895 and the fact that `kable` html output does not include odd and even on rows. 

Discovered by a user while loading kableExtra.
````md
---
title: "table format"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
knitr::kable(iris)
```
```` 

**kableExtra** is modifying the format for `knitr::kable` that default to markdown pipe output. By auto formating to html, just loading the package modify the behavior of kable. 

Two solutions: 
* We could revert and fix another solution for #1893 
* Modify **knitr** html table to include the `odd` and `even` class.

For now the former seems better, as there is a JS solution for #1893 (see https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1893#issuecomment-688877872)

cc @apreshill

title: Nested tibble containing large lists can make rmarkdown slow and generate huge html file
description:
When making a nested tibble with large lists (or tibbles) in rmarkdown/rnotebook, 
"knit/preview"  causes time consuming in pandoc and generate a very large html file.
Thus, the inner contents of a nested tibble should be removed before printing as a default option.  

Below is an example:

````
---
title: "R Notebook"
output: html_notebook
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
d <- nycflights13::flights
ds <- 
  bind_rows(d, d, d, d, d) %>% 
  mutate(no = rep(1:5, each = nrow(d))) %>% 
  relocate(no)

grouped <-
  ds %>% 
  group_by(no) %>% 
  nest()

grouped  ## <- it will make Rstudio slow and generate a huge html file, it was not affected by "max.print"
```

````

title: Re-consider a more user-friendly anchor symbol, or make the default FALSE for anchor_sections
description: Re: https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/pull/1884 I think the default `anchor_sections = TRUE` is hard as a default given the `#` symbol. It isn’t intuitive or self-explanatory, and most people don’t know that those are called anchors, so finding the argument `anchor_sections` to turn it off is hard to figure out. Also, because the hashtag symbol has a special meaning as a header in markdown syntax, it looks like a weird markdown rendering error when you see it- I even knew this feature was in place and STILL had a freak out and initially thought I was seeing an odd markdown parsing artifact at first. On the other hand, precisely because many users may not be familiar with the concept of anchor headers (even if they enjoy them!), it will be hard to figure out that you can turn it _ON_ as well if the default is `FALSE`. And I think the utility is extremely useful for users (adding anchor symbols to my HTML-based R Markdown outputs is often the first thing I do, and the first thing I asked my intern Desiree to do!- thank you @atusy for recognizing that need and adding the functionality 🌟 ). But, the more I use it in my own recent work across output formats and see users attempting to trouble-shoot this new feature, I think that if we want to keep `TRUE` as the default, we should switch to an svg symbol. This is familiar to many users because it is how GitHub `README`s look, `pkgdown` websites, and now `distill` as well, and there is even a link emoji :link:. All of the above boils down to: + If we keep the `#` symbol, I lean towards setting `FALSE` as the default across the board. + If we are open to an svg (single file, open source like the link icon here: https://material.io/resources/icons/?search=link&style=baseline), I think `TRUE` can stay as the default (with slide decks and perhaps pagedown setting it to `FALSE`) ## Some examples with svg icons --- By filing an issue to this repo, I promise that - [x] I have fully read the issue guide at https://yihui.org/issue/. - [x] I have provided the necessary information about my issue. - If I'm asking a question, I have already asked it on Stack Overflow or RStudio Community, waited for at least 24 hours, and included a link to my question there. - If I'm filing a bug report, I have included a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example, and have also included `xfun::session_info('rmarkdown')`. title: Should anchors be added to empty headings?
description:
The new `anchor_sections` feature adds anchors to empty headings in HTML documents and I think it may be better not to add anchors to these headings.

As one example, in learnr tutorials it's common to insert a pause by adding a blank level-3 heading. There's no need for the anchor in these cases and they're likely to be confusing since they appear in empty space where there is no text.

I'd be happy to submit a PR.

title: BUG with pdfcrop and fig_crop in v2.5 => plots not resized properly
description:
(Bug checked with cderv) The Rmd example below ~(except the \ before some triple backticks)~(edited) describes a bug/regression introduced in v2.5 (and probably in v2.4) with pdfcrop and fig_crop. In Beamer presentation, the plots are not resized properly anymore in the slide. It is ugly. This is due to the **fig_crop: true** line in the yaml header. The same ugly slides appear if the line **is missing**. Currently, the only solution is to write **fig_crop: false** to get something clean, as in v2.3 and previous versions. 


````
---
title: "A regression in rmarkdown from v_2.3 to v_2.5"
author: "pkR-pkR + cderv"
date: "October 23, 2020"
output: 
  beamer_presentation:
    template: default
    latex_engine: pdflatex
    keep_tex: true
    toc: false
    fig_caption: false
    fig_crop: true
fontsize: 10pt
--- 


# A regression in rmarkdown from v_2.3 to v_2.5

A regression in rmarkdown both on Windows and Debian:

- rmarkdown_2.3.tar.gz properly resizes the following plots
- rmarkdown_2.5.tar.gz badly resizes the following plots

The issue occurs/is linked to pdfcrop:

- Missing line **fig_crop**  in yaml header => BAD
- **fig_crop: true** in yaml header => BAD
- **fig_crop: false** in yaml header => OK

The current default settings break all previous .Rmd files.

Furthermore, pdfcrop on Windows is very slow.

Please, revert to the previous settings (pdfcrop disabled)!

(Bug reproduced by cderv)


# corrplot::corrplot() => OK with v_2.3, Bad with v_2.5

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
corrplot::corrplot(matrix(runif(900), 30, 30))
```


# lattice::levelplot() => OK with v_2.3, Bad with v_2.5

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
lattice::levelplot(matrix(runif(900), 30, 30))
```

````

title: Inconsistent behaviour of rmarkdown::render() ouput_file= parameter while rendering
description:
<!--
Please keep the below portion in your issue. Your issue will be closed if any of the boxes is not checked (i.e., replace `[ ]` by `[x]`). In certain (rare) cases, you may be exempted if you give a brief explanation (e.g., you are only making a suggestion for improvement). Thanks!
-->

Rendering an R Notebook document:

When specifying an output file to the `render()` function, the `.nb.html` is appended to the supplied file name inconsistently.
1. If the base name does not contain a dot or an extension, the file name is appended with `.nb.html`
2. If the base name contains an extension without an underscore (`_`) --and possibly other punctuation--, no `.nb.html` is appended.
3. If the extension does contain underscore (`_`), then `.nb.html` is appended.

I have not tested this with other output formats other than notebook. I think case 1 and case 3 are ok, but case 2 is inconsistent.
Always appending (or always not appending) would be a consistent behaviour, imho.  Perhaps checking if the `.nb.html` extension exists could be a reason to not append it.

MWE included:

```{r}
ll = "---\ntitle: \"Test\"\noutput: html_notebook\n---\n\n```{r}\nplot(cars)\n```\n"
f = tempfile(fileext=".Rmd")
writeLines(ll, con=f)
# Case 1: Appended
rmarkdown::render(input=f, output_file="A", output_dir=".", quiet=T)
# Case 2: Not appended
rmarkdown::render(input=f, output_file="A.b", output_dir=".", quiet=T)
# Case 3: Appended
rmarkdown::render(input=f, output_file="A.b_c", output_dir=".", quiet=T)
# Other tests
rmarkdown::render(input=f, output_file="A.verylongconformingextension", output_dir=".", quiet=T)
rmarkdown::render(input=f, output_file="A.verylongnon-conformingextension", output_dir=".", quiet=T)
# These next two understandably fail
rmarkdown::render(input=f, output_file="Another.verylongnon$conformingextension", output_dir=".", quiet=T)
rmarkdown::render(input=f, output_file="A.v$x", output_dir=".", quiet=T)
# But this one does not
rmarkdown::render(input=f, output_file="A.v=x", output_dir=".", quiet=T)

title: Invalid HTML in prerendered shiny documents
description:
`rmarkdown::run()` on a Rmd document with `runtime: shiny_prerendered` serves invalid HTML.

Consider the follwing Rmd file _invalidhtml/invalidhtml.Rmd_ with contents
```
---
title: "Invalid HTML"
output: html_document
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

This creates invalid HTML.
```

Running this document with
```R
rmarkdown::run("invalidhtml/invalidhtml.Rmd")
```

Will serve a document with the follwing invalid HTML (I removed most content for brevity)
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8"/>
  <script type="application/shiny-singletons"></script>
  <!-- text snippets removed -->
</head>
<body><!DOCTYPE html>

<html>

<head>
  <!-- text snippets removed -->
</head>
  <!-- text snippets removed -->
</body>
</html></body>
</html>
```

The problem is that rmarkdown is rendering the Rmd file to a standalone HTML document, and returning the whole HTML document in the shiny app's UI function. The UI function, however, expects only the body of the document.

I am not sure if this issue has not been discovered until now, or if it's accepted for simplicity (I think most major browsers accept this invalid HTML).

title: custom-style in docx only works for block-level text, does not work for inline text
description:
Using latest CRAN rmarkdown v2.4 and pandoc 2.7 As per the [pandoc documentation](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#custom-styles), it should be possible to use custom styles in docx documents. Custom styles need to first be defined in the reference docx and then they can be used either in inline text (span tags or "bracketed spans" syntax) or in paragraph level text (div tags or "fenced divs" syntax). In all following code chunks, [this reference word document](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/files/5337076/ref.docx), which has a custom style named "deanstyle" using red colour and underlined, is used as the "ref.docx". The following Rmd works correctly and produced the word "test" in red and underlined: ``` --- title: "testing custom styles inline vs block level" output: word_document: reference_docx: ref.docx ---
test
``` The following also works: ``` --- title: "testing custom styles inline vs block level" output: word_document: reference_docx: ref.docx --- ::: {custom-style="deanstyle"} test ::: ``` So it works with block level. But if I try to use inline text to have specific words with the style, it does not work: ``` --- title: "testing custom styles inline vs block level" output: word_document: reference_docx: ref.docx --- test ``` or ``` --- title: "testing custom styles inline vs block level" output: word_document: reference_docx: ref.docx --- [test]{custom-style="deanstyle"} ```

title: RMarkdown visual editor: toggle ability to surround (rather than replace) selected text
description:
Hi there,
I absolutely love the new visual markdown editor in the v 1.4 preview release. What a game changer! Thank you!

I'm wondering if it's possible to toggle surrounding selected text with quotes/backticks/parens in the visual RMarkdown editor, not just in the regular editor. 

In the Code > Editing pane in Global Options, there's this menu, where you can select whether to surround selected text with quotes/brackets (versus just replacing the text). I find this feature really convenient, but I've noticed that when I switch to the visual editor, my selections now get replaced instead of surrounded. 

![Screen Shot 2020-10-02 at 15 30 35](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37053323/94962296-3a1cd000-04c4-11eb-81df-c22fa97df6c1.png)

Is there a separate toggle somewhere for the visual editor, or does this option not exist? If it doesn't, would you consider adding it?

Thanks again for the great tool!

title: Improve pandoc lua filters handling to make it more usable from other package
description:
We are currently adding some lua filter also in https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/pull/940 

There are several pieces missing to make things easier to extend what is done in **rmarkdown**

1. `pandoc_lua_filters` helper is currently only working for **rmarkdown** filter. We currently create the same helper for each 📦 

2. The lua filters are not including the same way in all 📦 so it is not easy to make another package filter run before or after another one. 

About 2, sometime it is add inside the `pre_processor` part of the function https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/284b685c2feb68083b3434c6ca38717cd61cbeea/R/html_document_base.R#L109-L110

and in others outside of the pre preprocessor in the main format function, **before** `pandoc_args` argument
https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/284b685c2feb68083b3434c6ca38717cd61cbeea/R/pdf_document.R#L145-L149

We could start fixing this by being more aligned in all format. 

And to improve, I think we need a mechanism for choosing the order of the filter (pandoc will run in the order of the command line). This is necessary to avoir conflicts. There are several ways to that IMO - one is to make lua filters activate with a switch.

title: Headerless tables not formatted correctly
description:
Pandoc's [simple tables](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#extension-simple_tables) may or may not contain a header1. Headerless tables are, however, not formatted correctly by __rmarkdown__. The following document... ```Rmd --- title: "Beheaded tables" output: html_document --- Right Left Center Default ------- ------ ---------- ------- 12 12 12 12 123 123 123 123 1 1 1 1 Table: Simple table with header ------- ------ ---------- ------- 12 12 12 12 123 123 123 123 1 1 1 1 ------- ------ ---------- ------- Table: Simple table without header ``` ...renders to: ![beheaded tables](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12914806/92421420-bd266100-f178-11ea-9aa6-a8643ee870c0.png) I ran into this while attempting to write a table with a header column – for which a syntax [is underway](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/1024#issuecomment-629204782), but not available right now – and hence without a header row. My attempt to overcome __rmarkdown__'s limitation is as follows (based on [this solution by Jan](https://stackoverflow.com/a/44716658)): ``````Rmd --- title: "Patched up tables" output: html_document --- ```{r, echo=FALSE} table_header <- c("Title", "Author", "Version", "Last edit", "License", "Address", "Contact") table_body <- c("Headerless tables not formatted correctly", "fkohrt", "1.0.0", "2020-09-08", "CC0 1.0", "https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1893", "https://github.com/fkohrt") table_frame <- data.frame(table_body) row.names(table_frame) <- table_header table <- kableExtra::kable_styling(kableExtra::column_spec(knitr::kable(table_frame, format="html", caption="Not so simple table without header row"), 1, bold=TRUE), bootstrap_options = c("condensed")) gsub(".*", "", table) ``` `````` ...which looks like this: ![patched up tables](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12914806/92422899-56587600-f17f-11ea-90dd-e822bd987b27.png) But I believe there's no reason to limit R Markdown to ... capitated tables.

title: Inconsistent behaviour for multiple YAML metadata blocks
description:
The [Pandoc MANUAL](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#extension-yaml_metadata_block) says: > A document may contain multiple metadata blocks. If two metadata blocks attempt to set the same field, the value from the second block will be taken. This is the behaviour as of Pandoc 2.8 (jgm/pandoc@9c7f75a), earlier versions gave preference to the value from the first block. But it appears this change has not been implemented in the `rmarkdown::metadata` object, as the example below demonstrates: ````Rmd --- title: "Title 1" output: html_document --- --- title: "Title 2" --- ```{r, echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'} cat(rmarkdown::metadata$title) ``` ```` This leads to the following document: ![metadata](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12914806/92313704-f753ff00-efce-11ea-92f6-95156708b852.png) Note that the title of the document is set according to the second YAML metadata block, but the `rmarkdown::metadata` object reports a different title.

title: pandoc_convert() evaluates output argument in wrong directory
description:
In `pandoc_convert()`, the `output` argument is forced after changing the working directory. This is unexpected, not documented, and breaks `downlit::downlit_md_path()` and perhaps others. PR follows.

``` r
input <- tempfile("in", fileext = ".md")
input
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmpl3bcya/in6d94718e979a.md"
writeLines("# Document", input)

output <- "out.md"

# Breaks
writeLines("bogus", output)
normalizePath(output, mustWork = FALSE)
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp9ZZAHN/reprex6bed4897d478/out.md"
rmarkdown::pandoc_convert(input, output = normalizePath(output, mustWork = FALSE), verbose = TRUE)
#> /usr/lib/rstudio/bin/pandoc/pandoc +RTS -K512m -RTS /tmp/Rtmpl3bcya/in6d94718e979a.md --output out.md
readLines(output)
#> [1] "bogus"

# Works if we compute output outside of call
writeLines("bogus", output)
output <- normalizePath(output, mustWork = FALSE)
rmarkdown::pandoc_convert(input, output = output, verbose = TRUE)
#> /usr/lib/rstudio/bin/pandoc/pandoc +RTS -K512m -RTS /tmp/Rtmpl3bcya/in6d94718e979a.md --output /tmp/Rtmp9ZZAHN/reprex6bed4897d478/out.md
readLines(output)
#> [1] "Document" "========"
```

title: R Markdown Website not respecting language in _site.yml
description:
The following `_site.yml` creates a website with an `<html>` tag that does not specify a language. (Accessibility checkers will throw a complaint about this.)

```
name: "My Website!"
output_dir: "docs"
output:
  html_document:
    lang: en
```

If within an individual .Rmd file a language is specified in its YAML header, the correct HTML is created.

For example, within the .Rmd you use:

```
---
title: "Title of Page"
author: "Cool R Markdown User"
lang: en
---
```

The rendered document then contains: `<html lang="en" xml:lang="en">`

Is this a feature, or a bug? (Perhaps it's good practice to specify a language for each page individually?)

- This question was originally asked here: https://community.rstudio.com/t/r-markdown-website-not-respecting-language-in-site-yml/77769

title: JS renderer initialization in 'asis' Markdown chunck
description:
Hi,

First of all, my respect for the incredible work accomplished with RMarkdown/knitr : I'm thankful and impressed.

This is a question and perhaps issue [I asked in StackOveflow without getting a conclusive answer](https://stackoverflow.com/q/63534247/13513328):
"
'asis' chuncks are very useful to output a list of objects in a Markdown document, see following examples : [Highcharter](https://stackoverflow.com/a/63437006/13513328), [DT](https://stackoverflow.com/a/63533888/13513328), [Leaflet](https://stackoverflow.com/a/63495651/13513328), ...

However, in the above examples, the list of object won't print if the renderer hasn't been called once in a previous chunck, so that it gets initialized : this is a tricky workaround, and I found the solution more by trial / error than by finding it in documentation.

Before opening a possible Rmarkdown issue, I would like to know if I'm missing a knitr command/option to properly initialize the renderer in order to let the 'asis' chuncks work straight away.
"
This is a reprex with DT :
````
---
title: "Printing paged tables from a list of dataframes in Rmarkdown"
output:
  html_document:
  df_print: paged
---



```{r,echo=F}
library(DT)
library(rmarkdown)
library(purrr)
library(knitr)

df_list <- list("cars" = mtcars, "flowers" = iris)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)


```

```{r}
# If this first initialization isn't run, tabs won't print
DT::datatable(data.frame(Init="Init"))
```

# Test tabs {.tabset}

```{r, results='asis' }
imap(df_list, ~{
      cat('## Subtab ',.y,'\n')
      cat('\n')
      DT::datatable(.x) %>%
      htmltools::tagList() %>% as.character() %>% cat() })

```
````

If you remove : 
```
DT::datatable(data.frame(Init="Init"))
```
from the above code, the renderer won't initialize and the list will only print blank tabs.

From the answers to my question on StackOverflow, I came to this [vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/knitr/vignettes/knit_print.html), but didn't succeed to setup meta parameters to avoid the first initialization before printing the loop.

As this problems seems common to many JS libraries (DT, Leaflet, Highcharter,...), and a lot of users have the same question, I was wondering if this is a known issue or if we overlooked an obvious renderer / knitr option? If we overlooked an option, a clarification on this point would be very helpful! 

Thanks for your feedback,

title: line numbering is not working with pandoc 2.10.1
description:
```r
xfun::write_utf8(
  c(
    "# Line numbers",
    "",
    "```{r, attr.source='.numberLines'}",
    "x <- 1",
    "x+1",
    "```"
  ),
  "test.Rmd"
)

rmarkdown::find_pandoc()

# converting with Rmarkdown
rmarkdown::render("test.Rmd", 
                  output_format = rmarkdown::html_document(
                    highlight = "tango", 
                    keep_md = TRUE)
)
# open the resulting test.html and you'll have no numbering

# converting with pandoc only
rmarkdown::pandoc_convert("test.md", 
                          output = "test-pandoc.html", 
                          options = c("-s", "--highlight-style=tango"), 
                          verbose = TRUE)
# Open the resulting test-pandoc.html and you get correct numbering. 
```

This is an issue with pandoc (skylighting) and boostrap used by Rmarkdown 

boostrap defines 
```css
pre {
  overflow: auto;
}
```
and previously pandoc insured that overflow was visible with line number
```css
.sourceCode { overflow: visible; } -- needed for line numbers
```
but it has been removed (here https://github.com/jgm/skylighting/commit/7234122d64431e5f73af93637af1746c5f92ab07)

If we add it back to the Rmd file, it is working as expected
````md
---
title: "Untitled"
author: "Unauthored"
date: "0/20/2020"
output:
  html_document:
    highlight: tango
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{css, echo = FALSE}
.sourceCode { overflow: visible; }
```


## Line numbers

```{r, attr.source='.numberLines'}
if (TRUE) {
  x <- 1:10
  x + 1
}
```
````

An issue in pandoc will be opened to that this works again. 

_Moved from https://github.com/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/issues/271, originally reported by @aosavi_

title: `render` with `intermediates_dir` argument fails when applying original template to `output_format`

This is related to #457.
When `intermediates_dir` is specified, `pandoc` runs under the `intermediates_dir`.
As a result, pandoc fails to find template when its path is relative from `input_file`'s working directory.

There are two ways to solve the problem.

1. normalize path of the template file
2. copy the template file to `intermediates_dir`

Which would be a better choice? Maybe 1?

````r
pandoc_args <- rmarkdown::html_document()$pandoc$args
file.copy(
  pandoc_args[which(pandoc_args == '--template') + 1L],

)
writeLines(
  paste('---',
        'output:',
        '  html_document:',
        '    template: template.html',
        '---',
        sep = '\n'),
  'example.Rmd'
)
rmarkdown::render('example.Rmd', intermediates_dir = tempdir())

title: Path separators in YAML css parameter rendered as backslashes in HTML hrefs under Windows
description:
Path separators in the `css` field in YAML head matter are converted to backslashes when rendering rmarkdown to HTML formats under Windows. This leads to HTML files with backslashes in the hrefs. This can be fixed with a few minor code changes.

### Expected behavior

When RMarkdown documents are rendered as HTML, `href` fields use forward slashes as path separators

### Observed behavior 

Under windows, `href` fields for links generated from the `css` parameter use backslashes as path separators.

### Related issues and PRs

This is similar to #512, #1289, #1293, and #1302.

### Additional comments

I will submit a PR (changing 3 lines of code) as a suggested fix. See <https://github.com/jonathan-g/rmarkdown/tree/css-slash-fix>

I am not submitting a reprex because it would involve multiple rmarkdown source files (`.Rmd` and `.css`) to reproduce this behavior. Here is an example of a snippet from rmarkdown YAML head matter that will reproduce this:
``` yaml
css: "css/style.css"
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: false
```
This results in a line in the generated HTML file
```
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css\style.css" type="text/css" />
```

title: Square brackets in md_document
description:
Hi dev team, I'm using `pkgdown` to document my package, and I thus have to generate an `index.md` file. My documentation has some square brackets, and the knitting process unexpectedly escapes them. However, it seems that this is then interpreted incorrectly in the further HTML conversion, as the brackets disappear and the inside turns to italic (I think it triggers the math formula format). This happens whether I use the Rstudio "knit" button or I use `knitr::knit` myself. For now (until I'm able to correct it), you can see an example [here](https://danchaltiel.github.io/crosstable/index.html#margins-and-totals): the second row of the table should have square brackets, as median[IQR]. This also happens using the RStudio "preview" button on the `md` file. This behavior has already been described in 2016 in https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/667 but was closed without being truly solved. The OP accepted a workaround: including all bracket sequences as inline code. However, this won't work in generated HTML tables such as mine. Here is a reproducible example: ```Rmd --- output: md_document --- I want to describe something as median[IQR]. ``` Resulting `md` file: ```md I want to describe something as median\[IQR\]. ``` Resulting HTML: ```html

I want to describe something as median

I Q R
.

``` If I manually unescape these square brackets in the `md` file, the HTML result is OK. However, there can eventually be a whole lot of them, in multiple files, so this doesn't seem a sustainable solution to me. title: Enhancement: support for non-standard RMarkdown directory structures.
description:
I have the same issue as was raised in #146 (and I originally posted this issue as a comment there).

I organize my reveal.js slides for a semester in a directory structure:

    semester:
        lecture_lib (common material: css, js, etc.)
            assets (custom css themes, custom js, images, etc. that are shared across the whole project)
            revealjs
            font-awesome
        slides
            class_01
                assets (per-class assets)
                    images (images to include)
                    videos (video files)
                    fig (figures generated by RMarkdown)
            class_02
                assets (per-class assets)
                    images (images to include)
                    videos (video files)
                    fig (figures generated by RMarkdown)
            c;lass_03
                assets (per-class assets)
                    images (images to include)
                    videos (video files)
                    fig (figures generated by RMarkdown)
            ...

This lets me keep a consistent structure for each lecture.

If I use pandoc 2.7.x, RMarkdown works fine with my directory structures, but if I use any later version of Pandoc rendering the .Rmd file fails with an error message about `relativeTo()` because `lib_dir` is not a descendant of `output_dir`.

This is not a bug per-se since [by design](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/146#issuecomment-48591200), RMarkdown does not support this kind of directory structure. But it is something that a number of people have expressed interest in (#146, #472, https://github.com/jayhesselberth/widgetdown/issues/4, https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/95).

My non-standard (and unsupported) directory structure worked for many years, using a custom `reveal.js` HTML template for Pandoc to handle a more flexible directory structure but it broke several months ago when Pandoc moved to version 2.9 and rmarkdown introduced `html_dependency_header_attrs` to fix the duplication of HTML class attributes from `<section>` to `<h[1-9]>` tags that Pandoc introduced with version 2.8 or 2.9. I was able to work around this by continuing to work with an older Pandoc version (2.7).

I raise this in part because I think I could address this with a relatively minor PR (I have this working on a fork of rmarkdown at https://github.com/jonathan-g/rmarkdown/tree/minimal-tree-fix, and it changes about 14 lines of code, all of which are in the `html_dependencies_as_string()` function). I need to test this patch more before submitting it as a PR, but it should allow this non-standard directory structure through the YAML `lib_dir` parameter without disturbing any use cases except where `lib_dir` begins with `..`.

title: Question: how to define the scope of inline chunks
description:
Dear @yihui and colleagues, this is a rather technical question (see link to RStudio community at the end)

Within a package I am working on, I am creating optional vignettes that the user can build on demand.

I would like the building of such vignettes happens in an environment that does not have the global one as parent.
So, my custom vignette building function includes something like:

```r
vignette_env <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
rmarkdown::render(path.to.file, envir = vignette_env)
```

The problem, when I do that, is that the package loaded and the objects created inside knitr chunks are not visible (in scope) to inline calls that follow, although they are visible to other chunks.

I don't understand why and how to cope with this scoping issue.

I have posted a question on RStudio community **with a full reprex**  (https://community.rstudio.com/t/scoping-environment-struggle-in-r-markdown/70709), but failed to attract any attention in more than a week.

**It would be nice if Rmarkdown had an integrated option to output to mindmaps. (Preferably as .html than .mm).**

[markmap-lib](https://github.com/gera2ld/markmap-lib), a Nodejs package seems good, which uses [markmap](https://github.com/dundalek/markmap), a JavaScript library. Outputs nice mind maps in .html from .md
There is [Rmarkmap](https://github.com/seifer08ms/Rmarkmap), an R Interface to markmap library, also based on markmap. But it seems to be inactive.

A related R package, https://github.com/pzhaonet/mindr converts markdown (.md or .Rmd) files to mind maps (.mm, freeplane format) and vice versa. But it seems this produces/uses document outline only. Hence not very useful to quickly write markdown and visualize all points as mind map. 

A question was [asked on Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/53755281/rstudio-knitr-mind-mapping/53755499#53755499), regarding tikz package.

(I am not a developer. I am just a user of RStudio. Consider this a suggestion for improvement.)

title: Set pandoc's variable toc-title as an argument for html_document
description:
Thanks @atusy for allowing users to specify `toc-title` for `html_document` via #1771.

I would like to discuss the following two issues :

1. Users are tempting to use `toc_title` (instead of dashed `toc-title`) like `toc_float`. Could we add that? I was also one of them, following the existing underlined-metaname convention for Rmd yaml.
2. Could we consider moving the option to the same level as `toc`, right under `html_document` instead of the top-level in the YAML?

I think the following would be more logical.

``` yaml
---
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc-title: Table of Contents   # Also need to allow underlined `toc_title`
---
```

title: Rendering Rmd in a readonly directory does not work
description:
Hi, 

We package Rmd files with our shared packages and in downstream apps we load and render them. So the source directory with the Rmd file is read-only (since the shared package is in a system library) and so we cannot knit directly in it. I tried to use the parameters intermediates_dir and knit_root_dir and set them to a custom output directory (which is writable) but I get an error when knitting the document.
```
!!! Error: Cannot write tmp file `tmp-pdfcrop-2449.tex' (Permission denied)!
Error: LaTeX failed to compile /home/ak6/output/TestDoc.tex. See https://yihui.org/tinytex/r/#debugging for debugging tips.
```

I looked through the [source code](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/render.R) and it appears to be in these lines. It is explicitly setting the working directory to the dirname of the `input file`. 

```
  # execute within the input file's directory
  oldwd <- setwd(dirname(abs_path(input)))
  on.exit(setwd(oldwd), add = TRUE)
```

Can it use the `intermediates_dir` or `knit_root_dir` instead? 

The actual error shows up later in the call to `knitr::knit()`  since that calls getwd() but the lines above seem to be where it's changing the working directory. I also tried setting `root.dir` in knitr options as suggested [here](https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/277) but that didn't seem to work either. The only hack that I can think of is to temporarily copy the Rmd file from its read-only input location to `/tmp` or something like that, generate the output and then delete that temp file. Seems like a waste.

I don't know if this can be fixed based on how knitr works but thought I would ask. 

A reproducible example is below.

1) create directories called 'Rmd' and 'output'
2) rename the attached file to TestDoc.Rmd and copy to the 'Rmd' folder
3) make the 'Rmd' folder read-only
4) run the following code

```
rmarkdown::render(input="~/Rmd/TestDoc.Rmd",
                  output_format="pdf_document",
                  output_dir="~/output",
                  intermediates_dir="~/output",
                  knit_root_dir = "~/output",
                  quiet=TRUE)
```

title: Check older R versions using CI
description:
There was a recent change (https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1831) that caused rmarkdown to fail on R versions older than 3.6.

This issue could have been caught before being released to CRAN if rmarkdown was being checked on older R versions using CI.

The tidyverse team does this to ensure our packages support the last 5 minor R releases, which is now R 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6 and 4.0

It would be great if we could do rountily have similar checks for the knitr / rmarkdown stack, to ensure we don't lose compatibility with these critical packages accidently in the future.

title: Rmd-to-html codeblock highlight delivers unpleasant information for screen readers
description:
When code highlight is applied for `rmarkdown::html_document` output, screen-reader users experience unneccessary difficulties in reading code blocks.

I am not going to duplicate the issue here so please kindly visit [pandoc/issue#6352](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/6352#issuecomment-626106786) that I have detailed there.

Fortunately, the fix will be implemented in the next `pandoc` version; however, I wanted to create backword solution towards previous versions <= v2.9.2.1.

To this end, I have attempted to write a simple `lua` filter, but that does not seem to be possible unless we consider postprocessing an html output.

Many blind people, including me, have already experienced this challenge caused by redundant codeblock ID information, and I think we need to come up with some universal solutions for Rmd-to-html output process given that many tutorials and online books have been produced by rmarkdown/pandoc under the hood.

Does anyone have a great solution?

description:
I'm trying to make a package that specifies a custom vctrs-based data type. Part of its behavior is to be easily readable as part of a data.frame or tibble when working in the interactive portion of an RMarkdown document, the primary part of my workflow. I was able to achieve that fairly quickly using the `format` method. This is good when the table is rendered in text. However, that is not the case in chunk output rendered interactively (with ctrl+enter).

If I am correct (and I may not be) `rmarkdown::paged_table` is the way data frames are rendered below R chunks when working interactively. I thought the rendering would involve some call to `print` or `format` or some related method, but it does not. When rendered, all my custom objects are stuck with the uninformative name <S3: vrm_vector3>.

**My primary question is: how can that <S3: vrm_vector3> be changed?**

As a quick fix, I thought I could approach this by converting some part of the process in html_paged.R into a generic (e.g. paged_table_obj_sum). Unfortunately, it appears that rmarkdown::paged_table is not called when rendering interactively.

The reprex is below. 

Am I way off in finding what method is being called when the paged table in RStudio is being built?

````
---
title: "sample_reprex"
author: "Mark Roman Miller"
date: "5/13/2020"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tibble)
library(vctrs)
library(zeallot)

new_vector3 <- function(x=double(), y=double(), z=double()) {
  vec_assert(x, ptype=double())
  vec_assert(y, ptype=double())
  vec_assert(z, ptype=double())
  new_rcrd(list(x=x, y=y, z=z), class="vrm_vector3")
}

vector3 <- function(x, y, z) {
  c(x, y, z) %<-% vec_cast_common(x, y, z, .to=double())
  c(x, y, z) %<-% vec_recycle_common(x, y, z)
  new_vector3(x, y, z)
}

format.vrm_vector3 <- function(v, ...) {
  x <- field(v, "x")
  y <- field(v, "y")
  z <- field(v, "z")

  out <- paste0("(", x, ", ", y, ", ", z, ")")
  out[is.na(x) | is.na(y) | is.na(z)] <- NA

  out
}

vec_ptype_abbr.vrm_vector3 <- function(x, ...) {
  "vector3"
}

sqrt_1_3 <- sqrt(1/3)

sample_table <- tibble(pos = vector3(c(1, 0, 0, sqrt_1_3), c(0, 1, 0, sqrt_1_3), c(0, 0, 1, sqrt_1_3)))

rmarkdown::paged_table(sample_table)

sample_table

## 问题

rmarkdown 自带的两个 lua 脚本 `rmarkdown:::pandoc_lua_filters()` 对 html 和 pdf 输出自动加持了，但是对 beamer 幻灯片没有启用，感觉有点奇怪（beamer 的输出也是 pdf 呀），一个暗黑的做法是在输出格式的地方如下传递 Pandoc 的参数

```
pandoc_args: !expr c("--lua-filter", list.files(rmarkdown:::pandoc_lua_filters(), full.names = T)[1])
```

但是，是不是可以也自动支持一下？

## 动机

beamer 主题通常自定了很多 block，有了 Pandoc 的 lua 脚本外挂，不需要额外增加上面那个魔法

## 可重复的例子

````md
---
title: "R Markdown 制作 beamer 幻灯片"
author: "xx"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
documentclass: ctexbeamer
output: 
  bookdown::pdf_book: 
    number_sections: yes
    toc: no
    base_format: rmarkdown::beamer_presentation
    latex_engine: xelatex
    citation_package: natbib
    keep_tex: no # yes for debug
    template: null
    theme: Verona 
    pandoc_args: !expr c("--lua-filter", list.files(rmarkdown:::pandoc_lua_filters(), full.names = T)[1])
themeoptions: 
  - colorblocks
biblio-style: plainnat
link-citations: yes
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

## 设置主题 {#sec:setup-verona}
 
Ivan Valbusa 开发了 [Verona 主题的 Beamer 模版](https://bitbucket.org/rivanvx/beamer)，
目前 CTAN 上的版本是 0.2，文档说明见 <https://www.ctan.org/pkg/beamer-verona>
这个主题的宏包依赖很少！我很喜欢！

```r
tinytex::tlmgr_install('beamer-verona')
```


## 自定义的块 {#sec:custom-blocks}

::: {.exampleblock data-latex="{提示}"}
提示
:::

::: {.alertblock data-latex="{警告}"}
警告

::: {.block data-latex="{注意}"}
请读者注意
:::

description:

    - If I have posted the same issue elsewhere, I have also mentioned it in this issue.
- [x] I have learned the Github Markdown syntax, and formatted my issue correctly.

I understand that my issue may be closed if I don't fulfill my promises.

## Summary

When running `rmarkdown::render` with the `run_pandoc = FALSE` option, the markdown file that is generated, and the name of which is returned, is deleted in the clean up process. To keep the file, the option `clean = FALSE` must also be supplied which keeps more than the final markdown file.

## Reproducible example

```r
ex <- system.file("rmarkdown", "templates", "html_vignette", "skeleton", "skeleton.Rmd", package = "rmarkdown")

privatedir <- tempfile("PandocExample")
dir.create(privatedir)
setwd(privatedir)
file.copy(ex, ".")
list.files()

rmarkdown::render("skeleton.Rmd", run_pandoc = FALSE)
list.files()
rmarkdown::render("skeleton.Rmd", run_pandoc = FALSE, clean = FALSE)
list.files()
rmarkdown::render("skeleton.Rmd", run_pandoc = TRUE)
list.files()
```

## Description of example and expected and actual output

As this bug report involves the creation of files in the RMarkdown render process, first create a controlled environment. Use the `skeleton.Rmd` which comes with `rmarkdown` as the example file to render. Use `tempfile` to get a unique, writable, unused directory that will work for everyone. Create that directory, set the working directory to it, and copy the `skeleton.Rmd` file to it. At this point, `list.files()` should only return `"skeleton.Rmd"`.

The first invocation of `rmarkdown::render` has the `run_pandoc = FALSE` argument. The output of that (with irrelevant knitting details removed) is

```r
> rmarkdown::render("skeleton.Rmd", run_pandoc = FALSE)


processing file: skeleton.Rmd
[…]
output file: skeleton.knit.md

[1] "skeleton.knit.md"
attr(,"knit_meta")
list()
attr(,"intermediates")
[1] "skeleton.knit.md" "skeleton.utf8.md" "skeleton_files"  
> list.files()
[1] "skeleton.Rmd"
```
`rmarkdown::render` correctly returns `"skeleton.knit.md"` as the name of the knitted, but not pandoced, file. However, the file itself is not in the directory as seen by the output of `list.files()`. **The expected behavior is that `"skeleton.knit.md"` would be present in the directory.**

Invoking `rmarkdown::render` with both `run_pandoc = FALSE` and `clean = FALSE` gives identical printed output for the `rmarkdown::render` function, but `list.files()` now gives

```r
> list.files()
[1] "skeleton.knit.md" "skeleton.Rmd"     "skeleton.utf8.md" "skeleton_files"
```

This behaves as expected and appears to be the only way to get the `"skeleton.knit.md"` file to remain present after `rmarkdown::render()` is run.

The final invocation just demonstrates that when pandoc is run, the expected final output file (`"skeleton.html"`) is preserved.

## Discussion

When `rmarkdown::render()` is invoked with the `run_pandoc = FALSE` option, the markdown file created is not an intermediate file, but rather the expected, final output file. `clean = FALSE` should not be required to keep that file around as it keeps other files as well.

title: Provide required style in odt documents template for pagebreak feature
description:
Could the following be a possible improvement which complements the [pagebreak solution](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1610) developed by @cderv for pdf, word and html documents?

This is said in  `vignette("lua-filters", package = "rmarkdown")` (mentioned in [rmarkdown release 1.16](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/NEWS.md#rmarkdown-116)):

> To use the pagebreak feature with odt_document(), you need to provide a reference document that includes a paragraph style with, by default, the name Pagebreak. This named paragraph style should have no extra space before or after and have a pagebreak after it.

I wonder if Rmarkdown could **always** add a _Pagebreak_ paragraph style predefined by default to every odt_document (the same way it already includes a style named _Heading_20_1_ by default when we add a #Header1 markdown code, and so on for other headers). . 

I think paragraph styles are defined somewhere at the beginning of content.xml, within the `<office:automatic-styles>...</office:automatic-styles>` section. 
So perhaps adding something like this to that section, might do the trick:

`<style:style style:name="Pagebreak" style:family="paragraph" style:parent-style-name="Standard">**<style:paragraph-properties fo:break-before="page"/>**</style:style>`
(this is the style created when I open the Rmarkdown-produced ODT, after inserting a pagebreak and closing the document)

So, the **_Pagebreak_** style would always be available, no need to provide a reference document that includes that style (unless the user is interested in doing so to provide some other predefined styles, of course).

This is just an idea, although I'm not expert in pandoc or ODT (I just opened one odt to see where Pagebreak style properties were defined).
I wish I could develop this on my own, but I don't have the skills required to do it.

title: The latest pandoc might not be the best pandoc
description:
In [pandoc.R](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/pandoc.R) (lines 548-580), rmarkdown searches the machine for pandoc and selects the most recent version among the various installed locations. On its face, this seems a reasonable approach, but it has been causing me troubles. 

I want to have the current version of pandoc (2.9.2.1) installed on my machine. However, this version of pandoc causes errors with the current release version of rmarkdown, as noted in the [RStudio Community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/updated-pandoc-now-getting-an-error-when-i-knit-dyld-lazy-symbol-binding-failed/47692). 

However, I need this version of pandoc for some other uses which are not supported by pandoc 2.3.1 currently shipping with the release build of RStudio, so I need to have both versions living simultaneously on my machine. But since rmarkdown looks for the latest version, my only option is to remove the latest version from my PATH to hide it from rmarkdown, and call the executable directly. Not exactly a great solution. 

Could rmarkdown just be set to use the version of pandoc provided with RStudio unless there isn't one? Or at least have an option to behave as such? The latter might require filing an issue over in the IDE repo as well, which I'm happy to do if needed. 

(also if the issue with pandoc version 2.9.2.1 is news to you, I can file a bug report as well, if needed).

title: Fix #1550 ignores LaTeX documentclass passed as a pandoc variable or in a pandoc defaults file
description:
The changes made in #1550 work when `documentclass` is set at the top level of the document metadata. However, when `documentclass` is set in `pandoc_args` with either the pandoc `--variable` or `--metadata` options it is not recognised and `--variable 'geometry:margin=1in' ` is appended to the pandoc command line.

[Edit] The `documentclass` is also ignored when it is set in a pandoc defaults file and `pandoc_args` has the pandoc `--defaults` option set to the pandoc defaults file.

## Scenario

A main R Markdown document incorporates numerous child documents which are all located in a sub-directory. In order to not have to compile the complete document when working on a child document an `_output.yaml` file with the required output metadata is located in the subdirectory. This ensures that the metadata is applied to all the child documents, the metadata is consistent between child documents, and ongoing maintenance is reduced, limiting the possibility of error.

title: make latex-div lua filter apply only on latex output and no need for `data-latex=""`
description:
Design about this lua filters by @RLesur has been discussed in https://github.com/yihui/bookdown-crc/issues/1 and added in rmarkdown in https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/commit/cecd812743826989b539a7b0fcb1b8c08f09c05d

Currently, the lua filter is only activated and useful for `latex` output if `data-latex=` has been added. If not useful, it must be set to `""`

I think this is not obvious from what you expect from pandoc and it does not serve well "multi-format" output, because you need to add `data-latex=""` if you want it to work in pdf and in html. Currently, it seems that example in ongoing bookdown-cookbook is not working : https://github.com/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/issues/188

How about improving the filter  my thought: 
* we could make the `Div` function only apply for latex output format in the lua filter. No `return nil` required, and no risk to conflict with `fenced_divs` for other format ?
* That way if no `data-latex=` is provided, we could generate a `verbatim` environment, and otherwise `data-latex` should be provided to set options. 

I don't think this will break anything, just change the way the lua filter is activated, to make this type of example works
https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/multi-column-layout.html

I have something like this in mind
```lua
Div = function (div)
  local options = div.attributes['data-latex']

  -- if the output format is not latex, the object is left unchanged
  if FORMAT ~= 'latex' and FORMAT ~= 'beamer' then
    -- if options has been set for latex, unset for other output
    if options then
      div.attributes['data-latex'] = nil
    end
    return div
  end

  local env = div.classes[1]
  -- if the div has no class, the object is left unchanged
  if not env then return nil end

  -- insert raw latex before content
  table.insert(
    div.content, 1,
    pandoc.RawBlock('tex', '\\begin' .. '{' .. env .. '}' .. (options or ""))
  )
  -- insert raw latex after content
  table.insert(
    div.content,
    pandoc.RawBlock('tex', '\\end{' .. env .. '}')
  )
  return div
end
```

title: Suggestion: drop the smart parameter from output formats
description:
The output formats have the `smart` parameter (e.g., `html_document`).
This parameter is passed to `smart_extension` and adds `+smart` when `TRUE` and adds nothing when `FALSE`.

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/43def55d9001ced4526988cfd6feacb11fa6a7dc/R/output_format.R#L349-L351

However, the `smart` extension is enabled by default in the Pandoc's markdown.

https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/9feefa39319358acc84811e6017aeea60f9140c3/MANUAL.txt#L2627-L2628

This means, the `smart` extension is enabled regardless of the `smart` parameter (i.e., `html_document(smart = TRUE)` and `html_document(smart = FALSE)` cause the same result).

Thus, I suggest to drop smart parameter from the output formats.
By doing this, the user-specified `smart` parameter will be silently ignored as ellipsis.
If users really have to toggle the `smart` extension, they can do so via the `md_extension` parameter (i.e., `md_extension = "-smart"` disables the smart extension).
Currently, users have to specify both `smart=FALSE` and `md_extension="-smart"` to disable the `smart` extension.

title: issue with printing table containing custom vctrs classes
description:
I defined a new `vctrs` class and want to use it in a tibble. The normal printing works but when printing the tibble in a markdown document I get an error because `vec_cast.myvec.character()` gets called with `"__NA__"`.

````{r}
---
title: "test"
author: "Maximilian Girlich"
date: "2/3/2020"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


```{r}
library(vctrs)
library(rlang)
library(tibble)


# json --------------------------------------------------------------------

new_myvec <- function(x = character()) {
  vec_assert(x, character())
  stopifnot(all(x != "__NA__"))
  new_vctr(x, class = c("myvec"), inherit_base_type = TRUE)
}


# coerce ------------------------------------------------------------------

vec_ptype2.myvec <- function(x, y, ..., x_arg = "", y_arg = "") {
  UseMethod("vec_ptype2.myvec", y)
}

vec_ptype2.myvec.character <- function(x, y, ...) {
  character()
}

vec_ptype2.character.myvec <- function(x, y, ...) {
  character()
}


# cast --------------------------------------------------------------------

vec_cast.myvec <- function(x, to, ...) {
  UseMethod("vec_cast.myvec")
}

vec_cast.myvec.character <- function(x, to, ...) {
  new_myvec(vec_data(x))
}

vec_cast.character.myvec <- function(x, to, ...) {
  vec_data(x)
}


x <- new_myvec("a")
tibble(body = x)
```

````

and then render it with

```{r}
rmarkdown::render("test.Rmd", output_format="html_notebook")
```

title: Grab title for vignettes from "vignette" header
description:
One of my vignettes has this in the header:

```
---
title: "Column data types"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Column data types}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---
```

Ideally, I'd like to write

```
---
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Column data types}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---
```

and have the `title` inferred from the contents of `\VignetteIndexEntry` in the `vignette:`. This would remove redundancy and reduce error potential that arises from mismatching titles and index entries. The `title` still could be overridden.

Would you support this behavior?

title: fig.cap doesn't work for plotly for html notebook (but work for pure html)
description:
Here is an example `Rmd`:

````
---
title: "R Notebook"
output:
  html_notebook:
    fig_caption: yes
  html_document:
    df_print: paged
---

```{r, fig.cap="About cars"}
plot(cars)
```

```{r cars, fig.cap="About cars"}
library(plotly)
plot_ly(data=cars, x=~speed,y=~dist, type="scatter", mode="markers")
```
````

I notice that there is a fix for `knitr` at https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/1223 when `fig.cap` also doesn't work for plotly. But The fix seems not applicable to `html_notebook`?

title: Passing all *.bib files of given path to bibliography field in Rmd YAML
description:
I wish we had a way to list all `*.bib` files of any given path in `bibliography` field of `rmarkdown` YAML without having to pass every single bib file names manually.

[This StackOverflow Question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54277774/using-list-files-for-bibliography-field-in-rmd-yaml/54278990#54278990) and [This GitHub issue](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/5955#issuecomment-560446701) are related to this need.

Any ideas or plans to address this request?

title: html notebook rendering error when ploting data with unicode chinese char in ggplotly
description:
A minimally reprodicuble `Rmd` file:

````
---
title: "test"
output: html_notebook
---

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

df <- data.frame(x=1, y=1, t="我我我我")
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y, fill=t)) +
  geom_point()
ggplotly(p)
```
````

Then run:
```r
rmarkdown::render("test.Rmd", output_format="html_notebook")
```

Results in the following error:

```


processing file: test.Rmd
  |..............                                                        |  20%
  ordinary text without R code

  |............................                                          |  40%
label: unnamed-chunk-1
  |..........................................                            |  60%
  ordinary text without R code

  |........................................................              |  80%
label: unnamed-chunk-2
  |......................................................................| 100%
  ordinary text without R code


output file: test.knit.md

Error in extract(input_str) : Invalid nesting of html_preserve directives
Calls: <Anonymous> ... <Anonymous> -> base -> base -> extract_preserve_chunks -> extract
Execution halted
```

Interestingly, in RStudio for preview everything is fine.
And I've found out that **the length matters.**
So `"我我我我"` will cause the error but NOT `"我我我"`.

Here is my system info:

```
R version 3.6.0 (2019-04-26)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 (64-bit)
Running under: macOS High Sierra 10.13.4
rmarkdown 2.0
pandoc 2.7.3
```

I encounter the same error in my Ubuntu 16.04 machine.
I really have no idea what's going on here and it took me quite some time to finally pin down the root cause being UTF-8 Chinese characters. Still no clue why this happens. :(

title: Include option for placing footer outside the main container
description:
Currently, the footer in an html document is placed inside the content (`main-container`). In other words, when we specify ``` output: html_document: include: after_body: footer.html ``` we get html that looks like: ```
/* Main content of page */ --footer appears here--
``` Sure, there would be situations in which this would be what the author is looking for, but in many (most?) web pages, the footer appears outside the main content: ```
/* Main content of page */

title: render() and render_site() behaves differently in the presence of _site.yml.
description:
Say, I have files *index.Rmd*, *slide1.Rmd* and *_site.yml*

_index.Rmd_

```
---
title: Home
---

This is the home
```

_slide1.Rmd_

```
---
title: "Xaringan slide"
output:
  xaringan::moon_reader
---

Hello
```

__site.yml_

```
name: RMD test
navbar:
  title: RMD test
  right:
    - text: Home
      href: index.html
    - text: Slide
      href: slide1.html
output:
  rmarkdown::html_document
```

If I run `rmarkdown::render('slide1.Rmd')` (in the presence of *_site.yml*), the output is the document defined in *_site.yml*. The YAML definition in the Rmd file is ignored.

If I run `rmarkdown::render_site()`, the output of *slide1.Rmd* is a xaringan presentation (ie; document defined inside slide1.Rmd). As expected.

But in addition, I get this warning:

```
Output created: _site/index.html
Warning message:
In file.rename(output, output_dest) :
  cannot rename file '/home/user/Desktop/test-rmd/slide1.html' to './_site/slide1.html', reason 'No such file or directory'
```

Is there some way to make `render()` use only the YAML definition inside the file and not that from `_site.yml`? Is the warning something to worry about?

Issue on [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56064050/render-xaringan-rmd-when-using-site-yml-file).

title: tempfile() default argument requires R >=3.5.0
description:
The new [tempfile function](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/commit/922d2de3a331f99b4ab4529bf60c2cd60a0ac904) uses `tempdir(TRUE)` as a default argument. I believe this argument to `tempdir()` was added in R 3.5, which brings the minimum R version rmarkdown is compatible with to 3.5 from 3.0, as `tempfile()` is called with this default argument in several places in the package. title: raw_attribute in header-includes
description:
With rmarkdown version 1.18 the one can no longer use the `raw_attribute` extension when specifying a `header-includes`:

    ---
    output: 
      pdf_document:
        keep_tex: yes
    header-includes:
    - |
      ```{=latex}
      \newcommand{\foobar}[1]{Foo#1Bar}
      ```    
    ---
    
    ```{=latex}
    \foobar{Baz}
    ```
The ccontent of `header-includes` is copied verbatim to the TeX file which leads to a 

> ! LaTeX Error: Missing \begin{document}.

It works when one uses the more conventional

```
header-includes:
- \newcommand{\foobar}[1]{Foo#1Bar}
```
However, the pandoc manual actually advertises the use of raw-headers in the meta data block. 

Note: This is motivated by trying to answer https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59245638/latex-error-environment-threeparttable-undefined. It seems the `papaja` package uses raw-headers.

title: Producing native Abstract Syntax Tree from and within an Rmd YAML
description:
Currently, it does not seem like we have a convenient workaround to produce native `Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)` within an Rmd document.

For a markdown file, we use the following command in terminal:

```markup
pandoc -f markdown -s -t native -o output.native file.md [--lua-filter=lua_file.lua] ...
```

Of course, we could use the same command for any Rmd files; however, it would be so much convenient if we could had a relevant YAML option like `keep_tex` and `keep_md`.

What if we add a `keep_native` boolean option within an Rmd file YAML that can generate `[file_name].native` when set to true?

title: Tabsets don't work in pandoc 2.8
description:
Another compatibility issue with pandoc 2.8+ (cf. https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/issues/832) happens when using `.tabset`s. The difference is due to the following change: when running ``` pandoc -t html4 --section-divs <<< "# test {.tabset}" ``` gives in pandoc 2.7.3: ```

test

``` and in pandoc 2.8: ```

test

``` so the selector https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/07a0ca4c3b8a11cbaf3c8050fe2064b91de2f0b8/inst/rmd/h/navigation-1.1/tabsets.js#L136 fails. A solution is to change the above to ```js var tabsets = $("div.section.tabset"); if (tabsets.length == 0) tabsets = $("div.section").has(">.tabset"); ``` also https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/07a0ca4c3b8a11cbaf3c8050fe2064b91de2f0b8/inst/rmd/h/navigation-1.1/tabsets.js#L61 needs to be changed to ``` var match = tabset.attr('class').match(/level(\d)+/); ``` but it is a bit more tricky with sticky tabsets, hopefully someone can take it up from here... ---
minimal example: ``` --- title: test tabsets output: html_document --- # Tabs {.tabset} ## Number 1 Text 1 ## Numer 2 Text 2 ```

description:
## Observation

With 'rmarkdown' 1.18 (and also the newer version available via GitHub), running the following code (CV template using the package 'vitae') 

````rmd
---
name: Marie
surname: Curie
position: "Professor"
address: "School of Physics & Chemistry, École Normale Supérieure"
email: "Marie.Curie@ens.fr"
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%B %Y')`"

header-includes:

  - \newunicodechar{‑}{-} %this fixes wrong dash input inputs
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(vitae)
library(kableExtra)
``` 

# Test

* Test
````

drops the following error message:

```
Error in file(file, ifelse(append, "a", "w")) : 
  invalid 'description' argument

I've tried a couple of variants to understand the cause of this issue better, but I have to admit I do not fully understand what is going on. I think that it has something to do with changes introduced for `header-includes` in 'rmarkdown' 1.18 (since it works without any problem for version 1.17). title: Deletion of latex templates in v1.18 causes \mainmatter issue/bug for bookdown::pdf_book()
description:
<!--
Please keep the below portion in your issue. Your issue will be closed if any of the boxes is not checked (i.e., replace `[ ]` by `[x]`). In certain (rare) cases, you may be exempted if you give a brief explanation (e.g., you are only making a suggestion for improvement). Thanks!
-->

I think that in v1.18 the deletion of `default.tex` and the other latex templates by #1563 causes a small problem for bookdown relating to `\mainmatter`. 

I have created a simple repo which demonstrates the problem for the `bookdown::pdf_book()` output pdf.
https://github.com/remlapmot/example-rmarkdown-mainmatter-issue

- [Intended pdf (under v1.17)](https://github.com/remlapmot/example-rmarkdown-mainmatter-issue/blob/b6b741d16e4bad7d056644ae8074cae7f53c3b56/_book/_main-v1.17.pdf)
- [pdf with extra `\mainmatter` (under v1.18)](https://github.com/remlapmot/example-rmarkdown-mainmatter-issue/blob/b6b741d16e4bad7d056644ae8074cae7f53c3b56/_book/_main-v1.18.pdf) 

When compiled under rmarkdown v1.17 the Contents and Preface are in the `\frontmatter` as intended.

However, when compiled under rmarkdown v1.18 the different (I am assuming pandoc) template puts an extra `\mainmatter` immediately before the R Markdown input from `index.Rmd`. See [line 144](https://github.com/remlapmot/example-rmarkdown-mainmatter-issue/blob/b6b741d16e4bad7d056644ae8074cae7f53c3b56/_book/_main-v1.18.tex#L144
) of the combined tex file.

If you don't want to put the latex templates back in rmarkdown this could be solved by providing a latex template to bookdown.

Thanks for any help (I hope I have identified the correct source of the additional `\mainmatter`).

title: 1.19 update and fix #1716 breaks the compact title when only title and date fields are present
description:
It seems the most recent update to 1.19 removed the custom latex template and uses pandoc's default template. [Fix #1716](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/commit/cf8e5df1b309edc9d75e610f9c52c451588c302b) was proposed to keep a compact title by including `compact-title.tex` in the `includes` argument of `pdf_document()` (essentially `render("test.Rmd", output_format = pdf_document(includes = includes(in_header = "compact-title.tex")))`). However, if I have title and date fields but no author field, the rendered PDF document contains a blank line between the title and date. I'm not sure if this is a pandoc, latex, or rmarkdown change, as I receive a "no \author given" warning. Rmarkdown before used to render simply the title and date with no whitespace in between and wouldn't throw any issue with a missing \author.

test.Rmd
```
---
title: "test"
output: pdf_document
date: "12/3/2019"
---
This is a test document
```

title: default template does not work with multiple authors
description:
(This is perhaps a regression to #353, same problem and reprex).

A minimal reproducible example, `index.Rmd`:

```
---
title: "R Markdown v2 Demo"
author:
  - John
  - Joe
date: "2015/01/01"
output:
  pdf_document:
    keep_tex: yes

---

Hello world.
```

Running `rmarkdown::render('index.Rmd')` on this fails with:

```
! Misplaced \crcr.

l.84 \maketitle

Error: Failed to compile index.tex. See https://yihui.name/tinytex/r/#debugging for debugging tips. See index.log for more info.
Execution halted

Running `pandoc --standalone --from=markdown --output=index.pdf index.Rmd` produces the expected pdf.

description:
Would there be any way for us to support `ConTeXT` in `rmarkdown`?

I have found that `--pdf-engine` flag does not work with current `rmarkdown`.

---
output:

---

title: Interactive parameterization file max size
description:
The GUI for interactive parameter input in Rmarkdown (Knit with Parameters) does not accept files bigger than 5 Mb. This has been addressed [before](https://community.rstudio.com/t/rstudio-connect-rmarkdown-maximum-upload-size-exceeded/9937/5) on the RStudio community, but not resolved.

title: rmarkdown::run fails if file is NULL and dir is set
description:
Dear all,

I am trying to run `rmarkdown::run(file = NULL, dir = "/srv/shiny-server")` to start a shiny server to render an interactive document (lets say at `/srv/shiny-server/index.rmd`). 

The call fails with 
```
> rmarkdown::run(file = NULL, dir = '/srv/shiny-server')
Error in readLines(con, warn = FALSE) : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In readLines(con, warn = FALSE) :
  cannot open file 'index.rmd': No such file or directory
```

I was able to track this down to [line 128](https://github.com/jenzopr/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/shiny.R#L128) of `R/shiny.R`, where `file` is `NULL` and `default_file` gets a value of `"index.rmd"`, but unfortunately without the correct directory prefix from `dir`. The following [line 129](https://github.com/jenzopr/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/shiny.R#L129) then tries to get the documents runtime from the `"index.rmd"`s YAML header, whereas the *true* file resides in `/srv/shiny-server/index.rmd` (aka `file.path(dir, default_file)`).

The content of `/srv/shiny-server/index.rmd` is:

```
---
title: testfile
runtime: shiny
---

## Testfile
``` 

My proposed fix would be either to change [line 128](https://github.com/jenzopr/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/shiny.R#L128) to

```
target_file <- file %||% file.path(dir, default_file)
```

of prefix `default_file` directly with `dir` in case `default_file` was `NULL` (i.e in lines 76, 81, 88 and 99) of `R/shiny.R`.

I can file a PR if you're okay with either option. Please let me know what you think.

Best,
Jens

title: setmathfont not working with luatex when unicode-math is loaded
description:
If the following minimal, reproducible example is knitted:

```
---
title: "Untitled"
author: "Author"
header-includes:
   - \usepackage{unicode-math}
output:
  pdf_document:
    latex_engine: lualatex
mathfont: XITS Math
---

A
```

it will give an error:

```
! Undefined control sequence.
l.18     \setmathfont
                   (Digits,Latin,Greek)[]{XITS Math}

Error: Failed to compile tempmarkdown.tex. See https://yihui.name/tinytex/r/#debugging for debugging tips. See tempmarkdown.log for more info.
Execution halted
```

I believe that the root of the problem is that both `unicode-math` and `mathspec` define `setmathfont`, but unfortunately differently: [the latter](http://mirrors.ctan.org/macros/xetex/latex/mathspec/mathspec.pdf) allows the `(Digits,Latin,Greek)` "set specification", but there is no such for [the former](http://mirrors.ctan.org/macros/latex/contrib/unicode-math/unicode-math.pdf).

(The reason why it only causes problem with `luatex` is that `xetex` loads `mathspec`.)

title: find_external_resources does not locate Office templates
description:
## Repro

Save this doc as example.Rmd:

```
---
title: "Templates"
output:
  powerpoint_presentation:
    reference_doc: template.potx
---

### Overview
```

(if you don't have a `potx` file, just make an empty one)

Next, run `find_external_resources`:

```
> rmarkdown::find_external_resources("~/scratch/example.Rmd")
[1] path     explicit web     
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
```

The external resource is not discovered.

This is where this usually happens:

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/7ad693e10a7444de60e4f58bc3eef14eab212d35/R/html_resources.R#L285-L299

title: Issue with embedded SageMath cell
description:

I tried embedding a SageMath Cell inside an ioslides presentation following these instructions:
https://sagecell.sagemath.org/static/about.html?v=66c8a2df011da3aea3dfa789fc6117f4

I copied the html code from steps 1,2,3 into my Rmd and the SageMath cell was embedded but there was a problem with the position of the cursor inside the SageMath Cell. Looking into the ioslides theme CSS default.css, it appears that line 527: `left: -60px;`  may be the one that creates this problem with the SageMath Cell. I posted this issue on SageMath Cell community and after looking into the issue they advised me to raise the issue with the ioslides developers. 

It would be nice to have a properly working SageMath Cell inside ioslides. 

Thanks!

title: rmarkdown not compiling because of grffile TeX package
Rmarkdown fails to render in pdf_document with last latex version
description:
I think this error is the cause of https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/issues/152

There were some bugs recently with `graphicx` and `grffile` in last latex version. This has been reported in pandoc and upstream. See https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/5848#issuecomment-547246756. 

Changes has been made in pandoc templates now by removing package `grffile`. 
https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/commit/4d5fd9e2fe360e47fd5beab724c612ce29aa39ee

I wonder if we need to do the same with rmarkdown included template. 🤔 
There was also other modification in pandoc template since `pandoc 1.17` - it could be an opportunity to update it. What do you think ?

title: ioslides: images with width not inlined
description: The following R Markdown document does not inline the `logo.svg` image when rendering. ```markdown --- title: image without inlining output: ioslides_presentation: {} --- ![](logo.svg){width=20%} ``` This is because of how the `width` argument is rendered. Here is a Markdown document using two HTML image tags. The first (where `width` is before `src`) does not get the image inlined. The second (with `src` after the tag opens) has its image inlined. ```markdown --- title: image without inlining output: ioslides_presentation: {} --- ``` The shape of the HTML is what prevents inlining; both Markdown and HTML input cause the same problem. Content rendered to the ioslides output uses image inlining from in the `rmarkdown` package and appears to not rely on `pandoc` for inlining. https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/d9e4b4583b9b3d2fb5efc09c7409c1945b6220af/R/base64.R#L25-L30 The `base64.R` regular expression is pretty narrow; it expects `src` immediately after the `img` tag. I built this small patch to verify the cause -- it adds inlining when `width` is between `img` and `src`. It's probably not flexible enough. ```r process_images <- function(html, processor) { html <- process_html_res( html, "<\\s*[Ii][Mm][Gg]\\s+[Ss][Rr][Cc]\\s*=\\s*[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']", processor) process_html_res( html, "<\\s*[Ii][Mm][Gg]\\s+width=\".+?\"\\s+[Ss][Rr][Cc]\\s*=\\s*[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']", processor) } ```

title: Setting image width prevents inlining in ioslides
description: Take this simple Rmd doc and sample image: ``` --- output: ioslides_presentation --- ![](sample.png) ![](sample.png){width=80%} ``` If you knit this document, the first image is embedded (correct), and the second is not (incorrect).

title: Fails to render with python plots when knit_root_dir is set
description:
When running Rmarkdown on an `Rmd` file with a python chunk that produces a plot and the `knit_root_dir` option is set, pandoc fails to convert the intermediate markdown file: 

**notebook.Rmd**
````Rmd
```{r plot-r}
plot(1:10)
```

```{python plot-py}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.plot(range(10))
```

````

**directory structure**
```
.
├── nb_dir
│   └── notebook.Rmd
└── work_dir
```

**run rmarkdown** 
```bash
> Rscript -e "rmarkdown::render('nb_dir/notebook.Rmd',
 knit_root_dir='/abs/path/to/work_dir')"
[...]
File notebook_files/figure-html/plot-py-1.png not found in resource path
Error: pandoc document conversion failed with error 99
Execution halted
```

--- 
The reason for this seems to be that intermediate python plots are written to the `knit_root_dir`, while R plots are written to the file where the input file is located. 

```bash
> Rscript -e "rmarkdown::render('nb_dir/notebook.Rmd',
 run_pandoc=FALSE, clean=FALSE,
 knit_root_dir='/abs/path/to/work_dir')"
```
```
.
├── nb_dir
│   ├── notebook_files
│   │   └── figure-html
│   │       └── plot-r-1.png
│   ├── notebook.knit.md
│   ├── notebook.Rmd
│   └── notebook.utf8.md
└── work_dir
    └── notebook_files
        └── figure-html
            └── plot-py-1.png
```

---
### Edit: Behaviour of `intermediates_dir`
Setting intermediates_dir only moves the `*.md` files, but not the `_files` directory: 
```
> Rscript -e "rmarkdown::render('nb_dir/notebook.Rmd',
 run_pandoc=FALSE, clean=FALSE,
 knit_root_dir='/abs/path/to/work_dir',
 intermediates_dir='/abs/path/to/work_dir')"
```

```
.
├── nb_dir
│   ├── notebook_files
│   │   └── figure-html
│   │       └── plot-r-1.png
│   └── notebook.Rmd
└── work_dir
    ├── notebook_files
    │   └── figure-html
    │       └── plot-py-1.png
    ├── notebook.knit.md
    └── notebook.utf8.md
```
