title: Suggesting to correct the documentation
description:
It is mentioned in [Options - Chunk options and package options](https://yihui.name/knitr/options/) that the default `error` setting is `TRUE`:

> error: (TRUE; logical) whether to preserve errors (from stop()); by default, the evaluation will not stop even in case of errors!!

However, this is no longer the case (as confirmed [here](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/149#issuecomment-48138689)) and people do get confused regarding it. For example, check this [thread](https://community.rstudio.com/t/put-errors-in-code-chunks-for-students-to-find-and-fix-but-will-not-knit/43905).

May I request you to fix this?

title: some bootswatch 3 themes fail for rmarkdown websites
description:
I've just set up an rmarkdown website from the boilerplate that ships with RStudio 1.2.5013, just adding a different bootswatch theme:

`_site.yml`:

```
name: "my-website"
navbar:
  title: "My Website"
  left:
    - text: "Home"
      href: index.html
    - text: "About"
      href: about.html
output:
  html_document:
    theme: slate
```

When running `rmarkdown::render_site()`, this fails with:

```
Error in navbarHeights[[theme]] : subscript out of bounds
Calls: <Anonymous> ... <Anonymous> -> overlay -> pandoc_body_padding_variable_args
Execution halted

Exited with status 1.
```

The problem seems to exist for themes:

- `slate`

title: Color headers of floating TOC using external custom css file
description: I am using a .rmd file to generate a .html file. I would like to color certain header levels inside my floating TOC using external custom .css file. title: include footer.html causes this error pandoc: end.html: openBinaryFile: does not exist
description:
I am trying to add a footer to a rmakrdown website by adding `include:after_body: foobar.html`  in the _site.yml file. When I knit with the "build website" button, I get the "pandoc: end.html" file doesn't exist error.   

Initially I thought it had to do with pandoc, but after fiddling a bit,  it turns out to NOT be a pandoc issue, that is what I think anyway.  Here is how I am able to reproduce it.

```
> packageVersion("rmarkdown")
[1] ‘1.16.2’

```
The setup and steps I have taken to replicate the problem and work around:
1/ flat directory
2/ files in the directory: index.Rmd, About.Rmd, footer.Rmd
3/ my _site.yaml looks like this
```
output:
  html_document:
     theme: cerulean
     highlight: textmate
     include:
       after_body: footer.hml
     css: styles.css/ 

```
4/ When I press the knit button - index.html, About.html and footer.html get copied to "_site" directory. And the first go around works fine. 
5/ Next, I edited the footer.Rmd and when press the knit button I get "pandoc openBinaryFile doesn't exist error".
5/ To work around that. a) I remove the include after_body from the yml, and save. b) Delete the footer.hml from **_site** directory, c) knit the footer.Rmd file on its own (which copies the foother.html to _site directory. d) I then manually move the footer.html back to the home directory (where the footer.Rmd is), and e) re-add the include after_body again back to _site.yml, and knit. This website rendered without pondoc issue after that. 

I didn't experience the same issue for the index and about Rmd files. I can make changes and any time and they copy the respective .html to _site with changes made, and when knit they render with no manual add/delete or messing with the _site.yml.  

The footer.Rmd and _site are misbehaving somehow. It seems to me , somewhere in the script that looks at the yaml and the _site directory to render with pandoc is not quite right.

title: find_external_resources() errors when multiple files in includes
description:
I want to include multiple files in the `includes` section of an R markdown document.  This works fine when knitting, but throws an error when trying to deploy the document, e.g. to RStudio Connect.

The root cause is that `find_external_resources()` seems to throw the error:

```
File <file> not found in resource path
Error: pandoc document conversion failed with error 99
```

Here is a minimal reprex:

Create a file `minimal_includes.Rmd`:

````r
---
title: "multiple_includes"
output: 
  html_document:
    includes:
      after_body: 
      - dep1.html
      - dep2.html

---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## R Markdown

This document doesn't do anything, other than import two dependencies.
```
````

Then, create `dep1.html`:

```html
<!-- nothing interesting in dep1 -->
```

and `dep2.html`

```html
<!-- nothing interesting in dep2 -->
```

You will now be able to knit the document successfully.  However, the following will throw the error:

```r
rmarkdown::find_external_resources("multiple_includes.Rmd")
```

As I mentioned, this prevents me from deploying some documents to RStudio Connect.

title: Should render() favour reproducibility by default?
description:
In RStudio, pressing the 'knit' button appears to render an Rmd in separate R process - such that the code execution environment is not contaminated by the global environment or search path of the user's interactive session.

When calling `render()` from the console, the opposite is true. The user's environment is used by default (`parent.frame()`) and the library search path remains the same as the interactive session. So functions from previously attached packages can be called.

This means rendering an Rmd from the console is much more vulnerable to reproducibility issues than using the button in RStudio. I think it would be worth considering making `render()` use a separate process using `callr` by default, as is done in RStudio. The expectations set up by the GUI are setting people up for a surprise otherwise. This was certainly the case for me.

title: Behavior of render() in cleaning intermediates
description:
This issue is related to a [bug report](https://github.com/yixuan/prettydoc/issues/15) of `prettydoc` in cleaning temporary files. The situation is that if the document does not contain any figures, then the temporary files generated by `prettydoc` would not be properly deleted.

After some examinations I have located the cause of this issue: in the `render()` function, [the following lines](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/render.R#L798-L802) are used to add the temporary files to the intermediates.

```r
if (output_format$clean_supporting && !dir_exists(cache_dir)) {
  # unlink does not support / at the end of file path
  fig_path <- gsub("/$", "", knitr::opts_chunk$get('fig.path'))
  intermediates <- c(
    intermediates,
    if (identical(list.files(files_dir, '^figure-.+'), basename(fig_path))) {
      files_dir
    } else {
      fig_path
    }
  )
}
```

In my understanding, the condition `identical(list.files(files_dir, '^figure-.+'), basename(fig_path))` means the following: if there are multiple output formats involved, then only delete the figures generated by the current format (related to #1503).

However, this ignores one possibility: if no figure is in the document, then `list.files(files_dir, '^figure-.+')` is `character(0)`, so this condition will not be triggered. This does not cause problems for built-in output formats, since no figure in the document typically means `files_dir` is empty, and there is no need to clean. But in `prettydoc`, I need to copy a few files to `files_dir` even if there is no figure generated, so I do need to clean the whole `files_dir` folder.

I'm not sure whether this is a bug or a design in `rmarkdown`. If it is a bug, then it should be easily fixed by modifying the condition to

```
if (length(list.files(files_dir, '^figure-.+')) < 1 ||
  identical(list.files(files_dir, '^figure-.+'), basename(fig_path))
) {...}
```

And if it is a design, then I wonder what is the proper way to clean temporary files generated by `prettydoc`.

Thank you!

title: R Markdown Ioslides --- non-accessible HTML output
description:
### System details RStudio Edition : Desktop RStudio Version : 1.2.5001 OS Version : Ubuntu 18.04.3 LTS R Version : 3.4.4 (2018-03-15) ### Steps to reproduce the problem Use the default Ioslides template as generated when opening a new R Markdown presentation. Use the Knit to HMTL option. I have used the WAVE (http://wave.webaim.org/) accessibility check to determine the following issues in the HTML output. ### Describe the problem in detail 1. By default, there is no ```lang``` attribute included in the opening `````` tag of the document. This is an issue for screen readers. 2. On the title slide, in the absence of a sub-title, the template generates an empty ```

``` tag of the form, ```{html}

``` Empty headings cause issues for screen readers. 3. By default, plots generated by an R script do not include an ```alt``` attribute for the image automatically. This can be seen in the slide with a plot of pressure versus temperature, which does not have an ```alt``` attribute when generated by Knitr from the default template. The ```alt``` text is important for visually impaired; while it is difficult to automatically generate a relevant ```alt``` text for an arbitrary plot, it would be a useful addition if the user can define an ```alt``` attribute in the Markdown prior to rendering in HTML. ### Describe the behavior you expected Fixing the above accessibility issues would be greatly helpful in making Ioslides a simple-to-use option for academic presentations and lectures which are to be shared with students. Currently, making these presentations accessible requires manually adjusting the above in the HTML output.

title: Option to exclude files from cleanup in the output directory of render_site
description:
I ran into [this problem](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58138343/r-markdowns-render-site-function-is-deleting-the-contents-of-the-git-folder) while trying to version control a website generated by the `render_site` function where it would delete the contents of the `.git` folder within the output directory of the function during its cleanup step. As suggested by user [user2554330 in stackexchange](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58138343/r-markdowns-render-site-function-is-deleting-the-contents-of-the-git-folder/58145499#58145499), it would be nice to have a way to exclude certain files from the cleanup.

Here are a few steps to reproduce the issue with a simple structure:
`_site.yml`:
```yaml
name: "my-website"
navbar:
  title: "My Website"
  left:
    - text: "Home"
      href: index.html
```
`index.Rmd`:
```r
---
title: "My Website"
---

Hello, Website!
```
After building the website with `render_site` and initializing git the `_site` folder has the following structure:
```
_site/
├── .git
├── site_libs
└── index.html
```
In a subsequent build the files are updated but everything in the `.git` folder is deleted, save for the `objects` folder (which is maybe kept because of permissions?). 

Looking into the `render_site` and `default_site` functions i figured this was intended as the directory is cleaned and built from the ground up but, again, it would be nice to have a way to exclude certain files or directories from the cleanup.

title: "self_contained: no" prevents "pandoc_args: --eol=lf" from working
description:
I want to have LF line endings even on Windows when knitting Rmd to HTML.
This can be done with `pandoc_args: --eol=lf` as shown below.
However, setting `self_contained: no` causes the line endings to become CRLF anyway.

Save this as e.g. `test_eol.Rmd` and knit:

```
---
output:
  html_document:
    pandoc_args: --eol=lf
    # self_contained: no  # Uncommenting this causes CRLF
---

This is

a test.
```

**Expected outcome:**
This should knit to LF line endings with or without `self_contained: no`.

This knits correctly to LF line endings, unless I uncomment the commented-out line in the yaml header, in which case it knits to CRLF line endings.

title: pandoc_citeproc_convert does not work on windows
description:
I think this issue is the cause of https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/103

``` r
rmarkdown::pandoc_citeproc_convert("biblio.bib")
#> Error in system(command, intern = TRUE): 'pandoc-citeproc' not found
```

I think this is because `pandoc_citeproc` does not handle windows binaries
https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/73d055257ecb32b92d703ede9c1b55615bcb0629/R/pandoc.R#L666-L674

`citeproc_path` will not exist on windows because of a missing `.exe` at the end. 

This issue is currently only affecting `distill` i think because this package use directly `pandoc_citeproc_convert` and `rmardown` only pass pandoc-citeproc path to pandoc itself, and it is working without the exe.

One fix is to handle windows binary by adding `.exe` to the path.

title: r in-line expression evaluated even in quoted context with double backtick
description: ### System details RStudio Edition : Desktop RStudio Version : 1.2.1335 OS Version : linux (ubuntu) R Version : 3.6.1 ### Steps to reproduce the problem knit the following Rmd ``` --- title: "backticks inside your backticks..." output: html_document --- This shows that the in-line code mark is evaluated at a higher preference than the wrapping backticks: this `` `r nrow(c())` `` should be rendered as `` looking something like this `` ` r nrow(c())` `` (without the space needed to break the `` `r`` token). ``` ### Describe the problem in detail The internal `` `r expression` `` is evaluated before the enclosing double backticks. This makes it impossible to express an inline R expression as quoted code (the whole point of the double backticks in Markdown). ### Describe the behavior you expected I expect that the enclosing double backticks should take priority over the in-line expression evaluation. This is the more likely intention behind writing this sequence of bytes in a file and there is no other way to obtain knitted output. If a user did want generated ``-wrapped in-line expressions, this can be obtained exactly that way, by ```r expression```.

I understand that my issue may be closed if I don't fulfill my promises.

-->

I've got the following use case:

CI job on GitLab for the package repo that emits the `README.Rmd` as `README.html` and uploads it via API to Confluence Wiki.

The file in the repo uses `github_document` (for obvious reasons), but `rmarkdown::render` requires some gymnastics to produce an HTML output. So my approach now is to `sed -i -e 's/github_document/html_document/g' README.Rmd` before `render`ing. Feels a bit clunky.

By gymnastics I mean:

the `github_document` argument `html_preview` can be set to `TRUE`, but by default the output is sent to `tmp` and it's a bit hard to track the file down.

Through some detective work, I learned that actually the HTML preview is being sent to `RMARKDOWN_PREVIEW_DIR` in `env`, so I can set this to the directory where `render` is run and at least the preview will be "right there". The problem (more minor) is the file name becomes something like `preview-[alphanumeric_id].html`, meaning we need to do some globbing etc to match the file.

More problematic is that `RMARKDOWN_PREVIEW_DIR` is completely undocumented so I think I should consider it as internal behavior not to be relied on...

So, those are the pain points -- I think this could all be solved with a `keep_html` (or similar) option for `github_document` that would emit `README.html` as if `html_document` had been used.

title: RMarkdown does not produce valid XHTML
description:
The problem discussed in [issue #995](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/995) is still present. The `xmlns` attribute to the `<html>` tag causes some content-type detectors (Apache Tika) to declare generated html files as application/xhtml+xml. If the file is then served with this content type in the http header, the browser will report a parse error instead of displaying the page, since the file is not valid XHTML. 

In particular, seems that there are characters in the embedded javascript `<script>` blocks that cause the xml parser to fail.

There are two possible ideas for a fix that I came up with:

- Remove the `xmlns` atrribute from the `<html>` tag. The content type detector reports text/html and the page is served and parsed appropriately as ordinary HTML5. This option was rejected in #995.
- Add `<![CDATA[`...`]]>` delimiters around the portions of the document that are not valid XML. E.g.
```
<script>
/*<![CDATA[*/ 
...JQUERY_CODE... 
/*]]>*/
</script>
```
I added these delimiters around the embedded jQuery, bootstrap, Shiv, respond.js, the code labeled ECMA-262, jQuery Sticky Tabs, code folding script, and one other unlabeled javascript. With the CDATA delimiters present, the document successfully parsed as XHTML (in Chrome) and was displayed correctly when served as content-type:application/xhtml+xml

title: Misleading line numbers for errors generated in a child Rmd file?
description:
**Overview** One issue that I've noticed while when working with RMarkdown documents over the years is that for documents that are split up into multiple "child" Rmd files, included via statements like `{r child='xxx.Rmd'}`, the line numbers provided upon encountering an error during rendering are often misleading. In this case, multiple `Quitting from lines x-y (./child.Rmd)` statements are printed, only one of which (and sometimes possibly none?) is correct. **Example** Given the parent Rmd: 
```{r chunk1}
print('ok...')
```

```{r chunk2}
print('also ok...')
```

```{r child='child.Rmd'}
```
And the child Rmd: 
```{r chunk3}
message('good chunk in child doc...')
```

```{r chunk4}
stop('error occurs here...')
```
Attempting to render the parent document with a call to `rmarkdown::render()` results in the following error message: ``` |................................................. | 75% label: chunk4 Quitting from lines 6-7 (./child.Rmd) Quitting from lines NA-8 (./child.Rmd) Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : error occurs here... Calls: render ... handle -> withCallingHandlers -> withVisible -> eval -> eval ``` The actual error, which was generated from the chunk spanning lines 5-7 in `child.Rmd`, appears to correspond to the first set of line numbers "6-7". I'm guessing the later line numbers either refer to some internal version of the document generated, or perhaps to the `parent.Rmd`, and simply mislabeled as "child.Rmd"? Either way, those don't seem informative in this case. In a separate larger analysis, I noticed that the first set of lines appear to correspond to the actual problem, while the second set references some completely unrelated (and non-problematic) chunk in the same child document? It's a bit hard to isolate that behavior since it's part of a much larger analysis, but I'll update the issue if I find a way to. **Expected Behavior** Ideally, either a single set of lines would be presented, corresponding to the location of the chunk in the child document where the issue was actually encountered, or, if multiple lines are presented, it should represent something of a stack trace through the nested Rmd documents, e.g.: ``` Quitting from lines 120-121 (./parent.Rmd) Quitting from lines 200-250 (./child.Rmd) ``` Since the line to source the child document in the parent.Rmd is usually quite simple, however, it may be better just to ignore that altogether and only present a single set of line numbers corresponding to the actual problematic chunk. **Session Info** ``` R version 3.6.1 (2019-07-05) Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit) Running under: Arch Linux Locale: LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8 LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8 LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NAME=C LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C Package version: base64enc_0.1.3 digest_0.6.20 evaluate_0.14 glue_1.3.1 graphics_3.6.1 grDevices_3.6.1 highr_0.8 htmltools_0.3.6 jsonlite_1.6 knitr_1.24 magrittr_1.5 markdown_1.1 methods_3.6.1 mime_0.7 Rcpp_1.0.2 rmarkdown_1.14 stats_3.6.1 stringi_1.4.3 stringr_1.4.0 tinytex_0.15 tools_3.6.1 utils_3.6.1 xfun_0.8 yaml_2.2.0 Pandoc version: 2.7.3 ``` --- By filing an issue to this repo, I promise that - [X] I have fully read the issue guide at https://yihui.name/issue/. - [X] I have provided the necessary information about my issue. - If I'm asking a question, I have already asked it on Stack Overflow or RStudio Community, waited for at least 24 hours, and included a link to my question there. - If I'm filing a bug report, I have included a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example, and have also included `xfun::session_info('rmarkdown')`. title: Custom LaTeX macros not working in header-includes
description:
Hi All,

I am trying to add basic custom `LaTeX` `newcommand` macros
and trying to replicate this [SO answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/52484278/4687531)

Specifically I've created a `test_distill.Rmd` (a `distill` themed
Rmarkdown document) with the following contents:

```R
---
title: "Untitled"
description: |
  A new article created using the Distill format.
author:
  - name: Nora Jones 
    url: https://example.com/norajones
    affiliation: Spacely Sprockets
    affiliation_url: https://example.com/spacelysprokets
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: 
  distill::distill_article:
    includes:
        in_header: preamble.tex    
---

Let us test $\var$
```

I've also created the file `preamble.tex` in the same dir as
`test_distill.Rmd` and it's contents are:

```latex
\usepackage{amsthm}
\DeclareMathOperator*{\argmin}{argmin}
\newcommand{\var}{\mathrm{Var}}
```

When I render this as `HTML` the `\var` does not get parsed correctly
in `RStudio` viewer or in the knitted `HTML` output. It just displays

title: Embedded default CSS in HTML output causes wrong color when printing
rmarkdown should set output_dir option for tinytex
description:
Currently, the tinytex options for output_dir are not set when `rmarkdown::render` has non-default `output_dir` or `intermediate_dir` arguments.

This is a problem when the source code directory is read-only which could be the case in certain production settings where modifying the source code worktree is not allowed.

One way to get around this problem is for the user to set these options manually, but it is not intuitive and takes time to debug what is happening.

Steps to reproduce:
```bash
mkdir readonlydir

cat > readonlydir/demo.rmd <<EOF
---
output: pdf_document
---
Demo report 
EOF

# Change permissions of this directory to be read-only.
chmod -R ugo-w readonlydir

# This will fail.
Rscript \
  -e "idir <- '/tmp/intermediates_dir'" \
  -e "odir <- '/tmp/output_dir'" \
  -e "options(tinytex.verbose = TRUE)" \
  -e "rmarkdown::render('readonlydir/demo.rmd', output_dir=odir, intermediates_dir=idir)"

# This will pass.
Rscript \
  -e "idir <- '/tmp/intermediates_dir'" \
  -e "odir <- '/tmp/output_dir'" \
  -e "options(tinytex.verbose = TRUE)" \
  -e "options(tinytex.output_dir = idir)" \
  -e "options(tinytex.engine_args = sprintf('\'--output-directory=%s\'', idir))" \
  -e "rmarkdown::render('readonlydir/demo.rmd', output_dir=odir, intermediates_dir=idir)"
```

title: rmarkdown::render issue when calling render interacitvely
description:
I found an issue where dataframes are not printing when calling `rmarkdown::render` from a chunk. 

To reproduce, create an RMarkdown file `test.Rmd` with the following contents and open it in RStudio: 

````
---
title: "Render Issue"
author: "Mark Kirzon"
date: "8/2/2019"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, cache=FALSE)
library(tidyverse)   
```

This prints fine when the document is knit with the 'Knit' button or Ctrl+Shift+K
```{r}
a = data.frame(A = c(1:5), B = head(LETTERS, 5), stringsAsFactors = F)
print(a)
```

If this chunk is executed, the above dataframe is not displayed in the output html. I expected the behavior to be the same. 
```{r, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
rmarkdown::render("test.Rmd")
```
````

This is what it looks like when knit using the button/keyboard shortcut:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5666220/62388599-9c6def80-b512-11e9-8788-47ab60642585.png)

This is what it looks like when executing the block: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5666220/62388584-92e48780-b512-11e9-88ef-e478b2014949.png)

I think this is a bug as I am unable to print a normal dataframe when executing a chunk with the `rmarkdown::render` call. Note that it works fine if the same `rmarkdown::render` is run from the command line, rather than executed as a chunk. 

### Why I need to be able to execute from a chunk 
I like to include a chunk at the end of my analyses that has the various parametrization configurations that I frequently need to loop over. I've found it's really convenient and organized when all parametrizations are stored with the analysis. Here's the template that I include at the end of my analyses, which loops over N parameter configurations and updates the N html files. 
````
```{r looped_render, include=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
# Run this chunk interactively to render this document with custom parameters, to a custom destination

# Configure Output and parameters
path_out      = "" # If empty, current directory
output_prefix = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path)) # Output filename, needs to be non-empty
list_params = list(list()) # This is a list of lists. Leave as is if the document has no parameters

for (params_tmp in list_params) {
  print(params_tmp)
  
  output_fn = sprintf("%s%s.html", output_prefix, paste(names(params_tmp), unname(params_tmp), sep= "_", collapse = "&"))
  
  rmarkdown::render(
    input         = basename(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path),
    output_file   = file.path(path_out, output_fn),
    params        = params_tmp)
}
```
````

title: add a pagebreak feature in pdf, word and html document
description:
The idea came from a discussion in [rstudio.community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/starting-toc-on-a-new-page-after-title-page-in-rmd-to-word-doc-output/36081/9)

I think this is possible to easily add a feature where a pagebreak would be included in pdf, html or work document. It is already possible in pdf document with latex `\\newpage{}` but it also possible in html or word document using a custom output syntax. 

This feature is one of those available in [lua filters examples for pandoc](https://github.com/pandoc/lua-filters/tree/master/pagebreak). Adding `\newpage` or `\pagebreak` anywhere in the rmarkdown document will be modified by lua filter to be a pagebreak in the output document.
This would also work in epub, and can be customised via env variable (with current lua script).
For odt, it is not out of the box.

This lua script was interesting and that is why I try to implement it in rmarkdown by adding lua filter inside the package. See a working proof of concept in this branch
[cderv/rmarkdown@pagebreak](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/compare/master...cderv:pagebreak)
(if a draft PR is better to suggest such feature, I could also do that)

I don't know if you would consider adding such a lua file in rmarkdown package, also considering the lua filter is a feature available in pandoc > 2.0. Otherwise, implementing this feature in R directly should also be possible I guess and no dependent of pandoc version. 
However I have other ideas of use for Lua filter and this try was a way to begin with those and it would be nice to be able to add feature to rmarkdown thanks to Lua filters. 

Please, tell me if you are interested in a PR or if this is out of scope for Rmarkdown. 
Thanks.

title: Request: Allow dynamic parameters in parameterized Rmd reports
description:
Currently, the `params` of a parameterized report requires all parameters to be explicitly listed in the YAML of the Rmd file. Trying to use a parameter that has not been defined in the YAML results in a fatal error. I certainly understand and support this design decision.

However, I think there are some cases where being able to use parameters that haven't been defined in the YAML makes sense. Suppose you have a parent Rmd document that includes a child document, and that child document itself is a parameter. The parent Rmd doesn't know what parameters the child has. When I call `rmarkdown::render()` and supply a child document, I want to be able to also supply the necessary parameters, but rmarkdown complains that they aren't defined in the YAML. There are workarounds, but I think it would be great if there was a way for me to tell rmarkdown to allow undefined parameters, perhaps supporting something like `rmarkdown::render(check_params = FALSE)`

title: pagetitle metadata inserted as pandoc argument prevents setting title dynamically
description:
While working on this [community question](https://community.rstudio.com/t/use-r-object-in-title-of-flexdashboard/35847/2), it was discovered that a prior fix in rmarkdown was maybe a bit too strong. 

With pandoc, it is possible to use several yaml metadata blocs to define variables. Not only the one at the top. This [pandoc feature](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#extension-yaml_metadata_block)

However, if not title is set in the top header block, a `pagetitle` var is set to the name of the document
https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/227d2e15173e3e3b3f6eeb063bc17009253a2fb3/R/html_document_base.R#L112-L113
using `--metadata` overwrites any other definition in the document (in a later block)

That is causing a strange behavior :

This works 
````
---
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
my_title <- "I am the title"
```
---
title: '`r my_title`'
---

Test R Markdown HTML
```` 
but `pagetitle` variable is set anyway to the name of the document (and not the title)

This does not work 
````
---
output: 
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
my_title <- "I am the title"
```
---
title: '`r my_title`'
---

Test R Markdown flexdashboard
```` 
because flexdashboard currently use only `pagetitle`, that is set by Rmarkdown to the input utf8 filename. 
I opened rstudio/flexdashboard#226 to propose a more consistent use of `title` instead of `pagetitle`

Anyway, I think setting `--metadata pagetitle=` if no title is in the yaml header is a bit too strong as it overwrites. 

I would suggest two options
* use `--metadata-file` and a tmp yaml file to set this option because this does not overwrite any other definition (see [Pandoc Manual](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#option--metadata-file))
* Change parsing in Rmardown to all yaml block to be correct with extension [yaml_metadata_block](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#extension-yaml_metadata_block) and get all the metadata define in a md document. 

First one seems easy. Second one could have more impact but would be more relevant to adjust pandoc behavior. 

What do you think ?

title: Cannot add extra LaTeX content at the end of pdf_document using includes in YAML header
description:
Hi,

I am having difficulty adding extra content to the end of a PDF document using the `includes` option in the YAML header. I think the text below should create a minimally reproducible example of the error I'm running into.

Here is the basic setup to show the error (at least on my end).

First I created a `test.Rmd` file with this content:

```
---
output: 
  pdf_document:
    includes:
      after_body: test-add.tex
---

## R Markdown

Here is some text.
```

Then I created a second document, in the same directory as the first, titled `test-add.Rmd`, which includes the following content ~~(I added the backslashes here on GitHub to ignore the Rmd code blocks inside the code block below)~~:
````
---
output: 
  pdf_document:
    keep_tex: yes
---

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
````
 
I knit the `test-add.Rmd` file to produce the `test-add.tex` file; the PDF is produced and everything looks fine. Then I expected when I knit the `test.Rmd` file is would add the content to the end of the document. Here is the error in the `RStudio console`:

title: reference_docx rather than csl determining style of bibliography in word output (possibly bug)
description:
The following minor issue yields unexpected (from my point of view) output:

When setting both, a `reference_docx: my-style.docx` and `csl: apa.csl` in the yaml-header, the csl file will have no effect if the reference-docx already contains a bibliography.

In other words: irrespective of which csl file one chooses, the output will always look the same. This might be unexpected by many users.

Obviously, one can exclude the bibliography from the reference-docx and easily gets the desired output.

title: Trouble with an alternate MathJax URL and a custom template
description:
I think the problem comes from **rmarkdown**.
I found a little bug in **rmarkdown** when a HTML document is rendered with a custom template and `mathjax: <some_url>`.
For now, here is a workaround for this bug. In https://github.com/topepo/MathJax-test/blob/master/_output.yml, you can use these arguments:
```yaml
bookdown::gitbook:
  css: FES.css
  dev: svglite
  split_by: section
  mathjax: null
  pandoc_args: --mathjax=https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/mathjax/2.7.5/latest.js?config=TeX-MML-AM_HTMLorMML.js
```
I will open a PR in **rmarkdown** to fix this bug.

_Originally posted by @RLesur in https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/issues/683#issuecomment-506997150_

description:

- [X] I have learned the Github Markdown syntax, and formatted my issue correctly.

---

This is a suggestion, to solve a minor annoyance for me and maybe help some other people.

I mostly use R from the command line, rather than via Rstudio. I am working on integrating some rmarkdown report generation in a `make`-based approach:

```{makefile}
report-%.pdf: report.Rmd # ... some other dependencies set by % wildcard
	R -e "rmarkdown::render('$<', output_file='$@', output_format='pdf_document')" --args $(filter-out $<,$^)
```

Translating a bit for those less familiar with make: this specifies how to a create a target file named report-X.pdf (or report-Y.pdf, report-something.pdf, etc) from report.Rmd and other dependencies. `$<` resolves to report.Rmd and `$@` to the name of the target.  I was slightly surprised to discover that I had to manually specify `output_format=...` for this work.  When unspecified, I get the error:

```
> rmarkdown::render('report.Rmd', output_file='report-test.pdf')

processing file: report.Rmd
  |.................................................................| 100%
  ordinary text without R code

output file: report.knit.md

/usr/bin/pandoc +RTS -K512m -RTS report.utf8.md --to html4 --from markdown+autolink_bare_uris+ascii_identifiers+tex_math_single_backslash+smart --outputreport-test.pdf --email-obfuscation none --self-contained --standalone --section-divs --template /home/carl/libs/Rpackages/rmarkdown/rmd/h/default.html --no-highlight --variable highlightjs=1 --variable 'theme:bootstrap' --include-in-header /tmp/RtmppWfeua/rmarkdown-str602f78928780.html --mathjax --variable 'mathjax-url:https://mathjax.rstudio.com/latest/MathJax.js?config=TeX-AMS-MML_HTMLorMML' --metadata pagetitle=report.utf8.md
cannot produce pdf output from html4
Error: pandoc document conversion failed with error 1
Execution halted
make: *** [Makefile:32: report-test.pdf] Error 1
```

Obviously, I have the solution to avoid that error.  However, I'd like my make rule to be:

```{makefile}
report-%.pdf report-%.html report-%.docx: report.Rmd # ... some other dependencies set by % wildcard
	R -e "rmarkdown::render('$<', output_file='$@')" --args $(filter-out $<,$^)
```

This would allow the user to build whichever of the desired target types, and keep generation logic concise, consistent, etc. That approach would maintain the inference logic within the library, where details like `docx==word` are more readily known and minimize future external changes if there are tweaks to internal rmarkdown definitions.

Seems like something akin to

```{r}
# ...
if (missing(output_format) & !missing(output_file)) {
  output_format <- sprintf("%s_document", gsub("doc.*","word",gsub("^.+\\.(pdf|doc.*|html)$","\\1",output_file)))
}
# ...
```

in the `render` logic could do the trick, but I haven't dug into the details to see what other conflicts there might be, etc.

## Issue summary

When rendering an `html_notebook` with `rmarkdown::render`, if an R chunk returns a character vector, the elements are printed line by line in addition to the usual character vector output.

library(rmarkdown)

letters[1:5]

<!--

-->

---

**Note:** Sorry for the strange line wrapping below. I used the output format`github_document()`, but apparently GitHub markdown now respects line breaks. I manually fixed a few of the more egregious breaks below.

---

I have created a custom output format that extends `html_document()`. I
noticed that the argument `keep_md` is not properly inherited.

My first thought was that both the arguments `keep_md` and `df_print`
might have issues since they are arguments for both `output_format()`
and `html_document()`, but somehow `df_print` is properly inherited.

``` r
intersect(names(formals(rmarkdown::output_format)),
          names(formals(rmarkdown::html_document)))
```

    ## [1] "keep_md"  "df_print"

Here is a minimal example to demonstrate the issue. The function below
is a trivial output format that wraps `html_document()`, but doesn’t
change anything.

``` r
# A trivial wrapper for html_document()
html_wrap <- function(...) {
  rmarkdown::output_format(knitr = rmarkdown::knitr_options(),
                           pandoc = rmarkdown::pandoc_options(to = "html"),
                           base_format = rmarkdown::html_document(...))
}
```

If a user runs `render()` on an R Markdown file with the following YAML
header:

    ---
    output: html_wrap
    ---

then this would result in the following call to
`create_output_format()`:

``` r
o1 <- rmarkdown:::create_output_format(name = "html_wrap",
                                       options = list())
```

This inherits the default values from `html_document()` as expected:

``` r
environment(environment(o1[["pre_knit"]])[["overlay"]])[["toc"]]
```

    ## [1] FALSE

``` r
o1$keep_md
```

    ## [1] FALSE

``` r
environment(environment(o1[["pre_knit"]])[["overlay"]])[["keep_md"]]
```

    ## [1] FALSE

``` r
o1$df_print
```

    ## [1] "default"

``` r
environment(environment(o1[["pre_knit"]])[["overlay"]])[["df_print"]]
```

    ## [1] "default"

However, if a user runs `render()` on an R Markdown file with the
following YAML header:

    ---
    output:
      html_wrap:
        toc: true
        keep_md: TRUE
        df_print: "kable"
    ---

then this would result in the following call to `create_output_format()` ([line 378](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/f32025815587a2faf47a9bc5df06177541fab117/R/render.R#L378)):

``` r
o2 <- rmarkdown:::create_output_format(name = "html_wrap",
                                       options = list(toc = TRUE,
                                                      keep_md = TRUE,
                                                      df_print = "kable"))
```

`toc` is inherited as expected:

``` r
environment(environment(o2[["pre_knit"]])[["overlay"]])[["toc"]]
```

    ## [1] TRUE

`df_print` is inherited not only in the environment of the `pre_knit()`
function, but the value of the output format is also inherited:

``` r
o2$df_print
```

    ## [1] "kable"

``` r
environment(environment(o2[["pre_knit"]])[["overlay"]])[["df_print"]]
```

    ## [1] "kable"

Unfortunately, `keep_md` is only updated in the environment of the
`pre_knit()` function, where it has no effect.

``` r
o2$keep_md
```

    ## [1] FALSE

``` r
environment(environment(o2[["pre_knit"]])[["overlay"]])[["keep_md"]]
```

    ## [1] TRUE

When `render()` adds `rmarkdown.keep_md` to `knitr::opts_knit`, it uses
`output_format$keep_md` ([line 500](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/f32025815587a2faf47a9bc5df06177541fab117/R/render.R#L500)).
When `render()` decides to keep the md file, it again uses
`output_format$keep_md` ([line 869](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/f32025815587a2faf47a9bc5df06177541fab117/R/render.R#L869)).

Potentially related Issues include \#842 and \#928.

Note that [`bookdown::html_document2()`](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/master/R/html.R#L123) does not have this issue.

``` r
rmarkdown:::create_output_format(name = "bookdown::html_document2",
                                 options = list(keep_md = TRUE))$keep_md
```

    ## [1] TRUE

But it is unclear to me what part of its code would change the
inheritance of `keep_md`.

``` r
bookdown::html_document2
```

    ## function (..., number_sections = TRUE, pandoc_args = NULL, base_format = rmarkdown::html_document) 
    ## {
    ##     base_format = get_base_format(base_format)
    ##     config = base_format(..., number_sections = number_sections, 
    ##         pandoc_args = pandoc_args2(pandoc_args))
    ##     post = config$post_processor
    ##     config$post_processor = function(metadata, input, output, 
    ##         clean, verbose) {
    ##         if (is.function(post)) 
    ##             output = post(metadata, input, output, clean, verbose)
    ##         x = read_utf8(output)
    ##         x = restore_appendix_html(x, remove = FALSE)
    ##         x = restore_part_html(x, remove = FALSE)
    ##         x = resolve_refs_html(x, global = !number_sections)
    ##         x = clean_pandoc2_highlight_tags(x)
    ##         write_utf8(x, output)
    ##         output
    ##     }
    ##     config$bookdown_output_format = "html"
    ##     config = set_opts_knit(config)
    ##     config
    ## }
    ## <bytecode: 0x558e41c8af40>
    ## <environment: namespace:bookdown>

It appears to be directly editing the base output format instead of
inheriting from it using `output_format(base_format = )`, which is what
the [documentation](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/format-custom.html) recommends.

What is the recommended method for passing all arguments provided to a
custom output format to the base output format that it extends?

I realize that I could hard-code a work-around for the custom output
format to handle `keep_md`, but this is fragile. If a future release of
rmarkdown added a new argument to `output_format()`/`html_document()`, I
would have to update my code and also put a restriction on the minimum
version of rmarkdown that is compatible.

``` r
html_wrap2 <- function(...) {
  
  opts <- list(...)
  
  if (!is.null(opts$keep_md)) keep_md <- opts$keep_md else keep_md <- FALSE
  
  rmarkdown::output_format(knitr = rmarkdown::knitr_options(),
                           pandoc = rmarkdown::pandoc_options(to = "html"),
                           keep_md = keep_md,
                           base_format = rmarkdown::html_document(...))
}
rmarkdown:::create_output_format(name = "html_wrap2",
                                 options = list(keep_md = TRUE))$keep_md
```

    ## [1] TRUE

description:
By filing an issue to this repo, I promise that - [x] I have fully read the issue guide at https://yihui.name/issue/. - [x] I have provided the necessary information about my issue. - If I'm asking a question, I have already asked it on Stack Overflow or RStudio Community, waited for at least 24 hours, and included a link to my question there. - If I'm filing a bug report, I have included a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example, and have also included `xfun::session_info('rmarkdown')`. The hidden [knitr chunk option](https://yihui.name/knitr/options/) `indent` behaves differently for `html_document()` between pandoc 1 and 2. I realize this is a minor issue since `indent` is only supposed to be used for markdown output. Also, it could be argued that the pandoc 2 behavior is preferred. But since I observed it, I wanted to share the result in case anyone depended on the pandoc 1 behavior. ## Reproducible Rmd file The examples below use the following Rmd file, which I saved as `test-indent.Rmd`: ```` --- output: html_document: keep_md: true --- ```{r example, indent=" "} 1 + 1 ``` ```` ## pandoc 1 preserves the indentation in the HTML file Rendering this document with pandoc 1.19.2.1 preserves the indentation in the HTML file: ``` $ Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("test-indent.Rmd", quiet = TRUE)' $ grep '1 + 1' test-indent.* test-indent.html:

r 1 + 1

test-indent.md: 1 + 1 test-indent.Rmd:1 + 1 ``` which causes the code chunks to be malformed (screenshot below): ![indent-pandoc1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1608317/55034241-6613e700-4feb-11e9-8e21-ed1f9d48f6c5.png) ``` > xfun::session_info(c("knitr", "rmarkdown")) R version 3.5.1 (2018-07-02) Platform: x86_64-conda_cos6-linux-gnu (64-bit) Running under: Ubuntu 18.04.2 LTS Locale: LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8 LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8 LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NAME=C LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C Package version: base64enc_0.1.3 digest_0.6.18 evaluate_0.13 glue_1.3.1 graphics_3.5.1 grDevices_3.5.1 highr_0.8 htmltools_0.3.6 jsonlite_1.6 knitr_1.22 magrittr_1.5 markdown_0.9 methods_3.5.1 mime_0.6 Rcpp_1.0.1 rmarkdown_1.12 stats_3.5.1 stringi_1.4.3 stringr_1.4.0 tinytex_0.11 tools_3.5.1 utils_3.5.1 xfun_0.5 yaml_2.2.0 Pandoc version: 1.19.2.1 ``` For conda users, I created this environment with the following command: ``` conda create -y -n test-pandoc1 -c conda-forge pandoc=1.19.2.1 r-rmarkdown ``` ## pandoc 2 removes the indentation in the HTML file Rendering this document with pandoc 2.7.1 removes the indentation in the HTML file: ``` $ Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("test-indent.Rmd", quiet = TRUE)' $ grep '1 + 1' test-indent.* test-indent.html:

title: Enable rmarkdown::render() output_file argument to automate file extension
description:
I'm using `rmarkdown::render()` to create multiple output formats from a single .Rmd. I would like to change the name of the file *without* needing to specify the file extension. For example, this works:

```r
purrr::walk2(
  .x = c("ioslides_presentation", "slidy_presentation", "powerpoint_presentation"),
  .y = c("html", "html", "pptx"),
  ~ rmarkdown::render(
    "index.Rmd",
    output_file = glue::glue("slide_{.x}.{.y}"),
    output_dir = "gallery-output/test/",
    output_format = .x,
  )
)
```

But I would like to be able to specify the output file name dynamically (`{.x}`) and have the extension (currently `{.y}`) be automatic based on my output format. 

If I don’t specify `output_file` that happens, but I can’t exert control over the output filename. So, in my example, the ioslides presentation file gets overwritten by the slidy presentation.

```r
purrr::walk(
  .x = c("ioslides_presentation", "slidy_presentation", "powerpoint_presentation"),
  ~ rmarkdown::render(
    "index.Rmd",
    output_dir = "gallery-output/test2/",

)

Thank you for considering this feature request!
Alison

title: Disable custom margins with document class specified
description:
If one sets the margins without `geometry`, such as when using KOMA-Script, the custom Rmarkdown setting stops this from taking effect:

```markdown
---
documentclass: scrbook
classoption:
- DIV=12
---
```

At the moment, the margins are set to one inch unless there are custom settings for `geometry` in the YAML front matter:

<https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/cdf4ff0598bbae6c231451bad046e931a84c97aa/R/pdf_document.R#L173>

I would think that the user is very unlikely to want the margins set this way if using a document class other than `article`. Could I suggest that the custom margins be removed if either `geometry` or `documentclass` are set in the front matter?

`tag, as per [John Gruber](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax#block) > When you do want to insert a `

title: Add ability to append text to figure markdown?
description:
The pandoc filter [pandoc-crossref](http://lierdakil.github.io/pandoc-crossref/) provides syntax for creating cross references to figures and tables:

```
Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit (see @fig:figure1)

![Caption for figure](/path/to/figure){#fig:figure1}
```

It's possible to use it as a filter when knitting, and it works great:

```
---
title: "Title goes here"
output: 
  html_document: 
    pandoc_args:
      - --filter
      - pandoc-crossref
---

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit (see @fig:figure1)

![Caption for figure](/path/to/figure){#fig:figure1}
```

However, there's no easy solution to adding the `{#fig:blah}` to figures generated with R.

I've found two solutions so far:

## Use `cat()`

If you add `echo=FALSE, results="asis"` to the chunk options and use `cat()` to add the figure reference, the correct Markdown is generated and knitting works:

````
---
title: "Title goes here"
output: 
  html_document: 
    pandoc_args:
      - --filter
      - pandoc-crossref
---

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit (see @fig:figure1)

```{r method1, fig.width=4, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Here's a plot", echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
plot(1:10)
cat("{#fig:figure1}")
```
````

One problem with this is that it breaks if you use `echo=TRUE`. Which leads to the second method:

## Use raw markdown

Another option is to use raw markdown syntax to point to the figures that knitr generates:

````
---
title: "Title goes here"
output: 
  html_document: 
    pandoc_args:
      - --filter
      - pandoc-crossref
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Save figures to a folder named "fig"
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "fig/", echo = FALSE)
```

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit (see @fig:figure2)

```{r method2, fig.width=4, fig.height=4, include=FALSE}
plot(1:10)
```

![Here's a plot](fig/method2-1.png){#fig:figure2}
````

With this method you can use `echo=TRUE, results="hide"` to get the code but suppress the picture. This doesn't work with standalone HTML files, though.

---

Neither of these options are especially intuitive and they feel hacked together.

It might be nice to add an additional chunk option like `fig.suffix`, similar to `fig.lp`, that would append the passed-in text to the generated Markdown.

The main things to note about this bug:

1. Loading the `kableExtra` package modifies the `.knitEnv$meta` object;
2. Calling `rmarkdown::render()` causes that object to explode in size, presumedly from here: https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/bbd0786d82f82d9eaef7f0b9e2c553b523407161/R/render.R#L416-L423

title: working directory changed when filenames contain spaces
description:
Given a simple R Markdown file that writes a CSV to disk:

````
---
title: "filenames with spaces"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
filename <- paste0("mtcars_",Sys.Date(),".csv")
write.csv(mtcars, filename)
```

Here is a link to the file [`r filename`](`r filename`)
````

Write that R Markdown to a file named `with spaces.Rmd`; the whitespace in the filename is important.

Run `rmarkdown::render` with output and intermediates directories:

```r
rmarkdown::render("with spaces.Rmd", output_dir = "output", intermediates_dir = "inter")
```

The `inter` directory contains the R Markdown generated CSV file:

```r
list.files("inter")
# => [1] "mtcars_2019-02-19.csv"
```

The output directory (as expected), contains the rendered HTML:

```r
list.files("output")
# => [1] "with spaces.html"
```

This behavior does not happen if the R Markdown file is named `index.Rmd`. Rendering a file named `index.Rmd` causes the CSV to be written to the working directory (in this case, containing the R Markdown file).

Workaround: Avoid using spaces in R Markdown filenames.
Workaround: Avoid using `intermediates_dir`.

title: Chunk Output Inline and remote tables: kable force a table collect
description:
Dear all,

I've stumbled on a small issue when using a notebook (or more generally the Chunk Output Inline option) and a DBI connection. The default choice is to use kable to display the tables. This works as expected for local table but has the unfortunate side effect to `collect` the tables if they were not local. This is different from the usual behavior which collect only a few line from the remote database. 

This behavior is consistent with any DBI connexion. For instance, using RSQLite:
---
    title: "R Notebook"
    output: html_notebook
    ---

    ```{r}
    library(RSQLite)
    library(dplyr)
    con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), "iris")
    copy_to(con, iris, "iris")
    tbl(con, "iris")
    ```
There is a global option setting to modify this behavior
```r
options(paged.print = FALSE)
```
but it disables the nice kable display for all the tables whereas they are local or not.

I feel a better option would be to have a different behavior for local and remote tables so that we can keep the nice kable display even when some tables are not local.

Thank you and let me know how I can help.

title: ioslides does not support Markdown image attribute (e.g. width)
description:
In an RMarkdown presentation, I have a local image embedded via pandoc’s syntax:

```markdown
![Caption](path/to/image.png){width=90%}

title: remove `encoding` parameter in `render()` to avoid redundant and annoying warning
description:
Now, `knitr::knit('input_file', encoding = 'native.enc')` would give a warning

The encoding ("native.enc") is not UTF-8. We will only support UTF-8 in the future. Please re-save your file "demo.Rmd" with the UTF-8 encoding.

title: Use new LaTeX templates from Pandoc
`rmarkdown::render` does not respect symlinks
description:
When rendering a `.Rmd` file that is a symlink, the working directory becomes the parent directory of the original file where the symlink points to. As a result, the output appears in a different directory than the `.Rmd` file.

See the example below:
````
mkdir /tmp/foo
cd /tmp/foo
mkdir bar
mkdir baz
cat > bar/example.Rmd
---
title: Test
output: html_document
---

```{r}
getwd()
```
^D
ln -s ../bar/example.Rmd baz
````

The file structure looks like this:
```
/tmp/foo
├── bar
│   └── example.Rmd
└── baz
    └── example.Rmd -> ../bar/example.Rmd
```
Now I proceed to rendering the html:
```
cd baz
R -e "rmarkdown::render('example.Rmd',output_file='output.html')"
```
Now the file tree looks like this:
```
/tmp/foo
├── bar
│   ├── example.Rmd
│   └── output.html
└── baz
    └── example.Rmd -> ../bar/example.Rmd
```
Also, the output of `getwd()` in the html equals `"/tmp/foo/bar"`

In other words, running the command for rendering `/tmp/foo/baz/example.Rmd` resulted in `/tmp/foo/bar/example.Rmd` being rendered instead. That is, `render` followed the symlink before rendering the document. 

The expected behavior would be that `markdown::render` treats symlinks like normal files and does not follow them. At least, the current [docs](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/rmarkdown/versions/1.11/topics/render) do not mention anything about this special treatment for symlinks.

I'm not complaining though, `rmarkdown` is pretty neat. I just bumped into this and wanted to point it out :)

title: dir with figure is deleted in multi format generation
description:
From a question on [Rstudio community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/rmarkown-pdf-document-removes-other-files/20289/3), it seems that default behaviour for `html_document` is to delete the whole `files_dir` of the form `*_files` even if something else from other format is there.

I tried to come up with a reprex for this. See below

* `github_document` generate a figure that lives in a `figure-gfm` folder, required to use with the md file generated 
* `html_document` by default is `self_contained=TRUE`, so cleaning is activated (unless `clean = FALSE` in `render`. The cleaning process suppress the **whole** `files_dir` , *including the `figure-gfm`
* using output format `"all"` to generate both format shows that everything is deleted and the png file for the plot does not exist anymore for the github_document format.

````r
# create temporary directory to work in for example
dir_temp <- fs::path_temp("rmd")
fs::dir_create(dir_temp)

# create test rmd file
test_rmd <- fs::file_temp("test", dir_temp, ext = ".Rmd")
writeLines(c('---
title: "R Notebook"
output:
  github_document: default
  html_document:
      self_contained: true
---',
'This is a test file

```{r cars-plot, fig.cap = "plot of cars"}
plot(cars)
```

```{r mean-speed}
mean_speed <- mean(cars$speed)
```
'), test_rmd)

fs::dir_ls(dir_temp)
# creating plot file in a new folder
rmarkdown::render(test_rmd, "github_document")
fs::dir_ls(dir_temp, regexp = "_files", recursive = TRUE)

# without clean the dir is here
rmarkdown::render(test_rmd, "html_document", clean = FALSE)
fs::dir_ls(dir_temp, regexp = "_files", recursive = TRUE)

# with default clean = TRUE, the whole dir is deleted, even the file from github_document format.
rmarkdown::render(test_rmd, "html_document")
fs::dir_ls(dir_temp, regexp = "_files", recursive = TRUE)
fs::dir_ls(dir_temp, recursive = TRUE)

# no folder for github document containing the image
rmarkdown::render(test_rmd, "all")
fs::dir_ls(dir_temp, regexp = "_files", recursive = TRUE)
fs::dir_ls(dir_temp, recursive = TRUE)

# both folder are present
rmarkdown::render(test_rmd, "all", clean = FALSE)
fs::dir_ls(dir_temp, regexp = "_files", recursive = TRUE)
fs::dir_ls(dir_temp, recursive = TRUE)

# clean
unlink(dir_temp, recursive = TRUE)
````

There are different argument fir a workaround (`clean = FALSE`, or `self_contained: false`, change fig_path location) that will prevent that, but seems like an non wanted effect. 

What do you think ?

title: Dropdown navigation menu for HTML output
description:
## Intro
About a year ago there was a request #1116 for dropdown menus in the Rmarkdown HTML output. The contributed solution didn't work well for me, so I spent some time putting together [a standalone solution](https://github.com/mjaquiery/toc_menu) which produces a bootstrap-themed fixed navigation menu ([demo here](https://mjaquiery.github.io/toc_menu/demo)).

I don't have the time or knowledge to integrate my solution with the traditional Rmarkdown workflow, but perhaps someone with the necessary experience would benefit from having my code available. 

## What the code does
* Identify a heirachy of elements with the 'section' class (which Rmarkdown assigns to headers of each level).
* Compile the heirachy into a navigable menu with dropdowns where appropriate.
* Style the menu using Bootstrap nav and dropdown menu classes.
* Insert that menu into the HTML document above the main content.

## Advantages
I've found the floating ToC quite invasive for many documents, especially longer ones. This version is unobtrusive and provides links to everywhere in the document from everywhere in the document.

## Known issues
* The navigation to name markers doesn't account for the nav bar itself, so the title you asked to jump to is always hidden below the nav bar.

## Shortfalls
There are some features which aren't present here that would make the menu easier to use and more streamlined with the other Rmarkdown stuff:
* Customisable heading level depth. This is supported in the javascript, but can't be specified via Rmarkdown option at present
* Respecting user wishes re: in/exclusion similar to .tabset
* Easy implementation as with .tabset

P.S. please forgive (and correct) me if this isn't appropriate as an 'issue'; I'm fairly new to larger projects on GitHub.

title: Templates in PowerPoint Presentations with RStudio
description:
I'm starting work on a project to create PowerPoint presentations, and I'm trying to decide if I should use rmarkdown or a separate package (e.g., officer). I've watched the [webinar](https://resources.rstudio.com/webinars/make-powerpoint-presentations-with-r-markdown-nathan-stephens) and worked through what is given on [Rendering PowerPoint Presentations with RStudio](https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004672913-Rendering-PowerPoint-presentations-with-RStudio) in an attempt to create a working proof-of-concept. The particular proof-of-concept I'm attempting to create involves a corporate template. So far, I have not been able to get it working correctly.

I believe the instructions in the [Templates](https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004672913-Rendering-PowerPoint-presentations-with-RStudio#templates) section of that page are incorrect. After looking at the layouts given in a blank PowerPoint file, it looks like the order (and capitalization) should be

1. Title
2. Title and Content
3. Section Header
4. Two Content

instead of 

1. Title
2. Section header
3. Title and content
4. Two Content

Along with that "bug", I can't seem to get a handle on how many "#"s are needed for each level. The various combinations of 'slide_level' and "#"s I've tried do not seem to match the information on that support page. Could we get a full-blown working example (or multiple examples) that includes a template and content at all of the various levels (i.e., a working reproducible example)?

To wrap up, the main question I still have is, Is rmarkdown for creating PowerPoint presentations developed enough to make use of it at this point, or should I fall back to using officer (or other package) at this point?

title: HTML summary triangle is missing in Firefox
description:
## Description of the issue

The triangle that signals that a HTML section has been folded with `<details><summary>...</summary></details>` is missing in Firefox, as illustrated in the screenshot below from the [pkgdown details page](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/articles/test/details.html):

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8360597/48353275-507ed000-e68f-11e8-870a-50b7707e09b2.png)

## Steps to reproduce 

Run `rmarkdown::render()` on the following example and view the ouput **in Firefox**:

````
---
title: 'Missing triangle'
output: html_document
---

<details>Once upon a time...</details>

<details>
  <summary>Long story</summary>
  Once upon a time...
</details>
````

## Source of this issue

According to Mozilla docs, [the HTML spec requires `display: list-item` to display the triangle. On the other hand, `display: block` will remove it.](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/summary#Default_style)

This means the current `rmarkdown` bootstrap template will remove the triangle:

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/98751369bac17d1ae2a5ce966c11f0c473d6d8d7/inst/rmd/h/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.css#L27-L29

## Proposed fix

1. This was fixed upstream in https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/21060. The best solution would be to update `rmarkdown` bootstrap template to the latest version.

1. According to https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1260, it may be difficult to update the template so an alternative (temporary) fix would be to simply add:

```css
summary {
  display: list-item
}
```

to [`default.html`](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/0ff85d8db1c1b75386cc752062f6016884709139/inst/rmd/h/default.html) to overwrite the style specified in [`boostrap.css`](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/f111cf9601393317bac9cbc0e6dc81336c4fe002/inst/rmd/h/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.css)

## Additional info

This issue was first reported by @maelle in the pkgdown repo: https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/884

I can try to submit a PR if that helps. I would probably need some guidance if you decide to go with the first proposed fix (update bootstrap template) though.

I know I have to save my Rmd file as "UTF-8 without BOM," however, I was wondering if there would be any way to render Rmd file encoded with UTF-8 with BOM.

#> 
#> [1] /Users/jenny/resources/R/library
#> [2] /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.5/Resources/library
```

</details>

---

As of version 2.2.2, Pandoc parses YAML with HsYAML, which has a stricter interpretation of YAML 1.2 than the previous approach.

https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/b8573aab292cc7c75b9a7268602799e7abda5f81/changelog#L953-L959

```
pandoc (2.2.2)

  * Use HsYAML instead of yaml for translations and YAML metadata (#4747).
    yaml wraps a C library; HsYAML is pure Haskell.  Advances #4535.

    Note: HsYAML implements YAML 1.2, in which the valid true
    values are `true`, `True`, `TRUE`.  This means a change in
    the semantics of YAML metadata that could affect users:
    `y`, `yes`, and `on` no longer count as true values.
```

It's pretty common to see `yes` used as a true value in `.Rmd` documents, although perhaps it is always in the `output` key, which is *parsed* by Pandoc but not actually *used*. That YAML is used by rmarkdown itself. It still might be a good idea to shift from `yes` to `TRUE` in YAML we produce, in the long run.

Here is the one semi-breakage I see: indentation in a multi-line YAML collection.

Take the YAML from [3.1.10.5 Pandoc arguments](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/html-document.html#pandoc-arguments) in R Markdown: The Definitive Guide

``` yaml
---
title: "Habits"
output:
  html_document:
    pandoc_args: [
      "--title-prefix", "Foo",
      "--id-prefix", "Bar"
    ]
---
```

If I use `rmarkdown::render()` or the IDE's Knit button on this, I see these WARNINGs, but the render still works:

```
[WARNING] Could not parse YAML metadata at line 13 column 1: :7:26: Unexpected '
  '
[WARNING] This document format requires a nonempty <title> element.
  Please specify either 'title' or 'pagetitle' in the metadata.
  Falling back to 'foo.utf8'

Output created: foo.html
```

Changing the indentation clears the WARNING:

```yaml
---
title: "Habits"
output:
  html_document:
    pandoc_args: [
                   "--title-prefix", "Foo",
                   "--id-prefix", "Bar"
                 ]
---
```

description:
Originally from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52972948/rstudio-is-changing-my-default-r-notebook-output

---

Given this document:

`````

  html_document:
    df_print: paged
---

Let's compare the sort methods on a set of shuffled integers.

```{r}
library(microbenchmark)
n <- 10L
output <- microbenchmark(
   sort(sample.int(n), method = 'radix'),
   sort(sample.int(n), method = 'quick'),

)

```

Rendering it gives an output with a paged table like e.g.

title: Export pandoc()
description:
I was wondering if you could export `pandoc()`.  There are a few pandoc commands that aren't covered by `pandoc_convert()` or `pandoc_version()` and would be nice to be able to run against the same version of pandoc **rmarkdown** is using. 

In my case I am calling `pandoc --print-default-data-file reference.pptx` to get the pandoc's internal template, which could be different places depending on the system and if the user has placed a template in their pandoc data directory. I'm currently doing so with a `getFromNamespace()` hack:

```
#' @importFrom utils getFromNamespace
get_default_pandoc_pptx <- function(outfile = tempfile(fileext = ".pptx")) {
  sys::exec_wait(getFromNamespace("pandoc", "rmarkdown")(),
    args = c("--print-default-data-file", "reference.pptx"),
    std_out = outfile)
  return(outfile)
}
```

title: Critic markup
Feeding a list to the `envir` argument of `render`
description:
Feeding a list to the `envir` argument of `render` triggers a behavior that I find counter intuitive.

I laid out the issue on SO : https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52724682/use-rmarkdownrender-in-a-restricted-environment

It has confused me enough to spend an afternoon debugging (mostly looking at the wrong places obviously :) ) and have a top poster write and retract a long post so even if it's not a bug I believe the documentation would benefit from a mention of this use case.

As the use of a proper list (as opposed to environment) as the `envir` parameter is undocumented, I suggest creating a feature and changing the behavior so that feeding `render(envir = my_list,...)` is equivalent to `render(envir = list2env(my_list, parent.frame())`.

An alternative would to have the environment just before the base packages in the search path and then the `Rmd` would need to contain the library calls or use the `::` notation.

title: Passing greek letters as colnames to kable.
description:
I've been trying to name an R data frame columns with greek letters in order to call kable and get a latex output table with header names as these greek letters.
The result is that kable does not recognise column names as the way latex greek letters are written, or the arguments are not passing to the function in the correct format.

```{r}
A <- t(as.data.frame(seq(1:4)))
colnames(A) <- c("$\\\\alpha$", "$\\\\beta$", "$\\\\delta$", "$\\\\gamma$")
A %>%
  kable(.,"latex", escape = F, booktabs = T, linesep = "", align = "c")
```

Is there a way to do this propperly?

The best solution I,ve found so far is set column names of the data frame to NULL, and write the table headers form the knit options as follows:

```{r}
A <- t(as.data.frame(seq(1:4)))
colnames(A) <- NULL
A %>%
  kable(., "latex", escape = F, booktabs = T, linesep = "", align = "c") %>% 
  add_header_above(c("$\\\\alpha$", "$\\\\beta$", "$\\\\delta$", "$\\\\gamma$"))
```
But this way is quite messy and lacks of automation.

Finally I tried the following and it doesn't work too.
```{r}
A <- t(as.data.frame(seq(1:4)))
A %>%
  kable(., "latex", escape = F, booktabs = T, linesep = "", align = "c", col.names = c("$\alpha$", "$\beta$", "$\delta$", "$\gamma$"))
```

title: Add support for color table & font table manipulation in rtf_document
description:
I'm adding RTF support to the huxtable package, which prints out formatted tables. RTF documents have a per-document font table and color table; fonts and colors in the table itself are indexes into these. 

I'd like to be able to manipulate the font and color tables, so that e.g. if someone has a purple table background with Comic Sans text, that data can be put into them. There's some infrastructure for this in `rtf_fc_tables` at https://github.com/hughjonesd/huxtable/blob/master/R/rtf.R .

Would you guys be open to this? If so, I could try to submit a pull request.

title: Trouble rendering word document with style from shiny server
description:
I have been having trouble rendering a word docx file using a `reference_docx` style document on shiny server. The file renders but the style is not applied.

Curiously, the file and the style render as expected when the shiny app is run from rstudio server on the same machine. Plus I have tested a reprex on another machine and could not reproduce the error. 

I have created a [gihub repo](https://github.com/mrjoh3/reprex-shiny-rmd-docx) with a minimum example. I will include the shiny app code below.

The shiny server (open source) is version `Shiny Server v1.5.3.838" "Node.js v6.10.0` and is running on `Ubuntu 16.04.1`.  and I have updated the `shiny` and `rmarkdown` packages. 

The rmd and docx files are copied to a temp folder for rendering and I have ensured that the user permissions are and have ensured that the user permissions are `chmod 1777 /tmp`.

A similar issue was flagged on the [rstudio community forum](https://community.rstudio.com/t/generating-downloadable-reports-rmarkdown-reference-docx-yaml-header-is-not-read-by-knitr/3308), but the suggestions made there did not resolve the issue.My question there was moved [here](https://community.rstudio.com/t/issues-generating-downloadable-reports-from-shiny-server-word-document/14655),  @jcheng5 requested I submit an issue here with a reprex. All required files are in the [github repo](https://github.com/mrjoh3/reprex-shiny-rmd-docx), the `app.R` and `.Rmd` files are copied below. The `.docx` template file is [here](https://github.com/mrjoh3/reprex-shiny-rmd-docx/blob/984cc998709de6f08d55bb8321319d7bcd9d1f8d/photo_log_template.docx). 

please advise if more details are required.

## The app.R file 

```r
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(rmarkdown)
library(DT)
library(jsonlite)
library(hashids)


cat("Doing application setup\n")

onStop(function() {

  cat("Removing Temporary Files and Folders\n")
  unlink(temp_folder, recursive=TRUE)

})

temp_folder <<- file.path(tempdir(),
                          hashids::encode(as.integer(Sys.time()),
                                          hashid_settings(salt='fews', min_length = 6))
)

dir.create(temp_folder)

ui <- shinyUI(fluidRow(
  column(10,
        h2('Data Output'),
        DT::DTOutput("images"),
        downloadButton("report", "Generate report",
                       style="color: #fff; background-color: #337ab7; border-color: #2e6da4")
        )
  )
)

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

    dat <- reactiveValues(images = data_frame("photographer" = c('A','B'),
                                              "organisation" = 'The Org',
                                              "location" = 'The Place',
                                              "address" = c('2 some place', '3 that place'))
    )

    output$images <- DT::renderDT(dat$images,
                                  server = FALSE,
                                  rownames = FALSE,
                                  class = 'dt-body nowrap',
                                  selection = 'single', editable = TRUE,
                                  extensions = c('Buttons','Responsive'),
                                  options = list(pageLength = 5,
                                                 dom = 'Blfrtip',
                                                 buttons = c('csv', 'excel')))

    output$report <- downloadHandler(

      filename = "Photo_Log.docx",
      content = function(file) {

        tempReport <<- file.path(temp_folder, "report.Rmd")
        tempTemplate <<- file.path(temp_folder, "photo_log_template.docx")
        file.copy("report.Rmd", tempReport, overwrite = TRUE)
        file.copy("photo_log_template.docx", tempTemplate, overwrite = TRUE)

        params <- list(organisation = input$select_org,
                       photographer = input$select_user,
                       df = select(dat$images,
                                   `Premises / Location` = location,
                                   Address = address)
                       )

        rmarkdown::render(tempReport, 'word_document',
                          output_file = file,
                          params = params,
                          envir = new.env(parent = globalenv())
        )
      }
    )

})

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: Nested list indentation doesn't match Pandoc Markdown documentation
description:
I have noticed that the [Pandoc Markdown's nested list documentation](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#block-content-in-list-items) linked from the [rmarkdown website](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/lesson-8.html) does not match the actual behaviour of rmarkdown.

In the Pandoc documentation, it is said that two spaces are enough for nested lists. The [RMarkdown cheatsheet](https://www.rstudio.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/rmarkdown-cheatsheet-2.0.pdf) is not specific, the ["Markdown Basics" page](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_basics.html) says 4 spaces.

Is this an issue with Pandoc's documentation itself and should be reported there?

A different version of the Pandoc documentation, on Garrett Grolemund's website, uses the 4-space indentation (but also lists the tab option, which doesn't work): https://garrettgman.github.io/rmarkdown/authoring_pandoc_markdown.html#lists
It looks like this one was forked in 2016, so it's all very confusing to me...

Here is some Rmd to test it (you might have to replace the indentation with an actual tab in the tab line):

````
---
title: "indented-lists"
output: html_document
---

## Indented lists

Using `rmarkdown` version 1.10 and latest GitHub dev version (1.10.13):

* A list starts like this
     + Four spaces: works

* A list starts like this
  + Tab: does not work

* A list starts like this
  + Two spaces: does not work
````

---
**Edit**: the current cheatsheet does not specify how many spaces are needed, except for a line return inside a list (4 spaces).

title: markdown output for Jekyll sites should protect liquid tags
description:
I sought help for this problem on SO with no success:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52299423/how-to-prevent-urlencoding-of-liquid-tags

The working example I posted on SO is:
````
---
output: md_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_knit$set(base.url = '{{ site.baseurl }}/')
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = 'assets/images/')
```

```{r sin_plot}
plot(1:100, sin(1:100))
```
````

The `base.url` setting inserts the liquid tag into the figure's path in the Markdown document, and rmarkdown::render does that just fine ... but then comes pandoc. When rmarkdown::render calls pandoc on the knit document, the braces are urlencode, breaking Jekyll.

A SO user suggested I've got my pipeline confused, but I can't see a better way that would still allow folks on my team using RStudio + RMarkdown write posts their preferred way. The site is and will remain a Jekyll site hosted on GitHub pages.

If there is a YAML heading param that disables pandoc, that would probably solve the problem, but I cannot find one.
