title: Specific case when render() can't parse source code
description:
In https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex/issues/202, @kevinushey found a circumstance under which `render()` fails to parse source code . Specifically, if you try to render the following piece of code, you'll get a failure to parse error (see reproducible example below for error details):

```r
code <- "
#' hello, world!"
```

From what I can tell, `#'` must be the leading characters on the second line of the `code` string for this error to occur. For example, if you remove `#` you won't get an error, and if you add a few spaces before `#'` you also won't get an error. 

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(rmarkdown)

render_one <- function(src) {
  file <- "to-render.R"
  writeLines(src, file)
  render(file)
}

# doesn't work:

src_no_work <- "code <- \"
#' hello, world!\""
render_one(src_no_work)
#> Quitting from lines 3-4 (to-render.spin.Rmd)
#> Error in parse(text = x, srcfile = src) :
#>  <text>:1:9: unexpected INCOMPLETE_STRING
#> 1: code <- "
#>            ^


# ...but these all work:

# no ' after #
src1 <- "code <- \"
# hello, world!\""

# no # before '
src2 <- "code <- \"
' hello, world!\""

# #' is at the start of the first line of the string, not the second line
src3 <-"code <- \"#' hello, world!\""

# leading spaces come before #'
src4 <-"code <- \"
  #' hello, world!\""

lapply(c(src1, src2, src3, src4), render_one)
```

title: Remove quotes around metadata fields in pandoc args
description:
If providing a metadata field to `pandoc_args`, the resulting command includes quotation marks which I'm *pretty sure* is what's making pandoc ignore it.

But when I add `"-M nocite='@*'"` to `pandoc_args` or to `config$pandoc$args` e.g.:

title: Filtering admin docs to create custom recipes
description:
In order to run R in production, it's important that IT/Ops departments have recipes (i.e. scripts) that describe how to install and configure R and RStudio. But IT/Ops doesn't know R and they don't invest much time reading our admin guides, so often these scripts do not get written. Furthermore, the admin guides have many sections that don't apply to individual customers. If IT departments had an easier way to grok our admin guide by focusing only on the sections that mattered to them, they would be able to write a recipe that was specific to their needs.

Today's admin guide is a bookdown document made up of 9 R Markdown docs. I would like an easy way to filter only the sections I choose and produce a new document specific to my interests. This filtered document will then be used to create recipes for installing and configuring RStudio.

title: Suggested Improvement to documentation for knit_hooks
description:
Can I suggest the following change to the documentation for knit_hooks - it incorporates your answer to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28268584/trying-to-set-knitr-document-output-hook-results-in-code-chunk-line-breaks-bei **Output hooks** ... All these hooks should be of the form function(x, options) (except the inline and document hooks which only have one argument x), where x is the character string of the output, and options is a list of current chunk options. Output hooks can be set as follows (this adds extra html formatting to any error messages). ```r knitr::knit_hooks$set(error = function(x, options){ paste('\n\n
', gsub('##', '\n', gsub('^##\ Error', '**Error**', x)), '
', sep = '\n') }) ``` Hooks can be chained together with ```r knitr::knit_hooks$append(error = function(x, options){ "Additional actions" }) ``` Unlike chunk hooks which are empty by default, output hooks all come with default values which can be reset with: ```r knitr::knit_hooks$restore() ``` Output hooks should be set inside the document. If the hooks are set before `knitr::knit()` processes the document run then `render_xxxx()` must be called first, where *xxxx* is the output format eg `render_markdown()` or `render_html()` - see below. ...etc knitr is a great package, which I use everyday, so thank you for creating it.

title: missing pagetitle if title is not supplied
description:
#1355 introduced a bug where if the `pagetitle` is supplied and `title` is not supplied, the title of the document is now the name of the document, not the `pagetitle` value.

Example header in `my_document.md`:
```yaml
---
pagetitle: "my title"
---
```

Currently produces an html document with a title of `"my_document.md"`

(Top of the) resulting \LaTeX file : 
```
\documentclass[french,a4paper,twoside]{article}

\usepackage{amssymb,amsmath}
\usepackage{ifxetex,ifluatex}
\usepackage{fixltx2e} % provides \textsubscript
\ifnum 0\ifxetex 1\fi\ifluatex 1\fi=0 % if pdftex
  \usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
  \usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
\else % if luatex or xelatex

  \else

title: Resources with a space in name are not copied when using runtime: shiny
description:
Including a .css file via YAML header and runtime: shiny does not work when the **filename of the .Rmd contains a space**.

After ages of searching for the bug of why I cannot include external .css file and breaking it down to the lowest level (I swapped around between files and with and without runtime: shiny without any other code except for the YAML header), I realised that it works when I remove the space I had in the `.Rmd` file. So instead of `x y.Rmd` I had to rename it to `xy.Rmd` and now it works.

Long story short, the following code only works when the filename of the `.Rmd` document does not contain a space character and I think it would be good to add this functionality because I do not think it's obvious for users that they have to use filenames that do not include any spaces.

```
---
runtime: shiny
title: 'My Title'
output: 
  html_document:
    css: www/style.css
---
```

title: Issue with addition of automatic section-id for headers
description:
Something that was discussed a few years back and closed a year ago in this thread #133 seems to be a problem for me again: When including any r-shiny-code, RMarkdown wraps a span around it, e.g.: `Germany` RMarkdown doesn't realise this however, and assigns the ID of the header wrong, resulting in the following: ```html
-df" class="section level1">

title: Figure labels in latex not generated unless `fig.align` is set
description:
Summary - unsure if knitr or rmarkdown problem, but I do not get figure labels unless I set the `fig.align` or `out.width` option explicitly somewhere.

MWE

~~~
---
# MWE - first figure gets no \label but second does.
title: "Test"
output:
  pdf_document:
    fig_caption: true
    keep_tex: true
---

```{r setup, include=F}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=F)
library(ggplot2)
```

A test document.

```{r asdf, fig.cap="A plot"}
ggplot(iris, aes(x=Sepal.Length, y=Petal.Width)) + geom_point()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.align='center')
```

```{r fdas, fig.cap="The same plot"}
ggplot(iris, aes(x=Sepal.Length, y=Petal.Width)) + geom_point()
```
~~~

Relevant output of the tex file produced by `rmarkdown::render('test.rmd')`

~~~
\begin{document}
\maketitle

A test document.

\begin{figure}
\centering
\includegraphics{test_files/figure-latex/asdf-1.pdf}
\caption{A plot}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}

{\centering \includegraphics{test_files/figure-latex/fdas-1} 

}

\caption{The same plot}\label{fig:fdas}
\end{figure}


\end{document}
~~~

Note how the first figure does not get a `\label{fig:asdf}` while the second figure does get a `\label{fig:fdas}`; if I remove the line

~~~
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.align='center')
~~~

then both figures do not get a label. I also tried changing `fig.align='center'` to `out.width='0.8\\textwidth'` and this produced a label for the second figure; but setting say `fig.width=8` did *not* produce a label for the second figure.

Must one of `fig.align` or `out.width` (presumably `out.height` and possibly other options) be set in order to get labelled figures? It is not obvious that this should be the case.

title: knitr::include_graphics generates HTML instead of markdown code (for local JPEG images)
description:
I need the markdown output of an R Markdown file to convert it with pandoc manually. But when I use `knitr::include_graphics` to include local JPEG images and knit to HTML with `keep_md` (or to markdown), these JPEG images are embedded in HTML code instead of markdown code. This does not happen when I embed PNG, SVG or PDF images with `knitr::include_graphics`, nor when the path to the JPEG image is a URL. Embedding the same image with normal markdown syntax (`![caption](file.jpg)`) works as intended. On the other hand, in the temporary `$FILENAME.knit.md` generated when knitting to Word, all images are embedded correctly (in markdown). When knitting to HTML or markdown, local JPEG images are embedded in HTML in the temporary markdown file. When knitting to PDF, the same images are embedded in LaTeX code (while the rest are in markdown). This bug might be related to the one that forced me to convert markdown output from knitr manually with pandoc in the first place: #1338. Labels for cross-referencing are included in most examples below, but as the minimal example without caption or reference shows, they are independent from this bug. This problem with `include_graphics` and local JPEG files is fairly recent. The person I'm helping ran into it after updating their R packages, but I don't know from which versions. I can reproduce it with the newest packages installed. Attempted fixes that did not work: * rename the file from .jpg to .jpeg * use absolute local path to file: `C:/` etc. * use `file://` for local path (not accepted by pandoc) * not using opts_chunk `results='asis'` (which is necessary for cross-references to work The only fix I can think of is to grap the temporary markdown file when knitting to Word, but the original document is much more complex than this MWE and it would entail other limitations, e.g. with `include_before`. Also, that would be the second time I have to hack my way around a problem because because of a bug, not a missing feature, in rmarkdown/knitr, MWE: --- output: html_document: df_print: paged keep_md: yes md_document: variant: markdown pdf_document: keep_tex: yes word_document: default --- ```{r, echo = FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,results='asis') ``` ```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Works: Code chunk, JPEG image, https:// file path"} knitr::include_graphics("https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Lichtenstein.jpg/487px-Lichtenstein.jpg") cat("{#fig:1st_reference}") ``` Markdown output: ``` ![Works: Code chunk, JPEG image, https:// file path](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Lichtenstein.jpg/487px-Lichtenstein.jpg){#fig:1st_reference} ``` ```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Does not work: Code chunk, JPEG image, relative local file path"} knitr::include_graphics("Lichtenstein.jpg") cat("{#fig:2nd_reference}") ``` Markdown output: ```

For bug reports, please provide a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example by reducing your example as much as possible right before the problem goes away. By doing this, you may be able to figure out what the problem really is before reporting to us. You can attach your example as a zip file here along with `devtools::session_info('rmarkdown')`, and screenshots are often very helpful to illustrate your issues.

Please do install and test the development version here before you report a bug:

```r
devtools::install_github("rstudio/rmarkdown")
```

To include a verbatim chunk of arbitrary text, wrap it in a pair of three backticks. When any line of your text contains N backticks (N >= 3), use N + 1 backticks to wrap the text, e.g. use four backticks to wrap three:

````
---
title: Hello World
output: html_document
---

A sample document.

```{r}
1 + 1  # a line of code
```

Another paragraph.
````

If it is just a chunk of R code (or other languages) and you want syntax highlighting, you may use three backticks to format it, e.g.

rnorm(10)

title: Bibliography not rendered if given in YAML other than main header
description:
My package includes a function to programmatically build and render an RMarkdown file, including a bibliography.

If I place the `bibliography: ` parameter in the main YAML header of the document, it renders correctly (see 
[rmarkdown_bib_header_test.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/files/2065823/rmarkdown_bib_header_test.zip) for .R, .Rmd, and .bib files for this examples).

### Renders correctly:
```r
rmarkdown::render("bib_in_header.rmd")
```

However, if I place the `bibliography: ` parameter in a YAML block outside of the main header, rmarkdown doesn't pick this up and does not render the citations or bibliography.

### .bib file isn't found:
```r
rmarkdown::render("bib_not_in_header.rmd")
```

Other YAML metadata doesn't seem to behave like this (e.g., `nocite`, `csl`, and even `title` can all be placed in other YAML blocks and work correctly), so this seems like a bug. It would be really helpful if rmarkdown could be adjusted to accept `bibliography: ` metadata given outside the main header, as that would make it easier for users of my package to place the output of this function inside larger RMarkdown documents.

description:
Hi,

I've noticed some unexpected interplay between the different methods of customizing the document preamble in PDF documents. `header-includes` and `includes: in_header` both work individually, but when I use both `header-includes` appears to be ignored:

~~~yaml
---
title: "Untitled"
output: 
  pdf_document:
    keep_tex: true
    includes:
      in_header: preamble.tex

header-includes:
  - \usepackage{booktabs}
---
~~~

`preamble.tex` could for example simply contain

~~~tex
\usepackage{tabulary}
~~~

However, once I include the additional `extra_dependencies` everything is included.

~~~yaml
---
title: "Untitled"
output: 
  pdf_document:
    keep_tex: true
    extra_dependencies:
      - tabularx
    includes:
      in_header: preamble.tex

header-includes:
  - \usepackage{booktabs}
---
~~~

Is this intended behavior? To me it would be useful and less confusing if these three approaches could be used independently of one another.

title: two bibliography entries fails
description:
Originally filed under `rticles` package, but appears to be a `rmarkdown` issue: https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/657

I have two valid bibtex files, which build fine with a vignette with YAML header like:
```
bibliography:
  - one.bib
  - two.bib
```

`pkgdown` will only build the corresponding article if _either_ of the bib files is present, but fails with pandoc-citepro error 83 when both are present, stating that one.bib is not found if both are present.

Concatenating one.bib and two.bib into all.bib makes it work fine. Could this be related to #658, in that if only one YAML entry is expected, the YAML is misinterpreted.

title: Apply theme when using vignette builder
description:
I'm writing a vignette for [my package](https://github.com/naturalis/nbaR) and want to specify a theme and some settings like toc, etc. 
If I build the vignette with ```rmarkdown::render```, everything works and the theme is applied to the vignette:

```rmarkdown::render("vignettes/nbaR.Rmd")```

However, when I want to use the vignette builder specified in my package, the theme is not rendered, e.g. with 

```R CMD build . && R CMD INSTALL nbaR_0.0.0.tar.gz```

or with

```devtools::install_github("naturalis/nbaR", build_vignettes=T)```

so I guess `rmarkdown::render` is not used when building the vignette. In my `DESCRIPTION`, I have

```VignetteBuilder: knitr```

[Here the related question on SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50394988/rmarkdown-theme-not-applied-in-vignette-using-r-cmd-build)

How can I make the theme render when using e.g. ```install_github```? Many thanks in advance!

title: Two slides generated if knitr chunk outputs a plot in powerpoint_presentation
description:
When creating a simple plot using a knitr chunk like the following: 

```
    ```{r, cars, echo=TRUE}
    plot(cars)
    ```
```

The code output is always placed on one slide and the plot output on the following slide. This happens regardless of whether or not you use ```---``` beforehand. 

This only appears to happen when the knitr chunk output is a plot. For example, in the case of...

```
    ## Dinner

    - Eat spaghetti
    - Drink wine `r 2 + 2`

    ```{r, math}
    2 + 2
    ```
```

`r 2 + 2` will output the inline text correctly and the code and output of `math` also output to the same slide. It seems that only plots generated inside a code chunk show this behavior.  In other words, I can't seem to generate a plot on the same slide where I have text, nor can I keep the code (`echo=TRUE`) on the same slide.

title: Vertical space in place of float in PDF output
description:
When having a plot or image between two parts of text in a *.Rmd file, the generated LaTeX file for PDF output will have a blank lines before and after the figure environment storing this float.
Therefore, if LaTeX's algorithms move the figure to the top or bottom of the page, there will be a space between the 2 paragraphs, which looks strange and is not intended.
It would be great, if the LaTeX's `figure` environment would not be surrounded by blank lines, because then there wouldn't be the vertical space between the two parts of text.  
Those who want could still enter a blank line between the parts of the text to have it also in the PDF file in the end.

Minimal example:

    ---
    output: pdf_document
    ---
    
    This is my first paragraph. 
    Next in the Rmd file would be the code for the figure.  
    The figure is correctly treated as a float by LaTeX, meaning that LaTeX will put it to the next suitable position.
    ```{r pressure, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Example", out.width='0.5\\textwidth', fig.pos='B'}
      plot(pressure)
    ```
    The problem now is, that this leaves space to my second paragraph.
    Usually, this should not be the case.
    In pure LaTeX, there is a linebreak, of course, but no vertical space in addition.

title: [Feature request:] Implement an easy way to add attributes (e.g. labels for cross-referencing) to figures embedded with code chunks
description:
There is no easy way add attributes (e.g. labels for cross-referencing) to figures embedded with code chunks to get an output like this: `![Caption](file.ext){#fig:label}`

(This is needed for cross-referencing with [pandoc-crossref](https://github.com/lierdakil/pandoc-crossref), for example.)

The state-of-the-art way of doing this in rmarkdown [appears](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37116632/rmarkdown-html-number-figures) to be "to `cat` the figure label (in the form of `{#fig:figure_label}`) after each plot, although this requires `echo=FALSE` and `results='asis'`."

This is quite cumbersome and as of now doesn't even work properly with PDF output (cf. #1338).

title: *.utf8.md output of code chunk differs between formats (and breaks stuff)
description:
The `*.utf8.md` code for HTML and PDF output differs for the following code chunk:

`````
```{r fig.cap="Figure caption.", results='asis', echo = F}
image(volcano, col = viridis(200))
cat("{#fig:label}")
```
`````

I don't know the workings of the rmarkdown package well enough to narrow down the problem any more. Intuitively I would have thought the temporary `*.utf8.md` file, which pandoc converts to whatever format chosen, would be identical for all formats. But it's not.

The `*.uft8.md` for HTML output has

```{markdown}
![Figure caption.](1-example_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){#fig:label}
```

(and everything is fine). But the PDF output has a space before the `cat()`/label element:

```{markdown}
![Figure caption.](1-example_files/figure-latex/unnamed-chunk-2-1.pdf) {#fig:label}
```

Pandoc converts this to:

```{latex}
\includegraphics{1-example_files/figure-latex/unnamed-chunk-2-1.pdf}
\{\#fig:label\}
```

By manually parsing instead the first (HTML-output) `*.utf8.md` with pandoc, the `.tex` output is as intended.

## Reproducible example

````
---
title: "*.utf8.md output of code chunk differs between formats"
output:
  pdf_document:
    keep_tex: yes
  html_document:
    keep_md: yes
---

```{r include = FALSE}
library(viridis)
```

The `*.utf8.md` code for HTML and PDF output differs for the following figure:

```{r fig.cap="Figure caption.", results='asis', echo = F}
image(volcano, col = viridis(200))
cat("{#fig:label}")
```
````

title: Add support for Font Awesome 5?
description:
Beginning with v5.0.11, Font Awesome includes an icon for R (!!) (see [here](https://fontawesome.com/icons/r)). 

As of v1.9, RMarkdown automatically bundles Font Awesome v4.5. Given that Font Awesome 5 has been out for a few months now and is stable, it would be nice to have support for it in RMarkdown (perhaps as an option in `_site.yml` or in YAML frontmatter in individual Rmd files, like `font-awesome: 4` or `font-awesome: 5`)

title: Data.frames/tibbles not output as paged in RMarkdown after upgrading to R 3.5.0
description:
Since upgrading to R 3.5.0, there appears to be an issue with inline display and rendering to html of data.frames/tibbles when using R Notebooks - they are not rendered as paged tables, *unless* it is a grouped tibble (and for now, grouping a tibble by any variable before displaying seems to solve the problem).

Reproducible example including the results of the rendering (and written how it appears inline in RStudio):

https://rpubs.com/Granholm/384010

This happens *only* in R Notebooks, and adding `df_print: paged` to the header does not solve it:
````
---
title: "R Notebook"
output:
  html_notebook:
    df_print: paged
---
````

When knitting a regular RMarkdown document to html with the header shown below, all the three examples in the above link are rendered as paged tables and are all displayed correctly inline in RStudio (inline, the data.frame and tibble are displayed as in the console and the grouped tibble is displayed as a paged table).

````
---
title: "R Notebook"
output:
  html_document:
    df_print: paged
---
````

This appears to be present in both the most recent version of the rmarkdown package from CRAN and also the dev version from GitHub.

More people have been mentioning the issue in the RStudio Community forums:
https://community.rstudio.com/t/issues-with-r-markdown-notebook-in-r-3-5-0-not-displaying-tibble-df-nicely-inline/7651

https://community.rstudio.com/t/kable-results-not-displaying-inline/7828/4

I don't know if this is mostly an issue related to rmarkdown or knitr, so feel free to redirect me and close this issue if better suited elsewhere.

title: R Markdown Websites no longer work with non `html_document` formats
description:
R Markdown Websites were originally designed to work with any HTML based format (so long as it supports the site_libs and self_contained options). However, a recent change intended to address this issue (https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/793) has broken this:

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/pull/1177

So now the feature which originally supported any HTML based format can only work with html_document.

The original issue #793 is certainly also a legitimate use case (rendering PDFs alongside HTML documents) but this particular fix is too drastic, so I think should be reverted in preference to another fix (PR to follow with the revert, I'm not at all sure what the alternate fix should be, perhaps instantiating the output format and checking it's formals before forwarding on those parameters?).

title: Implicit dependency on config.yml not detected
description:
### Repro

First, create the following R Markdown document and save it as `config.Rmd`.

    ---
    title: "Config"
    output: html_document
    ---
    
    ```{r}
    config::get()
    ```

Next, add a `config.yml` file in the same folder.

Finally, run the following at the R console:

    rmarkdown::find_external_resources("~/rmd/config.Rmd")

### Expected result

The `config.yml` file should be returned.

### Actual result

No results are returned.

The `get()` function accepts a config filename. If this filename is specified explicitly, as in:

    config::get("foo.yml")

then the string-based filename finder will find it. However, because we only skim R strings for filenames, a filename supplied in a default argument value won't be discovered.

This ordinarily wouldn't be a big deal (and we probably don't need to worry about it for most arguments), but it's significant in this instance because `find_external_resources` is used to ascertain the set of files that need to be published, and `config.yml` is an important dependency.

title: R Markdown websites share same environment when using `render_site()`?
description:
This may be a bug, but it also might be the intended behavior for R Markdown. This comes from [an issue I posted on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49930372/use-new-environments-for-each-knitted-file-in-an-r-markdown-website). The reason I think it might be a bug is that when `blogdown` and `bookdown` compile a bunch of Rmd files, each one gets its own new environment, while `rmarkdown::render_site()` seems(?) to use one shared environment for all the Rmd files when knitting, which causes unexpected namespace issues.

For example, using this minimum working example with the following 5 files:

**testing.Rproj**

    Version: 1.0

    RestoreWorkspace: Default
    SaveWorkspace: Default
    AlwaysSaveHistory: Default

    EnableCodeIndexing: Yes
    UseSpacesForTab: Yes
    NumSpacesForTab: 2
    Encoding: UTF-8

    RnwWeave: Sweave
    LaTeX: pdfLaTeX

    AutoAppendNewline: Yes

    BuildType: Website


**\_site.yml**

    name: "testing"
    navbar:
      title: "Testing"
      left:
        - text: "Home"
          href: index.html
        - text: "Step 1"
          href: 01_something.html
        - text: "Step 2"
          href: 02_something-else.html

**index.Rmd**

    ---
    title: "Testing"
    ---

    Hello, Website!

**01_something.Rmd**

    ---
    title: "Step 1"
    ---

    Write some data just for fun.

    ```{r}
    library(tidyverse)
    library(here)

    write_csv(mtcars, file.path(here(), "cars.csv"))
    ```

**02_something-else.Rmd**

    ---
    title: "Step 2"
    ---

    This breaks because `lubridate::here()` and `here::here()` conflict, but *only* when rendering the whole site.

    ```{r}
    library(tidyverse)
    library(lubridate)
    library(here)

    # Do something with lubridate
    my_date <- ymd("2018-04-19")

    # Try to use here() and it breaks when rendering the whole site
    # It works just fine when knitting this file on its own, though, since here is loaded after lubridate
    cars <- read_csv(file.path(here(), "cars.csv"))
    ```


Both `here` and `lubridate` have a `here()` function, and because I want to use `lubridate`'s throughout the script in `02_something-else.Rmd`, I run `library(here)` after `library(lubridate)`. Running `02_something-else.Rmd` interactively or knitting it by itself works just fine—package loading happens in the right order and everything's great.

However, when building the site with `rmarkdown::render_site()` (from the console, from the "Build" button in RStudio, or from the terminal with `Rscript -e "rmarkdown::render_site())"`) there's an error when R gets to `02_something-else.Rmd`:

    Error: '2018-04-19 14:53:59/cars.csv' does not exist in current working directory

Instead of using `here::here()`, R is using `lubridate::here()` and inserting the current date and time, since `library(here)` was originally loaded in `01_something.Rmd` and that environment seems to still be loaded when R gets to `02_something-else.Rmd`.

According to [the documentation for `rmarkdown::render_site()`](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/rmarkdown/versions/1.9/topics/render_site), you can use the `envir = new.env()` argument to ensure that the site rendering uses a new environment, but that doesn't fix the problem. It seems that guarantees a new environment for the overall site building process, but not for the individual files.

Is there a way to ensure that *each individual file* in an R Markdown website gets its own new environment when knitted?

For now I've fixed the issue by prefixing all my lubridate functions with `lubridate::`, but this can cause more complicated namespace issues later on. For instance, `dplyr::filter()` and `MASS::filter()` commonly conflict with each other. If I use MASS in one file in the site, it would mess up code in all the files that come after, but I wouldn't realize it until I build the whole website.

`blogdown` and `bookdown` don't have this issue—it seems to be limited to just R Markdown websites. Perhaps this is by design, but I don't know.

---

output:
  github_document:
    toc: yes
---

# test2.

However, the `.` isn't always replaced by a '-'. If you use the header `test. test`, the correct link is `test_toc.md#test-test`.

title: render() fails to delete intermediate tex file if called from non-input working directory
description:
`render()` fails to delete the intermediate tex file (when `keep_tex = FALSE`) if it is called from a working directory which is different from that of the `input`.  It appears that there is a pseudo-race condition:

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/8cfc8783636b37876a6dc929dac2395df080e7ac/R/render.R#L154

is called before

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/8cfc8783636b37876a6dc929dac2395df080e7ac/R/render.R#L671

So by the time the exit hook evaluates `unlink(texfile)`, the working directory has already been changed back.

title: Problems with absolute paths in plots under LaTeX (Windows)
description:
Hi Yihui,

well, me again, I got into trouble with the handling of the rmardown generated plots in LaTeX.

As you might now, we are using Rmarkdown for a little Project with many writes on different operating systems. So our scripts have to run under Windows and *nix systems. But there is a little problem with the handling of plots.

I've made a short example, with is include in this bug report, but I will explain it  first:

Our directory structure is like this:

```
+-content/
!   +-child.Rmd
+-images/
!  +-rmarkdowrn.png
+-build/
+-MainTestDocument.Rmd
+-Makefile.R
```

We use the Makefile.R to build MainTestDocument.Rmd as MTDocument.pdf (as a beamer presentation) in the build/ directory.

We got no problem with including images, like rmarkdown in the images/ directory, because they will include with a relative path. 

But all plots will have a absolute path, with causes Windows system to get in trouble because of the absolute path part to the main document directory. 

We got something like

```tex
\includegraphics{C:\path\to\main\document\dirctory/path/to/generated/images.png}
```

On *nix systems it'll be:
```tex
\includegraphics{/path/to/main/document/dirctory/path/to/generated/images.png}
```

which is also not nice, but will do it. But it would be much nice to have only relative paths or correct paths on windows systems.

Thank in advance,
Norman

BTW: If I use the kntir-button in RStudio it works fine.

[yihui-test.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/files/1828445/yihui-test.zip)

title: Output cache directory can collide on multiuser systems
description:
(Reported by a Shiny Server Pro customer in Zendesk ticket 25396)

On some (most?) Linux setups, R's temp directories look like `/tmp/RtmpXXXXXX`. When caching output, rmarkdown creates temp directories that walk one level up from there and then back down: `/tmp/rmarkdown/YYYYYY` (where `YYYYYY` is a hash of the .Rmd file path and its mtime). When used in a multiuser system, whomever is first to create that `/tmp/rmarkdown` directory will own it and almost certainly set `0700` permissions on it by default. This prevents any other users from being able to create their own output cache directories.

To fix, add the username in between: `/tmp/jcheng/rmarkdown`, for example.

title: [Bug] Rstudio freezes when first time creating new RMarkdown files when the computer is in a closed network
description:
I am working under company network which blocks the CRAN R mirrors. When I tried to create a new RMarkdown file, R freezes, because it needed to install two extra packages, and it cannot establish a link to any of the mirrors. However, even when the warning about connection pops up, it kept being frozen. It's only when I connected to external network did it finally installed the required packages and start.

I think this counts as a bug as it's really hard to understand what's going on for novice users. I would like to suggest putting all the required packages for Rstudio to create RMarkdown files in the requirement for installing the `rmarkdown` package, or stop Rstudio from attempting to connect to a CRAN R mirror when the connection times out.

title: pre-rendered Shiny Rmd documents should have a cache invalidation mechanism
description:
This is an issue that has come up in discussion before (in fact the title is verbatim stolen from @yihui 's comment in https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1213#issuecomment-349420987). I have now bumped into it again because, with the latest `rmarkdown` version now on CRAN, I was testing `learnr` (using the tutorials in the repo's `examples` directory) and hitting the same obscure error:

![repro](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6527540/37159004-a0b78d7e-22e4-11e8-983c-044597ddcce4.png)

This turned out to be another "highlight.js 1.1" issue since I still had the .html files and other artifacts from previous rendered versions of the shiny pre-rendered  Rmd file. I think that the reason that https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/commit/6eb75a031a0a6977e4731697c098c66b208c72de was not enough is because there's also a call to `normalizePath(directoryPath, mustWork=TRUE)` in shiny that tries to fetch the highlight.js dependency. (From the shiny side, we could wrap this call in a `tryCatch` and provide a better error message than the result above.)

In any case, like in #1213, the issue is fixed by deleting the html file and re-rendering from scratch. However, this revives the problem of missing a cache invalidation mechanism and is, in the end, to be expected, as @jjallaire put it (https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1213#issuecomment-349421582):

>Yes, Winston that all stems for the cache invalidation.
>
>@yihui You are absolutely right that they need a cache invalidation mechanism or we will continue to see this sort of thing periodically.

Also, in that same issue, @jcheng5 sketched out a possible solution: see https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1213#issuecomment-350376918.

title: Problems with file.rename in 1.9.-1.9.2
description:
Hi folks,

the new code in 1.9(.2) in render.R, namely this one here:

```
    if (output_format$pandoc$keep_tex || knitr::is_latex_output()) {
      # do not use pandoc-citeproc if needs to build bibliography
      convert(texfile, run_citeproc && !need_bibtex)
      # unless the output file has the extension .tex, we assume it is PDF
      if (!grepl('[.]tex$', output_file)) {
        latexmk(texfile, output_format$pandoc$latex_engine, '--biblatex' %in% output_format$pandoc$args)
        file.rename(file_with_ext(texfile, "pdf"), output_file)
        # clean up the tex file if necessary
        if (!output_format$pandoc$keep_tex) on.exit(unlink(texfile), add = TRUE)
      }
    } else {
      convert(output_file, run_citeproc)
    }
```

make much trouble to me. You can't always rename a pdf document created bei latexmk with `file.rename(file_with_ext(textile, "pdf"), output_file)` and you should not do it!

If you use latexmk on a tex file (say demo.tex), and it produces pdf (demo.pdf) and output_file ist also demo.pdf, why renaming it do (demo.pdf). - If you try, this will cause trouble:

```
Fehler in tools::file_path_as_absolute(output_file) : 
  file '[...]/build/Datenerhebung-Statistik-Duesseldorf-DOZENTENVERSION.pdf' does not exist
Zusätzlich: Warnmeldungen:
1: In file.rename(file_with_ext(texfile, "pdf"), output_file) :
  kann Datei '[...]/build/Datenerhebung-Statistik-Duesseldorf-DOZENTENVERSION.pdf' nicht in '[...]/build/Datenerhebung-Statistik-Duesseldorf-DOZENTENVERSION.pdf' umbenennen. Grund 'No such file or directory' 
```

The main reason is:  '[...]/build/Datenerhebung-Statistik-Duesseldorf-DOZENTENVERSION.pdf' does exists by `latexmk` and so before `file.rename` is called!

I think you only should use `file.rename` here when `file_with_ext(textile, "pdf") != output_file`. - Or do I miss something?

Yours
Norman

title: Latest rmarkdown won't find any local *.sty files in base/main directory
description:
Hi folks,

after upgrading markdown and use tinytex I found a serious bug, I think it is one. Because I'm not sure where it needs to be fixed, I also filed a bug issue at [tinytex](https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/issues/22) .

Normally you may have a main directory in which your, lets say, test.Rmd files is. Let us guess you make a pdf (with keep_tex=true) out of it. You also uses a latex style file, name it mystyle.sty which is also in the main directory. You might render it, no problems.

BUT: If you use the latest rmarkdown and tinytex AND use an output_directory different from the main directory, you got into trouble!

I the old day, a temporary tex and pdf file was build in the main directory and moved after that into the output_directory, everything went well.
But now, it seems that you build the tex file first in the output_directory and rund latexmk (r something) on it in that directory, which is worse. Because the latex sty-files would not be in the search path of latex any more.
This is extremely annoying where you use your own beamer theme files (which are .sty files).

What might help as a quick bugfix is: Add the main directory to TEXINPUTS environment variable of the shell you use before starting any latexmk word. Something like "setenv TEXINPUTS ..:" or appropriate.

There is probably a much better solution, than my workaround... copying all tex and sty files to the output_directory is none!

Yours
Norman

title: slide-level for powerpoint_presentation
description:

Pandoc 2.1.1 has a very useful slide-level parameter for slide presentations. But currently this is not part of the powerpoint_presentation stuff inside rmarkdown.. So a YAMl part like

output:

    slide-level: 2
---

```
---
output:
powerpoint_presentation:
  pandoc_args:
    - --slide-level
    - 2
---
```

which also shows, that it is a known parameter by the pandoc powerpoint presentation writer.
I think it would be nice, if someone would fix it in the next release. - Thanks, and keep on going the good work!

title: data.frame / tibble printout for code chunks not showing grouping
description:
When a data frame or tibble is grouped with `dplyr`s  `group_by` function and printed out to the console, e.g.
```
data("mtcars")
mtcars %>% group_by(cyl)
```
The user gets information about the grouping, which helps to reduce errors produced by forgetting about a grouping done earlier, like this:
```
# A tibble: 32 x 11
# Groups:   cyl [3]
```
However, there is currently no way to produce this information about the grouping when displaying the data frames as chunk output in Rmd-Notebooks. This information might not be relevant for the final report created with `knitr`, but I do believe that this information would benefit the exploratory workflow when using notebooks and there should be a way to enable it documentwide.

Keep up the good work :)
Jannik

title: markup
description:
For general questions, please ask them on StackOverflow first, using the tags `r` and `rmarkdown` (other possibly relevant tags include `knitr`, `html`, `css`, and `latex`): http://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask Please come back here only if nobody answers your question there, and let us know the URL of your StackOverflow post. It is a better idea to use the wisdom of the community first.

For bug reports, please provide a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example by reducing your example as much as possible right before the problem goes away. By doing this, you may be able to figure out what the problem really is before reporting to us. You can attach your example as a zip file here along with `devtools::session_info('rmarkdown')`, and screenshots are often very helpful to illustrate your issues.

Please do install and test the development version here before you report a bug:

```r
devtools::install_github("rstudio/rmarkdown")
```

To include a verbatim chunk of arbitrary text, wrap it in a pair of three backticks. When any line of your text contains N backticks (N >= 3), use N + 1 backticks to wrap the text, e.g. use four backticks to wrap three:

````
---
title: Hello World
output: html_document
---

A sample document.

```{r}
1 + 1  # a line of code
```

Another paragraph.
````

If it is just a chunk of R code (or other languages) and you want syntax highlighting, you may use three backticks to format it, e.g.

```r
rnorm(10)
```

title: find_external_resources errs with variable chunk eval
description:
This test document was trimmed from a much larger one. It shows that a variable used to allow / prohibit the evaluation of a chunk produces an error (which appears to be ignored).

````
---
output: html_document
---

```{r setup,echo=FALSE}
hasNotes <- FALSE
```

Here is some text in a document.

```{r echo = FALSE, results = 'asis', eval = hasNotes}
cat("**We have notes!**\n")
```
````


Run the following in the R console:
```
rmarkdown::find_external_resources("error.Rmd")
```

Here's the output:
```
Error in eval(x, envir = envir) : object 'hasNotes' not found
[1] path     explicit web     
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
```

The `find_external_resources` function is used by `rsconnect` to discover files referenced by an Rmd that need to be included in a deployment bundle:
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/def0d46c806588af4b3c45853489eb997c97158d/R/deployDoc.R#L54

We don't really want to execute the document when analyzing it for resources. I was surprised to see this error about `hasNotes`. The `find_external_resources` function is supposed to be making "best effort" to identify resources. 

I do not know if this error is preventing resource discovery; it appears to be working fine. The error in my deploy console made me question it.

title: relax self-contained requirement for GitHub documents?
description:
Currently, the HTML previews generated for GitHub documents are generated with `--self-contained`, as per:

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/561b812d249c65e5031418b5e10ab1986bc9eecd/R/github_document.R#L61-L69

However, this can fail when attempting to preview documents that request external web resources, if that resource is inaccessible for some reason (no internet; old version of pandoc that doesn't handle `https://`; etc).

Is it worth relaxing the standalone requirement in this case, so that document previews can still be viewed?

I think if we take away `--self-contained` we also need to do a bit of extra work to ensure that the GitHub CSS is injected into the template by hand, as without `--self-contained` `pandoc` won't do that work for us.

cc: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1922

title: Feature Request: Permission Dependencies
description:
Our team is having a hard time assessing which pieces of the (Red Hat Linux) file structure a user needs access to in order to use the markdown document. It would be great if knit created an R object with the filepaths accessed upon successful completion. This way the creator would know the permissions required by the consumers.

We are currently having individuals open the same .Rmd file because RConnect won't let us publish markdown documents that reference the drivers needed to connect to SQL. However, upon completion (we are seeing warnings that are only created on successful completion), the users are being told they do not have access to the document that is created.

title: Allow sql-code-chunk-results to be collected and stored in an R object
description:
Using sql-code-chunks in a `.Rmd` is very convenient. It has nice syntax highlighting and we don't need any R functions around the sql code. Like the following:

    ```{sql connection=con}
    SELECT * 
    FROM my_table
    ```

However, as far as I know, it does not allow for pulling the query result into your R session to further analyse the data locally. This calls for the following code

    ```{r}
    my_table_in_r <-
      odbc::dbGetQuery(
      con,
      "SELECT *
       FROM my_table") %>%
      dplyr::collect()
    ```
In this silly example the sql code is still reasonably clear. However, as the query gets more complicated this can get quite messy, as it is in a character string with no sql syntax highlighting. Also you have to be careful with single and double quotes within the code, since the sql code is within one of them.

It would be super awesome if the result from a sql-chunk could be stored in an R object right away. Maybe by specifying the desired object name in the chunk argument like

    ```{sql connection=con, r_obj=my_table_in_r}
    SELECT * 
    FROM my_table
    ```
I have no idea if this is feasible, but it woud make me very happy!

title: Feature Request: Parameters for templates
description:
#1233 suggests a need for parameters for rmarkdown templates, and I am curious to discuss what such a feature might look like.  I imagine something like:

```
rmarkdown::draft("/path/to/folder", "html_vignette", 
        "rmarkdown", create_dir = FALSE, edit = FALSE
        , template_param = list("package"="mypackagename"))
```

Which would replace something like:

````
```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
library(template_param$package)
```
````

with something like:
````
```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
library(mypackagename)
```
````

Features to consider:
- syntax for replacement within a Rmd.  Would this simply be utilization of rmarkdown parameters?  Or would this be a "higher level" that is replaced on draft creation (I lean towards the latter)
- Ability to define a default value within the `template.yaml`
- Ability to define values within `rmarkdown::draft` (and elsewhere?)
- Plug-in to the UI that allows defining types, values, etc.
- It's not clear to me whether this should use R syntax or some other template syntax for replacement (i.e. `{{TEMPLATEPARAM}}`)

Happy to discuss!

title: How to display inline images in notebook viewer?
description:
The magick pkg has a [`knit_print` method](https://github.com/ropensci/magick/blob/master/R/base.R#L111-L118) which calls `knitr::include_graphics()` to automatically display images when rendering an rmarkdown document.

This works great via `knitr::knit()` or `rmarkdown::render()` however the `knit_print` method gets [ignored when knitting inside rmarkdown notebooks](https://github.com/ropensci/magick/issues/102). Is there an alternative hook or method to display inline images in the rmarkdown notebook IDE? cc @jmcphers

title: how to store embedded file (includes) in custom Rmarkdown
description:
This problem was previously posted on [stackoverflow.com](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47456968/how-to-store-embedded-file-includes-in-custom-rmarkdown).

I created my own format in Rmarkdown based on this blogpost. I implemented it in my personal package and it works great. I also added custom files in includes argument of html_document.

My question is whether it's possible to store my custom files (included in includes argument) after I click Knit button. Similarly to self_contained = F option which allows storing all Rmarkdown dependencies.

I should give you some context first. Let’s say I used my html format to create a report two months ago. Two weeks later I decided to implement major changes in my html format and updated my package.

After next two weeks, my boss came to me asking for adding minor changes in old report. Then, by clicking Knit button, the report was not able to create, because there was a new version of my html format, which was significantly different.

I see three possibilities how to deal with this request. Either I can install old version of my package (suboptimal), create a new html format every time I implement major changes or I can store my dependencies (header, footer, css files) in a separate subdirectory (like a packrat). Then each report would be independent and immune to changes in my custom format.

Let me know if there is any better solution.

--

H1b

output:

github toc

title: Pandoc 2.0 breaking all `runtime: shiny` docs
description:
When trying to find a minimal repro for https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/issues/158, I found that all `runtime: shiny` Rmd documents do not play well with Pandoc 2.0. It seems that ANY `runtime: shiny` document is vulnerable and that this bug manifests whenever the author interacts with `input` or `output`. At first, I thought this was a consequence of some weird state my Mac got in after everything I've put it through with Pandoc, but I reproduced the exact same bug in another computer (Microsoft) in a completely different (and much cleaner) environment...

It seems that Pandoc 2.0 is fundamentally not playing well with Shiny. I'm not sure where this problem resides. I only know it's not just `flexdashboard`. @yihui, @jcheng5 

Here is the code (from http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/interactive-docs.html):

---
runtime: shiny
output: html_document
---

```{r echo = FALSE}
library(shiny)

selectInput("n_breaks", label = "Number of bins:",
  choices = c(10, 20, 35, 50), selected = 20)

sliderInput("bw_adjust", label = "Bandwidth adjustment:",
  min = 0.2, max = 2, value = 1, step = 0.2)

```{r echo = FALSE}
renderPlot({
  hist(faithful$eruptions, probability = TRUE, 
    breaks = as.numeric(input$n_breaks),

    main = "Geyser eruption duration")

})

title: build_site resource copying reads through symlinks
description:
Given a site containing a symlink:

```
touch index.Rmd
touch _site.yml
ln -s ~/lunch.txt .
```

Rendering this site creates a `_site` directory with the contents of `lunch.txt`, not the symlink.

```
rmarkdown::render_site()
```

```
$ ls _site
index.html lunch.txt  site_libs
```

Comparing the two files:
```
$ ls -l lunch.txt _site/lunch.txt
-rw-r--r--  1 aron  staff  86 Oct 25 19:53 _site/lunch.txt
lrwxr-xr-x  1 aron  staff  21 Oct 25 19:50 lunch.txt -> /Users/aron/lunch.txt
```

I discovered this when investigating an issue with rmarkdown prior to the fix for #946 - we were copying the whole `packrat/lib` tree and also reading through symlinks. The packrat tree was pointing to cached package contents; reading through symlinks copied the package contents into the `_site` directory.

Maybe this doesn't deserve fixing, but I wanted to at least file the issue to record the behavior.

description:

``` r
#' ---
#' output:
#'   md_document:
#'     pandoc_args: [
#'       '-t', 'commonmark'
#'     ]
#' ---

plot(runif(1:3))
```

If you name it `foo.R`, you can use RStudio's html preview on the resulting `foo.md`, which includes the plot like so:

```
![](foo_files/figure-markdown_strict/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png "fig:")
```

If you name it something much longer, the html preview does not work because a hard line break has been introduced into the image syntax:

```
![](fooabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_files/figure-markdown_strict/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png
"fig:")
```

You get this pandoc error:

Error: pandoc document conversion failed with error 67
```

even though the file does exist.

To pre-emptively answer the question "why are you requesting CommonMark?", see #1148, i.e. it's related to [GitHub's adoption of CommonMark](https://github.com/blog/2333-a-formal-spec-for-github-flavored-markdown). If I use `output: github_document` this line break problem goes away, but then I have other problems.

title: Throw warning/error when using `output: html_notebook` and `runtime: shiny`
description:
## Overview
When using `output: html_notebook` **and** `runtime: shiny`, the normal code chunk evaluation sometimes occurs and sometimes doesn't. This is what happens locally. However, if the app is deployed (at least to Connect and shinyapps.io), you _never_ have code chunk evaluation. (The embedded Shiny app always works.)

@jcheng5 and I talked about how this is confusing and it may be better to either implement `runtime: shiny` for notebooks, or always warn/error if a user has both `output: html_notebook` and `runtime: shiny`. Currently, there is no warning or message that indicates that this is unsupported/undefined behavior. And since there's so much similarity between `html_document` and `html_notebook` (from a user's perspective), it isn't clear that this is unsupported. 

The repro code is below, along with screenshots of both cases and the output of `devtools::session_info('rmarkdown')`. I couldn't really figure out if the runs when the code evaluation works vs the ones it doesn't are deterministic, but they appear random. The closest to reproducibility that I got to is that it usually starts off working, then it stops (though it may resume working again in future runs) and a good way to get it to work is to close and reopen the file...

## Repro
````r
---
title: "R Notebook"
runtime: shiny
output: html_notebook
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(shiny)
```

### Normal chunk evaluation
Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. It never works when it's deployed.
```{r}
head(mtcars, 3)
```

---

### Shiny App Example
Always works.
```{r, echo=FALSE}
ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput('n', 'Number of obs', 200),
  plotOutput('plot')
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    hist(runif(input$n))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Object not found error associated with render() using intermediates_dir argument
description:
My use case: an R script, say driver.R, that calls `rmarkdown::render()` to render an .Rmd file into either pdf or html. I execute the driver by using `source("driver.R")`.

I want to conditionally execute chunks depending on whether certain conditions are true in the data, so within one chunk certain Booleans are defined, and later chunks use `eval` along with those Booleans to determine whether the chunk should be evaluated.

When I output to html_document or pdf_document, I get the following error, _but only when supplying an_ `intermediates_dir` _argument_.

```
Error in eval(x, envir = envir) : object 'runChunk1' not found
Error in eval(x, envir = envir) : object 'runChunk2' not found
```

It looks like some function called by`render()` to handle `intermediates_dir` scans the Rmd and looks at the `eval` arguments. But since it's not executing code in the chunks, the objects in later `eval` arguments are not found.

As far as MWE, here's a driver:

```
library(rmarkdown)

rmarkdown::render("process.Rmd",
  output_format="html_document",
  envir = topenv(),
  output_dir = "output_dir",

title: No blank lines created after HTML tags, which breaks CommonMark rendering
description:
Using `rmarkdown::render(..., output_format = "md_document")` causes any HTML tags to not have blank lines after them, even if they do in the source. This in turn means that according to CommonMark specs, the following lines will not be rendered as markdown. Example: This Rmd source ```

foo

**bar** ``` Generates this md output ```

foo

**bar** ``` (I'm doing this so that I can add an `id` attribute to the tag). This is undesirable because bar would no longer be rendered as bold, but instead it will just show the two asterisks. There should be a blank line before `**bar**` Reference: http://spec.commonmark.org/0.28/#html-blocks Proof of how this looks broken on github: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/952340/30890890-ae7acb7c-a2fd-11e7-8063-b582e5e1aeef.png)

title: pandoc_args behaves different for HTML and PDF
description:
When I used

~~~
output:
  pdf_document:
   pandoc_args: [
     "--data-dir", "_pandoc",
     "--template", "apa6.tex",
     "--output", "apa6.pdf"
   ]

on the YAML header of my document and run Knit, the log shows

~~~
usr/lib/rstudio/bin/pandoc/pandoc +RTS -K512m -RTS paper.utf8.md --to latex --from markdown+autolink_bare_uris+ascii_identifiers+tex_math_single_backslash --output paper.pdf --template /home/raniere/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.4/rmarkdown/rmd/latex/default-1.17.0.2.tex --highlight-style tango --latex-engine pdflatex --variable graphics=yes --data-dir _pandoc --template apa6.tex --output apa6.pdf --variable 'geometry:margin=1in'

Note that my `--template` option is after the default one which means that Pandoc is going to use the option that I provided.

When I used

~~~

      "--data-dir", "_pandoc",

title: default to svglite for html outputs
description:
Would it be possible to default to `dev = 'svglite'` for HTML documents?

Plots via `svglite` in HTML output just look so much better, and this would be one less thing for the average user to think about, set up (which, of course, can be done already). Upstream tools such as `bookdown` could also inherit this default behavior.

On the downside, `svglite` would be another dependency (and also has system dependencies via `gdtools`, I think).

Perhaps `rmarkdown` could default to `"svglite"` whenever `require("svglite")`, and else to `"png"`, that way, `rmarkdown` would always produce something.

Or would that be too clever by half?

Would be happy to put together a PR to this effect, but I'm not knowledgeable enough to judge whether this would be a good idea to begin with.

title: With shiny_prerendered, unhelpful error message when directory is not writable
description:
In deployment scenarios, it's not uncommon for users to have the wrong owner or permissions for their directories. With a `shiny_prerendered` doc, when the target directory isn't writable, it gives this unhelpful message:

```
> rmarkdown::run("test.Rmd", render_args = list(output_dir="/"))
Error in file(con, "r") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In normalizePath(path, winslash = winslash, mustWork = mustWork) :
  path[1]="//test.html": No such file or directory
2: In file(con, "r") :
  cannot open file '//test.html': No such file or directory
```

rstudio/learnr#112 is an example of this. The error message didn't help at all for diagnosing the problem.

I think the culprit is that when the directory isn't writable, it assumes that the prerendering doesn't need to happen, that the prerendered file already exists:
  https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/6def14c/R/shiny_prerendered.R#L79-L81

When it gets to this line, it expects the prerendered file to exist, but it doesn't, raising a warning. Later on it tries to read the file and errors out.
  https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/6def14c/R/shiny_prerendered.R#L131

I think the solution is to check if the file exists above line 131 and error if it's not there. Does that seem reasonable? I just want to make sure that I'm not overlooking some use case here.

How to reproduce: create a new Rmarkdown Slidy presentation with the following content: ``` ## Title This is rendered as paragraph: $$ \exp\left(-\sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i \log p_i\right) $$ This is not: \begin{align*} \exp\left(-\sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i \log p_i\right) \end{align*} Test: $$ x+y+z $$ ``` Then knit to HTML. When previewing the slide, the first and third paragraphs (with $$...$$ display math) has some left indentation, but the second paragraph (with \begin{align*}...\end{align*} display math) doesn't. Looking at the generated HTML source it seems that this is because the second paragraph is missing the enclosing `

` and `

` tags: ```

Title

This is rendered as paragraph: \[ \exp\left(-\sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i \log p_i\right) \]

This is not: \[\begin{align*} \exp\left(-\sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i \log p_i\right) \end{align*}\]

Test: \[ x+y+z \]

``` It's quite minor but visually bothersome. The `align*` environment is occasionally necessary for e.g. multiple equations.

title: Insert html plotly files to an rmarkdown html report
description:
Hi,

Suppose I created several figures, both `ggplot2` `png` figures and `plotly` `html` figures:
```

library(plotly)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

p <- plot_ly(z = volcano, type = "heatmap")
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(p,"p.html")

df <- reshape2::melt(volcano)
d <- ggplot(df,aes(value))+geom_histogram()
ggsave(d,filename = "d.png")

s <- ggplot(df,aes(x=Var1,y=Var2))+geom_point()
ggsave(s,filename = "s.png")

```

My `rmarkdown` code then tries to insert them:

```{r.setup, include=FALSE,echo=FALSE}
library(knitr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,out.width='1000px',dpi=200,fig.keep="all")
options(width = 1000)
options(knitr.table.format = "html")
```

```
---
title: "test"
output: html_document
---
```

```{r insert.ggplot1, echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("d.png")
```

```{r insert.plotly, echo=FALSE}
htmltools::includeHTML("p.html")
```

```{r insert.ggplot2, echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("s.png")
```


In the output `html` page I only see the `p.html` figure taking over the entire page rather than appearing between `d.png` and `s.png`.

So my question is what's the proper way to insert an `html` figure.

In addition, suppose I generated and saved a list of `plotly` figures, outside the `rmarkdown` code, for example:

```
for(i in 1:3){
  pi <- plot_ly(z = volcano, type = "heatmap")
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(pi,paste0("p.",i,".html"))
}

```

and I'd like to loop over them and insert them in the `rmarkdown` code. I know that if I'd generated them in the `rmarkdown` code I'd use `htmltools::tagList`, something like this:


```
plot.list <- vector(mode="list",3)
for(i in 1:3) plot.list[[i]] <- plot_ly(z = volcano, type = "heatmap")
htmltools::tagList(plot.list)

```

But I don't know how to import them. Any idea how to handle that?

title: Use keywords variable to include keyword list after abstract in PDF / LaTeX output
description:
When making PDF outputs, the list of provided keywords is included as PDF metadata but not displayed in the visible output. It would be good if they could be included (and perhaps even better if there were a setting to include / suppress them as desired).

Loosely following [this SO post](https://stackoverflow.com/a/38024787/4957167), I think that including keywords can be achieved by adding to each of the the tex templates in here...:

`rmarkdown/inst/rmd/latex/`

...a block of code list this...:

```
\newcommand*{\keywords}[1]{\textbf{\textit{Keywords---}} #1}
$if(keywords)$
    \keywords{$keywords$}
$endif$
```

...probably just after the abstract conditional block:

```
$if(abstract)$
\begin{abstract}
$abstract$
\end{abstract}
$endif$
```

I guess more would be required to make this conditional on some (YAML?) parameter.

Users can currently approximate this by making a copy of the default template (say, in their working directory) and editing it to include the above code block. One potential downside of that approach is that it might get out of sync with future upgrades to the default templates. But more immediately noticeable was that when using the 'Knit' button in RStudio, there seems to be different behaviour when a template is specified, compared to when not. Specifically, when no template is specified, I think Pandoc is called with these options, which are missing when a template is specified:

`--variable graphics=yes --variable "geometry:margin=1in"`

It took me a while to find out why my margins got all wide when I was switching to a copy of the same template. For anyone else hitting that, the solution that worked for me was to add an extra YAML line:

`geometry: "margin=1in"`

title: issues running code in chunks in vignettes since updating to RStudio 1.1
description:
Hello. Since updating to RStudio 1.1, some of the behaviour of code chunks in vignettes has changed. 

Within a code chunk in a vignette, pressing Cmd+Enter on a line in a chunk no longer runs it (similarly pressing Cmd+Enter from anywhere in a pipe). It only runs if highlighted first.

Also, typing the name of a data frame followed by the pipe operator then Enter no longer automatically indents the next line. 

Both of those behaviours still happen in R scripts, and in other .Rmd documents, just not in vignettes. The output doesn't seem to make a difference (I've tried rmarkdown::html_vignette, rmarkdown::html_document and bookdown::html_document2).

Removing the lines
```
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Vignette Title}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
```
from the yaml fixes the issue, but of course creates the issue of then not building the vignette! I'm using devtools::use_vignettes() to generate the vignette template.

I'm running RStudio 1.1.336, R 3.4.1, rmarkdown 1.6, knitr 1.16, macOS 10.12.5

title: Feature Request: Dropdown Options in Tabsets
description:
For tabsets created in an HTML document by rmarkdown, tabs are by default displayed horizontally, like so: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19809917/29225403-2caf0f0c-7e9c-11e7-8395-c96d96cf5680.png) However, with a little bit of tweaking of the HTML, you can turn the tabset into a dropdown menu: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19809917/29225450-530d37c8-7e9c-11e7-9380-aac7ea726306.png) Instead of having to tweak the HTML after Pandoc produces the HTML file, would it be possible to use rmarkdown to specify a dropdown layout? Perhaps the result could look something like this? ```markdown # Choose a Tab {.tabset .tabset-fade .tabset-dropdown} ## First Tab Here is the first tab's content. ## Second Tab Here is the second tab's content ``` For reference, the rmarkdown for this example is as follows: ```markdown --- title: "Tabset Example" output: html_document --- # The Tabset Section {.tabset .tabset-fade} ## First Tab Here is the first tab's content. ## Second Tab Here is the second tab's content ``` And the HTML produced for the tabset is this: ```html
  • First Tab
  • Second Tab
``` which can be replaced by the following HTML to produce a dropdown menu: ```html
  • Choose a Tab
    • First Tab
    • Second Tab
```

title: BibTeX error when `citation_package` is set for documents without citations
description:
Hi,
I've run into the following issue when attempting to build a PDF document with a format function which uses `citation_package = "natbib"`. 

**test.Rmd**
```markdown
---
title: "natbib issue"
author: "Andrzej Oleś"
output: function(...) output_format(NULL, NULL, base_format=pdf_document(..., citation_package="natbib"))
---

Test file to illustrate `citation_package` argument issue.
```
The PDF builds, but BibTeX gives an error.
```r
render("test.Rmd")
```
```
This is BibTeX, Version 0.99d (TeX Live 2013/dev)
The top-level auxiliary file: test.aux
The style file: plainnat.bst
I found no \citation commands---while reading file test.aux
I found no \bibdata command---while reading file test.aux
(There were 2 error messages)
```

In particular, this issue affects all of the *rticles* formats which use natbib as their default `citation_package`.

I believe the problem is caused by the fact that even though there are no actual citations in the document, BibTeX is called in an attempt of resolving them. It seems that this could be addressed by including the pandoc argument `--natbib` only when there are any citations in the document, or at least when there is a `bibliography` defined in the document metadata header. What do you think?

Cheers,
Andrzej

title: load params to aid in unit testing
description:
Sometimes, when working with a parametrized report, it helps to have a copy of the params in the global environment to do unit testing.


I use a function for this, usually
<details>
<summary> get_yaml </summary>

```r
#' get the yaml of an Rmd file, requires yaml package
#'
#' @param file should be an Rmarkdown file
#'
#' @return a named list
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' params <- get_yaml('file_with_params.rmd')
get_yaml <- function(file) {
    require(yaml) || stop('the yaml package is required')
    z <- readLines(file)
    endpoints <- which(z == '---')[1:2]
    yaml_lines <- z[do.call(seq, list(endpoints[1] + 1, endpoints[2] - 1))]
    yaml::yaml.load(paste(yaml_lines, collapse = '\n'))
}

```
</details>



This works fine for standard parametrized reports. 


However, this generates a problem if I want to use nested params, which I prefer for organizational purposes. 

According to Issue #929 the proper way to do this is as follows:

```
params:
  date:
    value:
      min: '2017-08-01'
      max: '2017-08-03'
  people: ['Alice', 'Bob']
```

In the Rmarkdown environment, this will result in a nested list:

```
List of 2
 $ date  :List of 2
  ..$ min: chr "2017-08-01"
  ..$ max: chr "2017-08-03"
 $ people: chr [1:2] "Alice" "Bob"
```


however, if I read it in as standard yaml, I get this:
```
str(params)
List of 2
 $ date  :List of 1
  ..$ value:List of 2
  .. ..$ min: chr "2017-08-01"
  .. ..$ max: chr "2017-08-03"
 $ people: chr [1:2] "Alice" "Bob"
```

Is there an easy way for me to parse the params the way that the markdown will?
(I can probably just remove any line with just `value:`
but I'd rather not make assumptions about the yaml structure if I can)

title: Running rmarkdown from the command line without the need for X11 capability
description:
Hi there,

I'm trying to run an `Rmarkdown` script from the command line on my linux cluster, that will generate an html report, using this command:
`R -e "rmarkdown::render('script.Rmd',output_file='output.html')"`

I don't have `X11` installed on my cluster nodes which caused it to crash so the solution was to install `xvfb`, and I'm now running it with this command: 
`xvfb-run --server-args="-screen 0 1024x768x24 -noreset" R -e "rmarkdown::render('script.Rmd',output_file='output.html')"`

While it doesn't crash immediately anymore, `xvfb` has `RAM` usage issues, which I thought would be solved by adding the `-noreset` argument, but unfortunately that's not the case, and it still occasionally seq faults and crashes when it's out of `RAM`.

So my question is if there's an alternative way to solve this? Perhaps it is possible to build the `Rmarkdown` package without the dependence on X11?

Hi, I need to list all the bibliography entries from a .bib file, none of them are cited. I found that it can be done with `nocite` as following
```
---
nocite: | 
  @item1, @item2
...
```
However, there are a lot of entries. So how can I use something like `\nocite{*}` to list all the entries?
Besides, if I want to place the bibliographies somewhere else instead of the end of the document, what's the easiest way to do that?
Thanks a lot.

title: Application data file get deleted by clean=TRUE on render()
description:
The intermediates cleaning mecanism is deleting a datafile read by the program.

The Rmd:
[Test_LostFile.Rmd.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/files/1125122/Test_LostFile.Rmd.txt)

<details>
<summary>Rmd Code </summary>

````markdown
---
title: "Test_LostFile"
author: "plr"
date: "5 de julio de 2017"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(readr)

```


```{r }

file <- "../temp/LostFile.csv"

dfX <- data.frame( l=letters, n=1:length(letters))

write.csv(dfX, file, row.names = FALSE)

dfY <- read_delim( file
                         ,delim=","
                         ,col_names=TRUE
                         ,col_type= cols(
                            l = col_character()
                            ,n = col_double()
))

```
````
</details>

With this command line:

```
export R_LIBS="C:/Users/Me/Documents/R/win-library/3.4"; export LANGUAGE="en_US.utf8"; \
        time Rscript -e "rmarkdown::render('src/Test_LostFile.Rmd', output_file='Test_LostFile.html', clean = TRUE, run_pandoc=FALSE, output_dir='reps', intermediates_dir='tmp.xxx')"
```

Under cygwin on Win7.

## First run
On the first run the program works fine and throw this output ('cause run_pandoc=FALSE):

```
...
output file: C:/BitSync/INE/Ensayo2016/Adapt2Censo/tmp.xxx/Test_LostFile.knit.md

[1] "C:/BitSync/INE/Ensayo2016/Adapt2Censo/tmp.xxx/Test_LostFile.knit.md"
attr(,"knit_meta")
list()
attr(,"intermediates")
[1] "C:/BitSync/INE/Ensayo2016/Adapt2Censo/tmp.xxx/Test_LostFile.knit.md"
[2] "C:/BitSync/INE/Ensayo2016/Adapt2Censo/tmp.xxx/Test_LostFile.utf8.md"
[3] "C:\\BitSync\\INE\\Ensayo2016\\Adapt2Censo\\reps\\Test_LostFile_files"

$ ls -ltr temp/LostFile.csv
-rwx------+ 1 Me Domain Users 208 Jul  5 10:51 temp/LostFile.csv
```

## The second time:
output file: C:/BitSync/INE/Ensayo2016/Adapt2Censo/tmp.xxx/Test_LostFile.knit.md

```
[1] "C:/BitSync/INE/Ensayo2016/Adapt2Censo/tmp.xxx/Test_LostFile.knit.md"
attr(,"knit_meta")
list()
attr(,"intermediates")
[1] "C:/BitSync/INE/Ensayo2016/Adapt2Censo/tmp.xxx/Test_LostFile.knit.md"
[2] "C:/BitSync/INE/Ensayo2016/Adapt2Censo/tmp.xxx/Test_LostFile.utf8.md"
**[3] "C:/BitSync/INE/Ensayo2016/Adapt2Censo/tmp.xxx/../temp/LostFile.csv"**
[4] "C:\\BitSync\\INE\\Ensayo2016\\Adapt2Censo\\reps\\Test_LostFile_files"
```

And the file get lost:
$ ls -ltr temp/LostFile.csv
ls: cannot access 'temp/LostFile.csv': No such file or directory

The problem seems to be the the combination of the ways :
* Data path is formed from relative file inside the program
* Intermediate files are identified (anything that start with the temporary dir path?)

The work around was to use rprojroot package to form an absolute path relative to project base.
In this manner the misidentification of the file is avoided.

regards
- Pablo

title: Unable to pass custom function to df_print in YAML header
description:
Per the rmarkdown documentation, `df_print` can be passed an arbitrary function for printing. This works fine when passed directly to `render()`, but [`resolve_df_print()` inside `render()`](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/render.R#L819) is not set up to handle the names of arbitrary functions passed via YAML headers in .Rmd documents. Could a case be added to the `resolve_df_print()` function to check that the passed string from YAML:

- is a valid function name
- that function returns the right kind of output

and if so, set that function to `df_print`. Step two I would imagine is optional, depending on its difficulty to define vs how you want the user to see an error. Example code for step one below. Apologies, I'm not sufficiently well versed in R development and the rmarkdown package to suggest code step two.  

    else if (is.function(get(df_print)))
            df_print <- get(df_print)

Ideally I'd like to do this with an R Notebook, but per issue #964, `df_print` has no effect when rendering an HTML notebook, which is suboptimal. Why not make `paged_table_html_asis` the default for `df_print`, instead of the exclusive, hardcoded option? 

Thanks for all your work on a great package!

title: Feature Request: Hooks for knitting (particularly after-knit-hook)
description:
Hi
# Feature Request
Hook to run code after successful knitting.

# Motivation
in my workflow I run a notebook which renders several other notebooks and in this process imports data, checks the data, creates some summary graphs, etc. All these are rendert as html_documents (and other formats as well) and the root notebook is called index and contains links to the others so that I can access all as a website.
Now there are others involved in the project who are also interested in the report and I am sharing it on as a website by copying them over to a http server.
Everything works automated, but the last step, the copying of the directories containing the final outputs, is done automatically.

# Examples
1. run a script (R, sh, doesn't matter) in a hook which is executed when the document is successfully knitted / exported to automatically copy the directory containing the to the http server.

2. send an email containing the report automatically to others

title: --smart pandoc option not used for Word doc output
description:
R Markdown documentation says that the `--smart` flag for pandoc is enabled by default, and this seems to be the case when I output to HTML documents. However, when outputting to Word documents, this does not seem to be the case. In addition, I can't seem to find a way to tell rmarkdown to set that flag. I've tried `params = list("smart" = "yes")` as an argument to a manual call to `render()`, as well as the YAML headers

    output:
      word_document:
        smart: yes
        pandoc_args: [
          "--smart"
        ]

as well as those two YAML headers separately. Neither have any effect. I manually copied the pandoc command generated by `render()` and executed it myself with an added `--smart`, which worked fine, so clearly pandoc supports the smart flag for Word outputs.

title: Paged Dataframe Printing doesn't work in Rmarkdown

And if you try to include any of the options listed there, like this: ``` --- output: html_document: df_print: paged max.print: 1 --- ``` It just returns an error when you try to 'Knit': ``` Error in yaml::yaml.load(string, ...) : Scanner error: mapping values are not allowed in this context at line 4, column 16 Calls: ... parse_yaml_front_matter -> yaml_load_utf8 -> -> .Call Execution halted ``` Is there something I am missing?
