title: Bug in rmarkdown::render params
description:
Good day, 

first of all a big thank you to the developers. 
When using rmarkdown today I just encountered a potential bug in rmarkdown::render when trying to pass params. 
The following .Rmd file was directly knit'able in RStudio:

```
---
title: My Document
output: pdf_document
params:
 etfnumber: !r c(1:5)
---

```{r}
params$etfnumber[3] ```
```
However, when trying to execute the following code, an error occurred:

`rmarkdown::render("C:/Users/"USER"/Desktop/asdf.rmd", output_file = "asdf.pdf", 
                  encoding = "UTF-8", params = list("etfnumber" = params$etfnumber))`

**Error in knit_params_get(input_lines, params) : object 'params' not found**

This counts for every subset of `params$etfnumber`, too.

The solution is to define params manually as follows.

`params = list("etfnumber" = c(1:5))`
`attr(params, 'class') = "knit_param_list"`

and then execute 

``rmarkdown::render("C:/Users/"USER"/Desktop/asdf.rmd", output_file = "asdf.pdf", 
                  encoding = "UTF-8", params = list("etfnumber" = params$etfnumber))``

title: html_notebook ignores global chunk options
description:
Global options are ignored when using the 'Preview notebook' engine.

Example:

    ---
    title: "Test"
    output:
      html_notebook: default
      html_document: default
    ---
    
    ```{r setup, echo=FALSE}     
    library(knitr)
    opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,results='hide',fig.keep='none')
    ```
    
    ```{r hidden}        
    1+1
    plot(1:5, 1:5)
    ```

The `html_document` renders only the title, with no output from the "hidden" chunk (as expected). However, in the `html_notebook` rendering the code, results, and figure are all shown. These have to be disabled individually for each chunk.

title: R Notebook removes blank lines from code chunks when eval=TRUE
description:
When previewing an R Notebook/knitting to .nb.html, code chunks that contain blank lines within the code (between lines of code, not leading or trailing whitespace) have those blank lines removed from the output, only when `eval=TRUE` (either explicitly or implicitly as the default). The blank lines are preserved when `eval=FALSE`, or when knitting to a HTML or PDF file (this only happens in an R Notebook). Should it not preserve the code formatting as is, or at least have an option to preserve these lines? I reviewed and tried several knitr chunk options that might be relevant to the code rendering, including `strip.white` and `tidy`; neither had any impact on this behavior. 

By way of example, this code chunk (`eval=TRUE`):

    ```{r CH-test, eval=TRUE}
    a <- c(1,2,3)
    b <- 4*a
    
    # leaving some space
    
    a
    ```

renders in the R Notebook as 

    a <- c(1,2,3)
    b <- 4*a
    # leaving some space
    a

while this chunk (`eval=FALSE`):

    ```{r CH-test, eval=FALSE}
    a <- c(1,2,3)
    b <- 4*a
    
    # leaving some space
    
    a
    ```

renders in the R Notebook as

    a <- c(1,2,3)
    b <- 4*a
    
    # leaving some space
    
    a

Using the default Theme and syntax highlighting style, RStudio version 1.0.143, `rmarkdown` package version 1.5, and `knitr` version 1.16.

title: Support CommonMark syntax for code chunks/fenced code blocks
description:

```r include=FALSE
x = 1+1
```
Is there any reason why the curly braces couldn't be made optional in R Markdown? It would be really nice if I could write valid R Markdown and also have code blocks be syntax highlighted when I open them in a text editor such as atom or vscode.

title: github_document(): headers with non-ASCII text don't work in TOC
description:
Given a document with contents like:

```
---
title: "Link test"
output:
    github_document:
        toc: true
        toc_depth: 3
---

## Datensätze
```

A Markdown file with contents like this is generated:

```
Link test
================

-   [Datensätze](#datensatze)

Datensätze
----------
```

However, because the link has been ASCII-ified while the actual title text has not, the link no longer works correctly when rendered by GitHub. It seems like there's two solutions here:

1. Add some attributes that explicitly declare the href / id on the actual title text,
2. Avoid ASCII-ifying in the TOC for `github_document()`.

title: asis_output overrides header-includes in .Rmd file
description:
(Moved over from yihui/knitr#1397)

In a .Rmd file, if you include a list of `rmarkdown::latex_dependency` objects in the `meta` argument to `asis_output`, this will override any `\usepackage` statements in the `header-includes` argument. See the attached mwe. This came up in hughjonesd/huxtable#7.

[knitr-bug-mwe.Rmd.zip](https://github.com/yihui/knitr/files/965951/knitr-bug-mwe.Rmd.zip)

A workaround is to use the `includes` argument to `pdf_document`.

The issue is that if a latex_dependency is present, pandoc is called with argument --include-in-header XXX, where XXX is a temporary file containing the stringified latex dependency. When this happens, it overrides the header-includes variable in the YAML front matter. 

I am trying to work out how to merge values from the command line and the YAML front matter, but I am not sure there is a way. In which case, one approach would be to take values from the YAML front matter and write them to the same file with the latex dependencies.

Another approach would be just to use `includes` - I get the impression that `header-includes` is a bit deprecated?

title: Add YAML option to disable Rmd download in html_notebook
description:
**Problem:** When sharing notebooks, there is sometimes confidential information stored in the code chunks. There is no way to disable this with the current format. While it is possible to hide them with `code_folding: hide` or `echo=FALSE` in the chunk, this is entirely visible when downloading the Rmd (which is embedded within the .nb.html output file).

**Workaround:** The author must be aware of the potential loss of confidentiality and externalise that from the notebook, possibly using `source` to pull in external scripts for example. This is tedious and I believe is outside the spirit of being able to maintain reproducible work with limited dependencies.

**Possible Solution:** Add a YAML option, such as `download_rmd`, the value could default `true` to maintain current behaviour, yet be set to `false` at the author's discretion.

title: Rmarkdown ignores fig.pos in code chunks
description:
Rmarkdown seems to be ignoring the figure position float placement specifier argument, `fig.pos`, in code chunks for LaTeX/PDF output.

Minimal working example:

``````r
---
output: pdf_document
---
Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.
```{r fig.cap = 'My caption', fig.pos = 'p'}
plot(1:10)
```
``````

The figure should appear on the next page but instead it appears on the same one.
Setting `keep_tex: true` reveals the following output.

```latex
\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\includegraphics{index_files/figure-latex/unnamed-chunk-1-1.pdf}
\caption{My caption}
\end{figure}
```

By contrast, the equivalent **knitr** R no-web (`.Rnw`) version of the MWE is:
```latex
\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.
<<fig.cap = 'My caption', fig.pos = 'p'>>=
plot(1:10)
@
\end{document}
```
which produces the correct output: (line breaks added for clarity)
```latex
\begin{figure}[p]
\includegraphics[width=\maxwidth]{figure/unnamed-chunk-1-1}
\caption[My caption]{My caption}
\label{fig:unnamed-chunk-1}
\end{figure}
```

I am using **rmarkdown** version 1.4 (the problem also occurs in version 1.3) and **pandoc** version 1.17.2.

The `htbp` specification appears to be the default when inserting a captioned image on its own line in Pandoc Markdown, i.e. `![My caption](image.png)` for pandoc 1.17.2 (the version bundled with RStudio).

I tried updating to pandoc 1.19.2.1 and the only difference appears to be that the default is `\begin{figure}` rather than `\begin{figure}[htbp]` --- settings in the chunk still have no effect.

Another user has reported this issue on [Stack Overflow](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/42486617/knitr-ignoring-fig-pos).

title: render() failing on windows when output_format="pdf_document" and output_dir path has underscore
description:
When render() called with output_format="pdf_document" and output_dir is a path with a directory starting with _ (underscore), the pdf cannot be made if the Rmd file is making figures. render() changes the figure path to use `\\` and if the path has `\\_` in it, this becomes `\_` in the intermediary md file. Latex cannot process a path with `\_` in it. Proposed solution: Change line 194 of render() to knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = normalize_path(figures_dir)) i.e. wrap figures_dir in normalize_path() Reproducible code of the error: Run on a Windows machine The tester1.Rmd file 
---
title: "Test"
output:
  html_document: default
  pdf_document: default
---

```{r plots}
plot(pressure)
```
Two testing directories each with the above file in it. C:/test C:/_test this code works on the directory with no leading underscore ``` setwd("C:/test") rmarkdown:::render("tester1.Rmd", output_format="pdf_document", output_dir="C:/test", clean=FALSE) ``` this does not work on the directory with a leading underscore ``` setwd("C:/_test") rmarkdown:::render("tester1.Rmd", output_format="pdf_document", output_dir="C:/_test", clean=FALSE) ``` Error is Could not find image `C:_test\tester1_files/figure-latex/plots-1.pdf` Here is the md file that is created in C:/_test for the above (tester1.knit.md) 
---
title: "Test"
output:
  html_document: default
  pdf_document: default
---

```r
plot(pressure)
```
![](C:\_test\tester1_files/figure-latex/plots-1.pdf)
Notice that render() changed the directory path to use a single `\` rather than a `/` as specified in the output_dir argument to render(). Latex cannot interpret a path with`\_` in it. So the intermediary md file cannot be processed. The path change occurs on line 139 of render() where `pandoc_path_arg(files_dir)` is called. This is where the directory path for the intermediary files changes from `C:/_test/tester1_files` to `C:\\_test\\tester1_files` Line 139 `files_dir <- pandoc_path_arg(files_dir)` Later on line 194 `knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = figures_dir)` Running knitr::opts_chunk$get()$fig.path we see the problem: ``` knitr::opts_chunk$get()$fig.path "C:\\_test\\tester1_files/figure-latex/" ``` Presumably knit() is somewhere processing `C:\\_test\\tester1_files` to `C:\_test\tester1_files` (which is how latex would convert the first to "text") and that is what is used for the figure path used in the intermediary md file. Possible solution: If line 194 were `knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = normalize_path(figures_dir))` It would work as the path would only have forward slashes. Note, Issue #235 indicates that "there are many instances where pandoc barfs when not presented with a path containing backslashes on Windows" . However, it does not seem that normalizing fig.path to unix style is a problem here. In fact the path that is currently specified by the call to opt_chunk$set(fig.path) on 194 is a mixture of `\\` and `/`.

title: TOC doesn't work with duplicate names and different capitalizations
description:
If there are duplicated section names at the same TOC level in the Rmd file, the TOC is properly indexed when rendering to HTML. However, if they differ in capitalization, the TOC does not index it properly (and you get sections with identical names in the HTML, which the TOC cannot handle).

# Rmarkdown section
# Rmarkdown section

# Rmarkdown section
# RMARKDOWN section

title: Allow 'pre_knit' hooks to return new file to be used for knit?
description:
Motivation: currently, HTML comments are not really properly handled by R Markdown or knitr. For example, with the following document:

    ---
    title: "Untitled"
    output: html_document
    ---

    <!--

    ```{r}
    print("Hello!")
    ```

    -->

Even though the R chunk below is within an HTML comment, that chunk still gets executed, and thus included and processed by Pandoc.

When rendering such a document in `html_document` mode, those comment markers survive, and so the generated output is not shown in the document, giving the user the impression that the commented chunk was ignored.

However, with `html_notebook`, we're not so lucky -- the closing comment tag is actually HTML-escaped, and so the comment never actually functions as expected -- we end up seeing the chunk output in the rendered document.

Correct me if I am wrong, but since the current experience is as though HTML comments in R Markdown documents are supported, we need to do something extra to ensure that this works for HTML notebooks.

My initial thought would be that the `pre_knit` hook could return a file path that would then be passed on to `knitr::knit()`, and that the `pre_knit` hook could be in charge of e.g. replacing comments with a placeholder (and later restoring the placeholders in e.g. a `post_process` hook). However, this is not currently possible because of how the `pre_knit` hooks are overlaid (the union of return values seems to be returned?)

Is this something that could be made possible?

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

## DT Test

```{r echo=FALSE}
library(DT)

n <- 1000
nGroup <- 100

testDF <- data.frame(text=paste0("Section", 1:n),
                     number=1:n,
                     group=rep(1:(n/nGroup), n/nGroup))

datatable(head(testDF), caption="Whole table", rownames=FALSE, escape=FALSE, options=list(paging=FALSE, info=FALSE))

getDT<-function(x) {
  a <- list()
  a[[1]] <- htmltools::tags$h3("test1")
  a[[2]] <- datatable(x[, c("text", "number")], caption=htmltools::tags$caption(style="caption-side: top; text-align: left;", "Group: ", htmltools::strong(x$group)), rownames=FALSE, escape=FALSE, filter=c("none"), options=list(paging=FALSE, info=FALSE))
  a[[3]] <- htmltools::tags$h4("test1")
  
  return(a)
}

res <- lapply(split(testDF, testDF$group), getDT)

htmltools::tagList(res)

title: Plot missing in HTML
description:
I've been working on a HTML document with Rmarkdown.

The document has several sp plots and ggplots and all of them appear in the HTML.

But when I call plotK (which is a function from stpp package to plot the spatio-temporal inhomogeneous k-funtion - STIKhat), the plot doesnt appear in the HTML.

Here's a reproducible example for Rmarkdown:

````
---
title: "Untitled"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
library(stpp)
data(fmd)
data(northcumbria)
FMD<-as.3dpoints(fmd[,1]/1000,fmd[,2]/1000,fmd[,3])
Northcumbria=northcumbria/1000
# estimation of the temporal intensity
Mt<-density(FMD[,3],n=1000)
mut<-Mt$y[findInterval(FMD[,3],Mt$x)]*dim(FMD)[1]
# estimation of the spatial intensity
h<-mse2d(as.points(FMD[,1:2]), Northcumbria, nsmse=50, range=4)
h<-h$h[which.min(h$mse)]
Ms<-kernel2d(as.points(FMD[,1:2]), Northcumbria, h, nx=5000, ny=5000)
atx<-findInterval(x=FMD[,1],vec=Ms$x)
aty<-findInterval(x=FMD[,2],vec=Ms$y)
mhat<-NULL
for(i in 1:length(atx)) mhat<-c(mhat,Ms$z[atx[i],aty[i]])
# estimation of the STIK function
u <- seq(0,10,by=1)
v <- seq(0,15,by=1)
stik1 <- STIKhat(xyt=FMD, s.region=northcumbria/1000,t.region=c(1,200),
                 lambda=mhat*mut/dim(FMD)[1], dist=u, times=v, infectious=TRUE)
```

```{r}
plotK(stik1)
```
````

after knitting, the plot doesnt appear in HTML. Does anyone has some idea what is going on?

Thank you so much!

title: build_site should ignore "packrat" folder by default
description:
Or maybe at least the following: "packrat/src","packrat/lib-R","packrat/lib-ext", "packrat/lib", "packrat/init.R" (the packrat.lock file might be nice to keep).

Otherwise packrat gets confused and tries to tangle .Rmd files in the src files of packages (which takes ages and will add unnecessary dependencies). It ignores them at the root, but not under e.g. _site.

title: including RMarkdown or Markdown with images in Shiny
description:
I have a RMarkdown document that need to be embedded in Shiny as documentation. There are several options:
- render rmd in shiny. But it's static content and doesn't need to be rendered in runtime.
- include rendered html with iframe like #792 , but the style doesn't match the ShinyDashboard.
- include rendered html with `includeHtml()`. This also broke the ShinyDashboard styles, i.e. the default page have a large empty box under the dashboard.
- include the rendered md and images with `includeMarkdown`. This is the simplest method that doesn't break ShinyDashboard. However there is a small problem.

The image in rendered md is like this

`![](workflow1_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-7.png)<!-- -->`

The `<!-- -->` doesn't show in RStudio preview but does show in Shiny app.

I tried to remove it and add some random caption inside `![]`, the problem solved. But I have to do this manually. There is an knitr option for rmd "add caption for image" looks like should solve this, but it didn't take any effect.

To solve this, either rendered markdown should take a different format, or `includeMarkdown` need be able to process this.

If you cannot reproduce this I can attach some sample file for test.

description:
Greetings,

The subject line says it all. The following ought to replicate.

      pdf_document: default

    \begin{align*}
    y_t&=\mu+\epsilon_t-\theta_1B\epsilon_t-\dots-\theta_qB^q\epsilon_t\cr
    &=\mu+(1-\theta_1B-\dots-\theta_qB^q)\epsilon_t\cr
    &=\mu+\mathbf{\Theta}(B)\epsilon_t,
    \end{align*}
    where $\mathbf{\Theta}(B)$ is a polynomial in the backwards shift operator $B$

title: It should be possible to import RMarkdown files
description:
A user asks [here](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/10966109/how-to-source-r-markdown-file-like-sourcemyfile-r) a very reasonable thing: to be able to "source" one RMarkdown file from another.  Although the user doesn't state this as the reason, the primary reason that comes to my mind is to be able to write one's entire codebase in the literate style, just like one [Literate Coffeescript](http://www.coffeescript.org#literate) file can import another.

Only one solution is offered, and Yihui [suggests that it is a bad idea](https://github.com/yihui/knitr/pull/812#issuecomment-53088636).  I have tried the solution and found that it works correctly in only simple situations, and more complex situations (such as A importing B importing C) cause errors (in that case, duplicate chunk labels for unnamed chunks).

I suggest that this be officially supported, with a new function for importing other RMarkdown files, due to the elegance and practicality of writing one's whole codebase literately, and having it be self-documenting.

title: rmarkdown::render within function gives error
description:
Hi,

I have a minor issue concerning a function I wrote containing `rmarkdown::render`. Specifically when using that function in combination with phyloseq-formatted data in a for-loop (or apply) gives an error while rendering.

# Minimal example

Function containing `rmarkdown::render`, that gives the error:
```r
# Method 1
my_render <- function(input) {
    rmarkdown::render(input = input)
}
my_render(input = "test.Rmd")
```

rmarkdown::render on its own does not give the error:
```r
# Method 2
input = "test.Rmd"
rmarkdown::render(input = input)
```

## Test example that always works
If test.Rmd contains this for-loop, everything is fine:
```r
test_df <- data.frame(taxa = rep(LETTERS[1:5], 2),
                      count = 1:10,
                      count2 = 11:20)
test_taxa <- unique(test_df$taxa)
test_list <- list()
for (z in test_taxa) {
  test_list[[z]] <- sum(test_df[which(test_df$taxa == z), c("count", "count2")]) / 
    sum(rowSums(test_df[, c("count", "count2")]))
}
test_list

title: Use output_format with base_format argument only
description:
I am creating a custom html_document format. using the html_document and **output_format** functions.

This is what I planned to do initially

```
knitr_opts <- knitr_options()
html_document_custom <- html_document()
output_format(knitr = knitr_opts,   base_format = html_document_custom)
```
This will NOT work since output_format requires a pandoc argument.
This means that despite the fact that I have an object, html_document_custom, with all the required goodies, I need to pass it argument by argument:

```
 output_format(
    knitr = knitr_opts,
    pandoc = html_document_custom$pandoc,
    keep_md = html_document_custom$keep_md,
    clean_supporting = html_document_custom$clean_supporting,
    df_print =  html_document_custom$df_print,
    pre_knit = html_document_custom$pre_knit,
    post_knit = html_document_custom$post_knit,
    pre_processor = html_document_custom$pre_processor,
    intermediates_generator = html_document_custom$intermediates_generator,
    post_processor = html_document_custom$post_processor,
    on_exit = html_document_custom$on_exit
  )
```

I think solution is error-prone and I am likely to run into issues if the arguments of output_format change in the future. 

I've also tried to trick the function like this:

```
output_format(knitr = knitr_opts,
              pandoc = html_document_custom$pandoc,
              base_format = html_document_custom)
```

This works, but the side effect is that all the pandoc arguments are duplicated. This has unwanted consequences on your final output. For example all your css will be added TWICE to your html output. 

- Am I using the correct mechanism ?
- If so, Would it be possible modify output_format so that is can run with the base_format argument alone?

Thanks for all the great work !

title: bugs in pdf_document extra_dependencies
description:
Hi, I discovered a few bugs in the `extra_dependencies` option in `pdf_document`. I found them out in an afford trying to load a latex package from a R function while using rmarkdown + knitr. 

1. [Fixed in PR #911 ] First of all, in the current github version of rmarkdown (https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/pdf_document.R#L176-L187), for `pdf_documents`, the content of `extra_dependency` is passed to a list called `format_deps`. This `format_deps` will not be put into real use unless `has_latex_dependencies(knit_meta)` is `TRUE`.  I think this bug will prevent people from using `extra_dependency` in most cases. 

~~2. Also, if people use the results of `latex_dependency()` directly to `extra_dependency`, they will receive the following error message:~~
~~YAML header:~~
```
---
title: "Untitled"
output: 
  pdf_document:
    keep_tex: true
    extra_dependencies: "`r rmarkdown::latex_dependency('multirow')`"
---
```
~~Error:~~
```
processing file: Untitled.Rmd
Quitting from lines 2-8 (Untitled.Rmd) 
Error in vapply(x, format_sci_one, character(1L), ..., USE.NAMES = FALSE) : 
  values must be length 1,
 but FUN(X[[2]]) result is length 0
Calls: <Anonymous> ... paste -> hook -> .inline.hook -> format_sci -> vapply
Execution halted
```


3. [Fixed in PR #911 ] Even if people find a way around to get the results of `latex_dependency` to `pdf_document`, the results of `latex_dependency`, as a list of 3, should not be append to `format_deps` directly (https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/pdf_document.R#L177). We should put a list round it so the whole list can be passed as an element. 


I have worked around solutions to question 1 & 3 and I will submit a PR very soon. Also, I added a feature so people can use `extra_dependencies` in the YAML section more easily.

title: render_site with Rmd parameters
description:
I started to use the `rmarkdown::render_site` function. At some point I had an `Rmd` file with parameters, and I wanted to render it several times with different options.

To do that, I adapted a custom site generator. I would like to know if you are interested in a pull request or at least export some functions so I don't need to use `:::`.

# render_site with rmarkdown parameters

I wrote a custom site generator named `site_with_params` based on [`default_site`](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/render_site.R#L154). The main changes with respect to the default_site are:

- The yaml header of `index.Rmd` needs to have `site: site_with_params` to use this site generator.
- An additional `files` section to `_site.yml` is required, that states how html files need to be rendered. An example of `_site.yml` is shown here (note the "files" section):

```yaml
name: "my-website"
navbar:
  title: "My Website"
  left:
    - text: "Home"
      href: index.html
    - text: "Domestic results"
       href: domestic.html
    - text: "Foreign results"
      href: foreign.html
files:
  index.html:
    src: index.Rmd
  domestic.html:
    src: domestic_foreign.Rmd
    params:
      type_of_flight: "domestic"
  foreign.html:
    src: domestic_foreign.Rmd
    params:
      type_of_flight: "foreign"
```

# Questions

- Would you would be interested in a pull request offering this "site with parameters" feature?
- In case you are not interested, would it be possible to export `rmarkdown:::site_config`, `rmarkdown:::input_as_dir`, `rmarkdown:::knitr_files_dir`, `rmarkdown:::dir_exists`, `rmarkdown:::copy_site_resources` and `rmarkdown:::knitr_root_cache_dir` so it is easy to provide custom site generators in other packages?

# Actual code

The code I wrote is adapted from `default_site` and uses several non-exported rmarkdown functions. 

This could be submitted as a PR if there is interest:

```r
#' Generate site with Rmd files with parameters
#' To use this site generator set \code{site: rmarkdown::site_with_params}
#' in the yaml header of the \code{index.Rmd} file.
#' Then in the \code{_site.yml} file, add a files section:
#'
#' \code{
#' files:
#'   index.html:
#'     src: index.Rmd
#'     params:
#'       opt1: Val1
#'   about.html:
#'     src: about.Rmd
#'     params:
#'       opt1: Val2
#' }
#'
#' @param input
#'
#' @export
site_with_params <- function(input, encoding = getOption("encoding"), ...) {

  # get the site config
  config <- rmarkdown:::site_config(input, encoding)
  if (is.null(config))
    stop("No site configuration (_site.yml) file found.")

  input_dir <- rmarkdown:::input_as_dir(input)
  output_file_options <- config[["files"]]
  # config[["files"]] has:
  # files:
  #   index.html:
  #     src: index.Rmd
  #     params:
  #       opt1: Val1
  #   about.html:
  #     src: about.Rmd
  #     params:
  #       opt1: Val2

  # define render function (use ... to gracefully handle future args)
  render <- function(input_file,
                     output_format,
                     envir,
                     quiet,
                     encoding, ...) {

    # track outputs
    outputs <- c()

    # see if this is an incremental render
    incremental <- !is.null(input_file)


    if (incremental) {
      all_input_files <- vapply(output_file_options, function(x) x[["src"]], character(1))
      output_files <- names(output_file_options[all_input_files %in% input_file])
    } else {
      output_files <- names(output_file_options)
    }
    sapply(output_files, function(x) {
      # we suppress messages so that "Output created" isn't emitted
      # (which could result in RStudio previewing the wrong file)
      output <- suppressMessages(
        rmarkdown::render(file.path(input_dir, output_file_options[[x]][["src"]]),
                          output_format = output_format,
                          output_file = x,
                          params = output_file_options[[x]]$params,
                          output_options = list(lib_dir = "site_libs",
                                                self_contained = FALSE),
                          envir = envir,
                          quiet = quiet,
                          encoding = encoding)
      )

      # add to global list of outputs
      outputs <<- c(outputs, output)

      # check for files dir and add that as well
      sidecar_files_dir <- rmarkdown:::knitr_files_dir(output)
      files_dir_info <- file.info(sidecar_files_dir)
      if (isTRUE(files_dir_info$isdir))
        outputs <<- c(outputs, sidecar_files_dir)
    })

    # do we have a relative output directory? if so then remove,
    # recreate, and copy outputs to it (we don't however remove
    # it for incremental builds)
    if (config$output_dir != '.') {

      # remove and recreate output dir if necessary
      output_dir <- file.path(input, config$output_dir)
      if (file.exists(output_dir)) {
        if (!incremental) {
          unlink(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
          dir.create(output_dir)
        }
      } else {
        dir.create(output_dir)
      }

      # move outputs
      for (output in outputs) {

        # don't move it if it's a _files dir that has a _cache dir
        if (grepl("^.*_files$", output)) {
          cache_dir <- gsub("_files$", "_cache", output)
          if (rmarkdown:::dir_exists(cache_dir))
            next;
        }

        output_dest <- file.path(output_dir, basename(output))
        if (rmarkdown:::dir_exists(output_dest))
          unlink(output_dest, recursive = TRUE)
        file.rename(output, output_dest)
      }

      # copy lib dir a directory at a time (allows it to work with incremental)
      lib_dir <- file.path(input, "site_libs")
      output_lib_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "site_libs")
      if (!file.exists(output_lib_dir))
        dir.create(output_lib_dir)
      libs <- list.files(lib_dir)
      for (lib in libs)
        file.copy(file.path(lib_dir, lib), output_lib_dir, recursive = TRUE)
      unlink(lib_dir, recursive = TRUE)

      # copy other files
      rmarkdown:::copy_site_resources(input, encoding)
    }

    # Print output created for rstudio preview
    if (!quiet) {
      # determine output file
      output_file <- ifelse(is.null(input_file),
                            "index.html",
                            output_files)
      if (config$output_dir != ".")
        output_file <- file.path(config$output_dir, output_file)
      message("\nOutput created: ", output_file)
    }
  }

  # define clean function
  clean <- function() {

    # build list of generated files
    generated <- c()


    # get html files
    html_files <- names(config[["files"]])

    # _files peers are always removed (they could be here due to
    # output_dir == "." or due to a _cache existing for the page)
    html_supporting <- paste0(rmarkdown:::knitr_files_dir(html_files), '/')
    generated <- c(generated, html_supporting)

    # _cache peers are always removed
    html_cache <- paste0(rmarkdown:::knitr_root_cache_dir(html_files), '/')
    generated <- c(generated, html_cache)

    # for rendering in the current directory we need to eliminate
    # output files for our inputs (including _files) and the lib dir
    if (config$output_dir == ".") {

      # .html peers
      generated <- c(generated, html_files)

      # site_libs dir
      generated <- c(generated, "site_libs/")

      # for an explicit output_dir just remove the directory
    } else {
      generated <- c(generated, paste0(config$output_dir, '/'))
    }

    # filter out by existence
    generated[file.exists(file.path(input, generated))]
  }

  # return site generator
  list(
    name = config$name,
    output_dir = config$output_dir,
    render = render,
    clean = clean
  )
}
```

title: Use spin with render_site
description:
Building a site from RStudio runs `rmarkdown::render_site(encoding = 'UTF-8')`, which renders all `.Rmd` files in the root directory. 

It will not render any `.R` files, which ordinarily is fine, since those don't typically produced HTML output. However, `rmarkdown::spin()` can knit any files—including `.R` files—and keeping R scripts as `.R` instead of `.Rmd` [can be advantageous](http://deanattali.com/2015/03/24/knitrs-best-hidden-gem-spin/).

Right now, if a `.R` script is included in a website project (like the minimal one below), it will not get knitted.

```r
#' ---
#' title: "Testing stuff"
#' output: html_document
#' ---

#' Here's some R code
2 + 2
```

It might be helpful to be able to specify a list of knittable files in `_site.yml` or somewhere else so that these non-`.Rmd` files are rendered when the site is built with `render_site()`. It is currently possible to include `.R` files in the built website with the `include:` YAML key, but including files only copies the raw file to the final site and does not render them.

title: Handle to modify knitted document header
description:
I find the following behavior potentially limiting: the `metadata` argument to `post_knit`, `pre_processor` and `post_processor` functions passed to `output_format` contains raw values from document YAML front matter *before* they are parsed by **knitr**, even though conceptually these functions are executed after knitting the document.

In my use case I have a metadata field containing an R expression, which I would like to access after it has been evaluated. In fact, I didn't find a way to get the knitted YAML metadata in the current API. What I would like to ultimately achieve is to process the *knitted* header in order to alter some of its fields before the document is handed over to pandoc.

I came up with a [`pre_processor` function](https://github.com/Bioconductor/BiocStyle/blob/49f727c6f4614d127334dcd69484a05757561680/R/rmd_common.R) which extracts the metadata header from the knitted md file by using `rmarkdown:::partition_yaml_front_matter`. But maybe there is a better way of modifying the document's front matter without the need of resorting to **rmarkdown**'s internal functions?

In summary, it would be great if you would consider providing ways to access the knitted document metadata, and to modify the document's front matter.

Thanks for your help, and keep up the good work!
Andrzej

title: Using rmarkdown::render fails to prompt for params when called from Rscript
description:
The following fails to prompt for Rmd parameters in a Shiny app

```
 Rscript -e "library(rmarkdown);render('test.Rmd',params='ask')"
```
instead, it fails with:

```Error in knit_params_get(input_lines, params) : 
render parameter configuration only allowed in an interactive environment
```

which is explicitly raised [in params.R](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/395d2a39b0cd3b3220ba5ab53bcb47302f9c7cae/R/params.R#L15-L16) testing that `interactive() == FALSE` 

However, by following [this hack](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/17328172/forcing-interactive-r-session) it is possible to "trick" R into thinking it is running interactive, as follows:

```
 Rscript -e "unlockBinding('interactive',as.environment('package:base'));assign('interactive',function() TRUE,envir=as.environment('package:base'));library(rmarkdown);render('test.Rmd',params='ask')"
```

In which case the Shiny app pops up and everything works.

I wonder if this test is really required in params.R.  I would like to be able to render rmarkdown files from the command line like this without requiring this workaround.  Am I misguided in my efforts?

The same question was posted on StackOverflow: http://stackoverflow.com/q/40517733/559676

title: Enhancement Request: Allow for Themes in RNotebooks

This HTML file can be shared with R programmers and non R-programmers alike, and include both raw code as well as an general narrative around the analysis being performed.

@yihui 's [site](http://statr.me/2016/08/creating-pretty-documents-with-the-prettydoc-package/) describes how RMarkdown can be augmented to produce documents with an aesthetically pleasing theme.

**Request**
RNotebooks provide a tremendous methodology for dissemination of analytics.  Ensuring they support themes in the generation of HTML output would be a fantastic addition.

title: redundant usage of metavariable `lang` and `babel-lang`
description:
Dear `rmarkdown`-team!

I am not sure, if I oversee something regarding the `"default"` pandoc templates for `rmarkdown::pdf_document`, but I think, there could be a simplified approach steering the language options via the YAML metavariables.

Currently there are four pandoc tex templates stored in `inst/rmd/latex`. The two older template versions

  - default.tex
  - default-1.14.tex

only use the meta variable `lang` via

```tex
\documentclass[... $if(lang)$$lang$,$endif$ ... ]{$documentclass$}
...
$if(lang)$
\ifxetex
  \usepackage{polyglossia}
  \setmainlanguage{$mainlang$}
\else
  \usepackage[shorthands=off,$lang$]{babel}
\fi
...
```

The two newer templates 

  - default-1.15.2.tex
  - default-1.17.0.2.tex

use
```tex
\documentclass[... $if(lang)$$babel-lang$,$endif$ ... ]{$documentclass$}
...
$if(lang)$
\ifnum 0\ifxetex 1\fi\ifluatex 1\fi=0 % if pdftex
  \usepackage[shorthands=off,$for(babel-otherlangs)$$babel-otherlangs$,$endfor$main=$babel-lang$]{babel}
$if(babel-newcommands)$
  $babel-newcommands$
$endif$
...
```
Therefore it is necessary in the latter case, to hand over both metavariables `lang` and `babel-lang` via the YAML header to steer the language settings.

By changing the two newer tex templates to 

```tex
\documentclass[... $if(lang)$$lang$,$endif$ ... ]{$documentclass$}
...
$if(lang)$
\ifnum 0\ifxetex 1\fi\ifluatex 1\fi=0 % if pdftex
  \usepackage[shorthands=off,$for(babel-otherlangs)$$babel-otherlangs$,$endfor$main=$lang$]{babel}
$if(babel-newcommands)$
  $babel-newcommands$
$endif$
...
```
only one metavariable would be required to steer the language for the babel package and in addition downwards compatability of the YAML-header and therefore the final Rmd document could be realised.

title: 'clean_supporting' argument to output_format() not inherited from base format
description:
Hi,
I've just run into the following, somehow unexpected behavior: when extending one of the existing format functions which has set the option `clean_supporting = FALSE` through a call to `output_format()` the `clean_supporting` is not retained but gets overwritten by the default value  `TRUE`. I consider this not consistent with the overall idea of how `output_format` works, because the rest of the arguments such as `knitr` or `pandoc` do not supersede the base format values but rather extend them.

``` r
library(rmarkdown)

base_format <- md_document()

base_format$clean_supporting

## [1] FALSE

new_format <- output_format(knitr=NULL,
                            pandoc=NULL,
                            base_format=base_format)

new_format$clean_supporting

## [1] TRUE

sapply(names(new_format), function(i) identical(base_format[[i]], new_format[[i]]))

##                   knitr                  pandoc                 keep_md 
##                    TRUE                    TRUE                    TRUE 
##        clean_supporting                df_print                pre_knit 
##                   FALSE                    TRUE                    TRUE 
##               post_knit           pre_processor intermediates_generator 
##                    TRUE                    TRUE                    TRUE 
##          post_processor                 on_exit 
##                    TRUE                   FALSE
```

Similar reasoning applies to the `on_exit` function. I would suggest modifying the default behavior of `output_format` in such a way that unless the argument `clean_supporting` is explicitly set to `TRUE/FALSE`, it's value gets inherited from the `base_format` argument (if present).

Cheers,
Andrzej

title: Applying a pandoc filter after pandoc-citeproc
description:
Hi there, I have spent several hours looking for a solution but have come up empty. Any ideas would be greatly appreciated.

I'm creating documents that need citations in APA format. I'm using the APA citation style, which works great with one exception:

In APA guidelines 6th edition, Section 6.12 mention that:

> Precede the final name in a multiple-author citation in a running text by the word and. In parenthetical material, in tables and captions, and in the reference list, join the names by an ampersand (&).
> 
> as Kurtines **and** Szapocznik (2003) demonstrated
> as has been shown (Kurtines **&** Szapocznik 2003)

However, with pandoc-citeproc all "and" are rendered as ampersands.

> as Kurtines **&** Szapocznik (2003) demonstrated
> as has been shown (Kurtines **&** Szapocznik 2003)

I know this is because in-text citations are not supported by CSL and there is no way to define the in-text "and". I have written a simple filter that modifies the output of `pandoc-citeproc` to overcome this issue. The filter works on the AST and replaces all in-text `&` with `and`.

``` r
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
intext_and <- function(x) {
  gsub("(\"citationMode\":\\{\"t\":\"AuthorInText\".*?\\})(.*?\\}\\],\\[.*?)(&)(.*?\\}\\]\\]\\})", "\\1\\2and\\4", x)
}

ast <- readLines(file("stdin"))
write(intext_and(ast), stdout())
```

The problem is, I need to call this filter after `--filter pandoc-citeproc`. From [another issue](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/592) I get the impression the call to `pandoc-citeproc` is always appended at the end of the system call and there is no way to apply another filter after it. Is this indeed the case? Is there any way to apply a filter after `pandoc-citeproc`?

title: Relative paths are rewritten to absolute paths
description:
I just discovered something unusual in how relative paths containing `../` are handled when rendering Rmarkdown documents. I also posted about this issue on [StackOverflow](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/39481092/how-to-stop-relative-paths-from-being-rewritten-to-absolute-paths-in-rmarkdown-d). Let's say I have a project with a structure as shown below: ``` ./ ├── files/ │   ├── some_image.jpg │   └── test.Rmd └── some_other_image.jpg ``` And I want to render the Rmarkdown document `test.Rmd` into HTML containing both jpegs `some_image.jpg` and `some_other_image.jpg`, like so: ``` --- title: "Path Test" output: html_fragment: self_contained: false keep_md: true --- Path without ../ is not altered ![Unaltered](some_image.jpg) Path with ../ is converted to an absolute path! ![Altered](../some_other_image.jpg) ``` If I create the HTML document with `rmarkdown::render("files/test.Rmd", clean = FALSE)`, it produces the following HTML: ```

Path without ../ is not altered

Path with ../ is converted to an absolute path!

``` If you look at the `src` attribute for each image, you can see that **the image path that was specified using `../` gets rewritten to use an absolute path!!** Moreover, this conversions _only_ happens when the specified file exists! My questions: Why is this happening? This doesn't happen to me when manually using `pandoc` to convert this very same markdown to HTML? And if you inspect the intermediate markdown file produced, the path to `some_other_image.jpg` is still `../some_other_image.jpg`. And what can I do to stop it? It works fine on my particular machine of course, but this is a big problem if the page is going to be deployed somewhere else. I'm running Rmarkdown version 1.0 with R version 3.3.1 on debian testing, in case that's relevant for reproducing.

title: Empty _files directory created with ioslides, self_contained and lib_dir
description:
Normally if you use the `self_contained: false` YAML option for an rmarkdown document (lets say it's called `document.Rmd` for example), external dependencies such as css, javascript and any figures that get created are placed in a special directory following the naming convention "name_of_Rmd_file" + "_files" (so here the external dependencies folder for my example .Rmd file would be called `document_files`)

If you use the `self_contained: false` option along with the `lib_dir` YAML option and the `fig.path` knitr option when rendering a standard `html_document` file, no directory called `document_files` gets created. Consider the following example:

``````

---
title: "No _files dir created"
output: 
  html_document:
      self_contained: false
      lib_dir: libs

---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set("cache" = FALSE, "fig.path" = "figures/")
```

## Including Plots
You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```
``````

Not creating the `document_files` directory makes sense here: all the plots that get created get placed in the the `figures/` directory, and all the javascript/css gets placed the `libs` directory, so there is no need for  the `document_files` directory.

But if I use the same setup when creating an `ioslides_presentation`, a `document_files` directory _is_ created, and it's empty, because all the external dependencies are placed elsewhere! To see this, contrast the output from this example file with the previous one:

``````

---
title: "Empty _files dir created!"
output: 
  ioslides_presentation:
      self_contained: false
      lib_dir: libs

---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set("cache" = FALSE, "fig.path" = "figures/")
```

## Including Plots
You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```
``````

My question: Is there anyway to prevent these empty directories from being generated when rendering stand alone ioslides presentations? Or is this a bug?

title: consider disabling 'markdown_in_html_blocks'?
description:
Right now, it appears that `pandoc` will attempt to render markdown encountered in HTML blocks. Unfortunately, this can lead to surprising / unexpected behavior in some cases: ``` $ cat inline-html.md Foo $ pandoc inline-html.md --from markdown --to html --output inline-html.html && cat inline-html.html 
Foo</td>
``` One can opt-out of this behavior with `-markdown_in_html_blocks`, e.g. ``` $ pandoc inline-html.md --from markdown-markdown_in_html_blocks --to html --output inline-html.html && cat inline-html.html Foo ``` This would help users who generate raw HTML avoid somewhat surprising behavior, when generating indented HTML (or HTML with contents that are indented). However, it certainly is possible that some users rely on the 'markdown in HTML' behavior, so I'm not sure if this would be a good change. It's also possible that we need to instruct users to generate HTML with `htmltools::htmlPreserve`, or perhaps even that some of the `htmltools` APIs for generating HTML should do this by default. Any thoughts on if we should handle this; and if so, how?

title: Please allow us to disable param defaults
description:
This is more of a request than an issue.

Currently, when a parameterized .Rmd is created, a default value must be coded for each param. For example, if I have the following param in the YAML...

``` yaml
other: 
      value: first
      choices: [first, second, third]
      input: select
      label: Other
      multiple: yes
```

...then I must specify a default option to go into the 'value' spot. If I leave this spot blank, it throws an error*. If I try knitting this doc with the above code, then backspacing this param widget so that no value is showing, it returns the first available value (from my choices) in the rendered doc.

It seems that RMarkdown requires a default value for every param in order to render. Is there a way I could create a parameter with no defaults (i.e., a param that passes through to the output as NULL)?

*There seems to be some NULL capability built into params in RMarkdown, but it is unpredictable (or I am using it incorrectly). For example, when I leave the 'value:' spot blank (or I make it NULL) and knit the doc with parameters, I can sometimes get an option to appear in the select widget that says "Unspecified (NULL)" and another option that says "Use a custom value." Selecting the first option _does_ pass a NULL value through to the output. Selecting the second option resets the widget to display my original choices, but throws an error during the knit. It seems like the more coder-friendly alternative would be to simply allow RMarkdown to interpret these NULL values (or blank widgets) as such, without displaying the extra options.

Thank you,

Diana

title: Unnecessary metadata append at the end of intermerdiates *.spin.Rmd
description:
Hey, 

Trying to understand how work `outpur_dir`, `intermediates_dir` and _working directory_ when using `rmarkdown::render` for Rmd and R files, I encounter a strange behaviour for knitting R files.

`render` looks at the file extension to see if it is an R file or a Rmd file. When it sees it is an R file, it will uses 
`knit::spin` to generate a *.spin.Rmd. Then something that looks odd to me : it will append at the end of the file, a metadata. 

Here the lines of code 

``` r
if (identical(tolower(tools::file_ext(input)), "r")) {
        spin_input <- intermediates_loc(file_with_meta_ext(input, 
            "spin", "R"))
        file.copy(input, spin_input, overwrite = TRUE)
        intermediates <- c(intermediates, spin_input)
        spin_rmd <- knitr::spin(spin_input, knit = FALSE, envir = envir, 
            format = "Rmd")
        intermediates <- c(intermediates, spin_rmd)
        knit_input <- spin_rmd
        metadata <- paste("\n", "---\n", "title: \"", input, 
            "\"\n", "author: \"", Sys.info()[["user"]], "\"\n", 
            "date: \"", date(), "\"\n", "---\n", sep = "")
        if (!identical(encoding, "native.enc")) 
            metadata <- iconv(metadata, to = encoding)
        cat(metadata, file = knit_input, append = TRUE)
    }
```

Why append this at the end of the file ? It seems unnecessary.
I could see why a default metadata is generated if no metadata is at the start of the file. But at the end don't see why. 

Conclusion, I do not know if it's something or not. It may be on purpose and I missed why. However, I prefered to ask and reporting this instead of do nothing.

title: font-awesome not loaded correctly when using `html_dependency_font_awesome` and calling `shiny::icon()`
description:
I found out about the `html_dependency_foo()` functions while creating an htmlwidget and I was told I can use these functions to include common shiny libraries (https://github.com/ramnathv/htmlwidgets/issues/218)

I think I may have found a bug with including font-awesome though, and I'm not sure if it belongs here, in htmlwidgets, or in shiny, so I'll just tag (ie spam....) a few people @wch @jcheng5 @jjallaire @ramnathv @yihui @jmcphers

I can call `createWidget()` and add bootstrap and jquery to the dependency list using `rmarkdown::html_dependency_foo()` with no problem.  But when I also try to include font-awesome (`rmarkdown::html_dependency_font_awesome()`), and then use `shiny::icon()` to render an icon, then the icons don't end up showing up in a non-shiny environment (such as when running the widget in the RStudio console).

It looks like the problem is that when calling `html_dependency_foo()`, the dependency resource path gets set to `lib/foo` (eg `lib/font-awesome-4.5.0/css/font-awesome.min.css`), but inside the `shiny::icon` function, the resource path gets set to `shared/font-awesome/css/font-awesome.min.css` instead.  This file actually leads to nowhere and is the reason font-awesome doesn't work. If instead of calling the `shiny::icon` function I just use `tags$i(class = "fa ...")` then the fonts do render properly because the `lib/` path gets used.

I hope this makes sense

title: Message handling in R Notebooks
description:
Thanks a lot for the new R Notebooks, the new possibilities are really exciting!

I encountered two issues with messages, which work fine in a standard `html_document`:
1. In this case I use `message` inside the function to display the variable which is plotted.
   In contrast to a standard `html_document`, the output of `message` is placed  on top of 
   the graphs, not in between them.

``` r
{r, message=TRUE}
message("hi")

library(ggplot2)
vars <- names(mtcars)

plots <- function(var) {
  p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes_string("mpg", var)) + geom_point()
  print(p)
  message(var)
}

purrr::walk(vars[1:3], plots)
```

(2) It is not possible to surpress messages via chunk options, neither inside the chunk, nor one level deeper inside the function:

``` r
{r, message=FALSE}
message("hi")

library(ggplot2)
vars <- names(mtcars)

plots <- function(var) {
  p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes_string("mpg", var)) + geom_point()
  print(p)
  message(var)
}

title: html_fragment and scripts, lib_dir etc.
description:
## Problem

Libraries such as rCharts and ggplot2 can be included in an html_fragment, their dependent files live in the `<body>`.

Many newer htmlwidgets place JS and CSS in the document head. This is of course sensible, especially for CSS.

However, I have not found a way to programmatically create an html_fragment and import the right header files that I can rely on.

My use case is that I dynamically generate (among other things) feedback graphs (via openCPU) for my survey software. I'm using my own bootstrap styles to keep the feedback in the same look as the site.

If I use html_fragment as the output, anything that would go in the lib_dir is not created in the first place. Same for md_document.
## Possible solutions I can think of
1. I can use html_document, parse the <head>, drop title, cruft and bootstrap and put it in my own header. But that seems likely to fail at some point and isn't very elegant.
2. You could re-write html_fragment to use the lib_dir directory option, then I could use this more easily as a parseable "necessary resources for inclusion" list. I'm not sure this would suffice since you have a quite colorful mix of external inlined styles and scripts in many rmarkdown-generated documents.
3. You could re-write html_fragment to inline styles and scripts for htmlwidgets like rCharts does. Would generate invalid HTML, but would work. Probably this is not something that rmarkdown is completely in charge of and it would be hell to maintain?
4. I could also include html_documents as iframes. I would now have to insert my styles via a header template. This seems most future-proof and elegant, but I wouldn't want to do it in cases where I generate lots of small fragments, and the way my program is written, this is very flexible for the user and I can't tell from rmarkdown's output for html_fragment whether any dependencies have gone missing.

So, solution 4 sounds best?

The most efficient way to do that is to use this yaml instead: ``` --- output: github_document --- ``` Here's the goofy html preview: All of this markdown looks as expected on GitHub and all html files look as expected in Safari. title: Abnormal use of resources when using download function from package downloader
description:
Hello,

I encountered an issue when using the _download()_ function from package _downloader_ in a Rmd document (see code below). It is not such a big issue and there is an easy fix, but I just wanted to report it.

``` r dl_clean, message=FALSE
# load packages
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(downloader, data.table, dplyr)

# download and load the data (Windows setup)
if(!file.exists("./data/insertion_raw.csv")) {
      if(!file.exists("./data")) {dir.create("./data")}
      dataUrl <- paste0("https://data.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr/explore/dataset/", 
                        "fr-esr-insertion_professionnelle-master/download?format=csv")

      download(dataUrl, dest="./data/insertion_raw.csv", mode="wb")
} else message("The dataset had previously been downloaded.")
```

In this case, _download.file()_ would report a warning: “downloaded length 978696 != reported length 200”. I use the _downloader::download()_ function instead and it suppresses this warning but the download bar continues further than 100%. When using Knit HTML this results in an endless printing of “=” signs in the R Markdown pane of R Studio. During this time on my computer (Dell XPS 13), R Studio proc usage becomes abnormally high, and the application stops responding. After a few minutes it stops freezing and the html document is successfully compiled, but R Studio remains unstable until you close and restart it (evaluation of R code can become very slow).

Specifying quiet=TRUE avoids this issue.

``` r dl_clean2, message=FALSE
download(dataUrl, dest="./data/insertion_raw.csv", mode="wb", quiet=TRUE)
```

md_document(variant="markdown", preserve_yaml=T) produces two YAML blocks
description:
The `md_document` format interacts strangely with the `preserve_yaml` option when the specified markdown variant is `markdown` (ie pandoc markdown).

Consider the following `test.Rmd`:

``````

---
title: Example
output:
  md_document:
    variant: markdown
    preserve_yaml: true

---

An example.

```{r}
2 + 2
```
``````

Converting this with `rmarkdown::render("test.Rmd")` produces the following on my Mac with either rmarkdown from CRAN or the latest version from github:

``````

---
title: Example
output:
  md_document:
    variant: markdown
    preserve_yaml: true

---

---
output:
  md_document:
    preserve_yaml: True
    variant: markdown
title: Example
...

An example.

``` {.r}
2 + 2
```

    ## [1] 4
``````

This appears to be because `md_document` always passes pandoc the `--standalone` option (see [here](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/md_document.R#L63)), which causes pandoc to output the yaml metadata itself (converting the terminating delimiter to `...`), appended after the metadata block from rmarkdown's output. This does not happen with the default `markdown_strict` variant, only `markdown`. May I suggest not giving pandoc the `--standalone` option when `preserve_yaml` is true?

The creates problems when knitting Rmd to markdown with metadata for static-site generators like jekyll.

title: Resolving HTML dependencies with the same name but requiring different files
description:
I just ran into a situation where a certain dependency object may point to different files depending on the actually required files, e.g.,

``` r
fooDependency = function(modules = c('a', 'b')) {
  htmlDependency(
    script = c(if ('a' %in% modules) 'a.js', if ('b' %in% modules) c('b1.js', 'b2.js'))
  )
}
```

For example, users may only want to use the module `a`, in which case I only need to load `a.js`.

rmarkdown seems to be ignoring later dependency objects with the same name as a previous dependency object, so if I have two HTML widgets using different modules of a library, the second widget will not render correctly because its JS dependencies are not included in the HTML head.

I feel the dependency objects in knitr metadata should be merged in this case, instead of using the first one to override all following ones.

title: Combat belief that captions do not work by setting `fig_caption = TRUE`?
description:
Is it possible to make the default for `fig_caption = TRUE` (especially for pdf documents)?

I keep encountering the false belief that R Markdown does not support captions (e.g. from users at last week's CSP conference, in emails from students, at the end of this article: http://www.ssc.wisc.edu/sscc/pubs/RFR/RFR_RMarkdown.html)

I think people try to set the chunk option `fig.cap` and then see no effect because `fig_caption = FALSE`. This behavior led me to believe that captions did not work, until Yihui told me otherwise.

This is just a suggestion because I do not know the other side of the story (e.g. why `fig_caption = FALSE`).

description:

title: Order of filters in pandoc invocation
description:
Hi.

I'm an author of [pandoc-crossref](https://github.com/lierdakil/pandoc-crossref) filter, and apparently using this filter with RMarkdown can be challenging (judging from user reports)

From skimming over sources in this repository, I found that custom Pandoc arguments are passed after `--filter pandoc-citeproc`. This invariably breaks filters that leverage citation syntax for other purposes (like pandoc-crossref does), due to `pandoc-crossref` being applied before other filters.

Solution would be to move `--filter pandoc-crossref` to the end of argument list, or at least somewhere after custom Pandoc arguments.

Thanks.

title: render markdown with paths relative to output directory
description:
If I have an Rmd file named `somefile.Rmd`, with the yaml header

```

---
title: Some title
output: md_document

---
```

using 

```
rmarkdown::render('test.Rmd', 
                  output_file='test/test.md')
```

will create `test/test.md`, with figures in the directory `test/test_files`. However, figure paths in the markdown document will be relative to the directory `test.Rmd` lives in (`test/test_files/figure-html/chunk-1.png`). It makes sense that Rmarkdown might use this convention, in order to convert from markdown to html from the current working directory. However, if viewed as the final output from rmarkdown, the markdown file is not very self-contained: in order to view it or convert it to another format, a user needs to know what directory the original Rmarkdown file was in.

Moreover, if I use

```
rmarkdown::render('test.Rmd', output_file='test.md', output_dir='test')
```

It will produce the same files, except this time, the paths in the markdown document will be absolute--which leads to the same issue. Intuitively, since the figure directory is put in same folder as `test.md`, I would expect the figure paths to be relative to that file, so using the markdown file doesn't necessarily require knowledge about where it was generated from.

It seems like the cases right now are..
1. generated figure paths are relative to Rmarkdown file (output_file case)
2. generated figure paths are absolute (output_dir case)
3. generated figure paths are relative to markdown file (no case? except for manually tinkering with rmd file/knitr)

Case 3 seems very useful and intuitive if a markdown document is being considered as a final product of render, rather than an intermediate. Is there a simple way to do get this using render? Otherwise, does it seem reasonable to implement it, either by changing the default behavior of output_file/dir or adding an options for it? I'm happing to try implementing a solution if it seems reasonable, and someone points me in the right direction.

(also, I remember reading a knitr issue similar to this. Sorry if I've repeated it!)

title: Will we ever be able to use `pandoc-citeproc` with RMarkdown again?
description:
First, I love love love RMarkdown. Thank you for making it.

Second, I've been writing all my manuscripts using [pandoc-style citations](http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_bibliographies_and_citations.html#citation-syntax) as specified on [RStudio's markdown page](http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com). For example:

```
Blah blah [see @doe99, pp. 33-35; also @smith04, ch. 1].

Blah blah [@doe99, pp. 33-35, 38-39 and *passim*].

Blah blah [@smith04; @doe99].
```

**But**, as of https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/commit/b6e3f39f731b28af5ff1823c0de8714d8fb78df7 RMarkdown [no longer supports](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/b6e3f39f731b28af5ff1823c0de8714d8fb78df7/inst/NEWS#L11-L18) `pandoc-citeproc`:

> ```
> * For PDF/LaTeX output, citations are processed via natbib or biblatex instead
>   of pandoc-citeproc. The ciation package natbib or biblatex can be chosen using
>   the argument `citation_package` in `pdf_document()`, `beamer_presentation()`,
>   and `tufte_handout()`. LaTeX is compiled to PDF via latexmk
>   (https://www.ctan.org/pkg/latexmk/); if it is not installed, a simple
>   emulation will be used (run pdflatex/xelatex/lualatex, bibtex, and makeindex
>   a few times). You are recommended to install latexmk, and please note latexmk
>   requires a Perl installation (this is important especially for Windows users).
> ```

So,
1. Will `pandoc-citeproc` support ever be coming back?
2. Is there any way I can use `pandoc-citeproc` given how Rmarkdown works now?

Basically, I'm trying to figure out what I need to do with all my pandoc-style-citation-formatted RMarkdown manuscripts because they don't render properly anymore :-(

title: Feature request: Placing bibliographies before the end of the document
description:
From the [R Markdown V2 documentation](http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_bibliographies_and_citations.html):

> Bibliographies will be placed at the end of the document.

Some journals require articles to include figures or tables after the references.  At the moment, this means that you have to create a main document, then create a second document for the figures and tables, and manually stitch them together.

It would be nice to have a feature allowing you to override the position of the bibliography in an R Markdown document.

title: render's document_format does not always use output_file name
description:
If I have an Rmd file named `somefile.Rmd`, with the yaml header

```

---
title: Some title
output: 
    html_document:
        keep_md: true

---
```

Then using `rmarkdown::render('somefile.Rmd', output_file='newname.html')` will reports named `newname.html` and `newname.md`.

However, if I try to render the file using

``` r
rmarkdown::render('somefile.Rmd', output_file='newname.html',
  output_format=c("html_document", "md_document")
```

it will produce reports names `somefile.html` and `somefile.md`.

Intuitively, I would have expected the above command to have produced `newname.html` and `newname.md`. Is this the intended behavior? If so, is there a way to rename the output **and** specify multiple output formats when using render? 

I'm happy to try and make changes if someone can point me in the right direction (and I can find some free time!).

(this is with Rmarkdown 0.8.1)

title: R inliners with special characters (ampersand) inside LaTeX environment not escaped automatically
description:
R string containing ampersand (&) displays correctly when used outside LaTeX environment, such as `\begin{itemize}`

This works and ampersand is automatically escaped by `pandoc` (or `knitr`?):

```

---
output:
  pdf_document

---

`r "Guns & Roses"`
```

Now, when the R inliner with ampersand string is specified inside LaTeX environment, following error is thrown: 
`! Misplaced alignment tab character &.`:

```

---
output:
  pdf_document

---

\begin{itemize}
\item `r "Guns & Roses"`
\end{itemize}
```

The `R` inliner must be wrapped in the `\verb`, when inside any LaTeX environment. That works:

```

---
output:
  pdf_document

---

\begin{itemize}
\item \verb| `r "Guns & Roses"`|
\end{itemize}
```

It would be great to have the same/consistent behaviour inside and outside the environment, i.e. without the need for the user to manually insert `\verb`

title: ioslides_presentation ignores custom css option
unexpected results when rendering html_vignette() output via "Knit HTML" button
description:
If I have a vignette `foo.Rmd` with YAML like so:

```

---
title: "Whatever"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
author: "Jenny Bryan"
output:
  rmarkdown::html_vignette:
    keep_md: true
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Whatever}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}

---
```

and I render via the "Knit HTML" button, no files are created within the package's `vignettes` subdirectory. No `foo.md`, `foo.html`, etc. Yet I get an HTML preview. I gather it's _all_ being placed in a temporary directory?

The only way to get the expected files to appear locally appears to be via _Build > Document_ or `devtools::document(roclets = "vignette")`.

[The documentation](http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/package_vignette_format.html) says that "All options support for `html_document` also work for `html_vignette` so I guess I expect it to function like all other Rmd files destined for HTML. I can't figure out why "Knit HTML" would work differently when output is `html_vignette`.

If you alternate between these two ways of rendering the vignette, this makes it really easy to commit and push out-of-date `.md`, `.html` and figs.

title: Invalid rendering of hyperlink text that contains a URI scheme prefix
description:

For example, `[elovl4a](http://identifiers.org/ncbigene/393769)` renders as [elovl4a](http://identifiers.org/ncbigene/393769). Some preliminary gene names contain a prefix and a colon that are on the [list of URI schemes](http://www.iana.org/assignments/uri-schemes/uri-schemes.xhtml). This works fine here at GitHub and also in [MarkdownPad2](http://markdownpad.com/); for example, `[im:7139490](http://identifiers.org/zfin/ZDB-GENE-050522-453)` renders as [im:7139490](http://identifiers.org/zfin/ZDB-GENE-050522-453). However, with rmarkdown it renders invalidly as two nested `` tags; see below. The error seems to happen with any URI scheme prefix, e.g. `gopher`, `http`, etc. Example of the error, using an `im:` prefix, which is also used for instant messaging URIs: ``` r writeLines("[im:test this](http://example.org)", "test.Md") rmarkdown::render("test.Md") grep("im:test this

" ``` Example without error, using an `in:` prefix, which is not used in any URI scheme: ``` r writeLines("[in:test this](http://example.org)", "test.Md") rmarkdown::render("test.Md") grep("in:test this

description:
I'm currently trying to update some pages on a website that is a collaboration between several people where I'm the only Windows user.

In our `_output.yaml` we have a line:

```
css: libs/local/nav.css
```

When any of the other collaborators render a markdown file, the resulting HTML has:

```
<link rel="stylesheet" href="libs/local/nav.css" type="text/css" />
```

But when I render, I get

```
<link rel="stylesheet" href="libs\local\nav.css" type="text/css" />
```

It's probably not going to make a difference in practice, but it's not ideal that every time I commit a file, the diff will show all these lines as changed, and every time someone else renders that file it will again show a change in that file.

I would like to be able to force rmarkdown to add unix style slashes even when I render on Windows.

title: Plotting in `for` loop after second-level header
description:
I do not know whether this is a bug or just my lack of understanding. Consider the situation where I want to create a PDF file that includes a multitude of similar plots. To get multiple plots side by side I use `par(mfrow = c(3, 2))`. In the minimal example below the number of plots is 18, so given the specified layout R supposedly creates three high-level plots. Here, I use `fig.height=7` just to force each plot on a new page. 

When running the example below, however, the subsection `## Plot` is on the second page of the document and the first and second high-level plot is printed to the same page (the second not being visible as it extends beyond the page).

`````` r

---
title: "Multiple figures after header"
output: pdf_document

---

# Section

Some text

## Plot

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.height=7}
par(mfrow = c(3, 2))
for (i in 1:18) plot(i, main = i)
`` `
``````

This **only** occurs if there is standard text in of the sections. When removing `Some text` the following example works just fine:

`````` r

---
title: "Multiple figures after header"
output: pdf_document

---

# Section

## Plot

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.height=7}
par(mfrow = c(3, 2))
for (i in 1:18) plot(i, main = i)
`` `
``````

Here, section `## Plot` is on the first page and each of the three plots are on a separate page. As a workaround I found that encapsulating the text in the markdown syntax for links (`[text](link)`) works as intended:

`````` r

---
title: "Multiple figures after header"
output: pdf_document

---

# Section

[Some text]()

## Plot

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.height=7}
par(mfrow = c(3, 2))
for (i in 1:18) plot(i, main = i)
`` `
``````

I played around with some of the plot related chunk options and also tried `layout()` instead of `par(mfrow)`, but to no avail.  This also occurs when removing the layout options, so that each of the 18 plots is expected to be on a new page. I also observed that removing the second level header (here: `## Plot`) solves the problem or, in other words, that there must be no second level header before plotting in a `for` loop.

title: parallel render()'s with different output_file's overwrite each other
description:
I commonly write `.Rmd` templates, that then get rendered to create a report with different input parameters. However, if more than one such job is being rendered at the same time, since the name of the intermediate `.md` file is based on the `input`, all jobs write to the same intermediate. The result is that I (silently) get wrong reports. Here is a MWE. `test.Rmd`: ``` I am writing to `r outname`.html. ``` `test.sh`: ``` #!/bin/bash R --vanilla -e "outname=\"${1}\";require(rmarkdown);render(\"test.Rmd\",output_file=\"${1}.html\")" ``` Run two at the same time: ``` for x in one two; do (./test.sh $x &); done grep "writing to" *.html # one.html:

I am writing to two.html.

# two.html:

I am writing to two.html.

``` **Non-workarounds:** - "specify `intermediates_dir`", but if there's images in the document this fails (#500) - "first render to `md_document`, then render to html", but the same problem occurs because render actually outputs to `input.utf8.md`, with no chance to change this **A fix?** It seems better to use `tempfile()`, e.g. ``` knit_output <- intermediates_loc(tempfile(tmpdir=".",fileext=".knit.md")) ``` ... at least when output_file is specified.

title: output_dir and yaml for lib directories vs style files.
description:
I posted an issue yesterday, this one is different.  This is a minor issue about lib_dir vs css fields in the yaml.

Now suppose my Rmarkdown document resides in /tmp, but ultimately I want to use lib and style directories in /tmp/01, and render an html into /tmp/01.  The file and directory structure prior to generating a report are this:

```
/tmp/foo.Rmd
/tmp/01/lib
/tmp/01/style.css
```

The appropriate yaml to get everything working right  (and as far as I know the only yaml) is:

```

---
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: false
    lib_dir: 01/lib
    css: style.css

---
```

After a call to render("foo.Rmd", output_dir=/tmp/01),  the generated html files will have this in it:

```
<script src="lib/jquery-1.11.0/jquery.min.js"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css" type="text/css" />
```

A more intuitive yaml to me was this because it did not treat lib_dir and css as different relative to the generating .Rmd.

```

---
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: false
    lib_dir: 01/lib
    css: 01/style.css

---
```

(In actual fact a more intuitive yaml to me was one without 01 because I wanted to think of the files as relative to the html but that isn't how it works.)

But if you do that you end up with html like this:

```
<script src="lib/jquery-1.11.0/jquery.min.js"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="01/style.css" type="text/css" />
```

The issue is that 01 is the directory the html file is in, and that style sheet won't be found.  The point here is the css and lib_dir field have two different relative behaviors when used with output_dir.  I am just letting you know about this counter-intuitive aspect of yamls and rmarkdown render with output_dir that could slow down adoption.

title: error = T
description:
Today I noticed that I cannot easily override the "new" `error = F` default in rmarkdown from outside the render function, by simply calling `opts_chunk$set(error=TRUE)`. The workaround I use now is to call `html_document()` first, and then set `output_format$knitr$opts_chunk$error = TRUE` (e.g. [here](https://github.com/rubenarslan/formr/blob/master/R/rmarkdown_options.R#L26)).

I want to suggest that this be simplified, i.e. through an option like `break_on_error` in the render function. 

Once that option exists, it would be great if the new options gear icon next to the "Knit HTML" button in Rstudio had this as a checkbox, since the error handling that rmarkdown already has sometimes doesn't meet my needs (see also https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/381). Also, I sometimes prefer to keep errors in my report (e.g. if I run a bunch of models and one does not converge, that's something I want in my report in some cases).

title: base64, pandoc 1.14.x, ggvis dependencies
description:
It looks like you are [already planning on updating pandoc](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/422#issuecomment-97207511) and have already [been bitten](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/79f595b6dbcc28703a6136d2afafc9a11c6b6d49/R/html_dependencies.R#L15) a [few times](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/2224).

While debugging why ggvis plots fail to display when rendered self_contained using pandoc 1.14 I discovered the ggvis dependencies are being encoded in base64 (double encoded?) and as such there is name mangling going on.

A guess is that the change implementing [Improved building of data URIs in SelfContained.](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/commit/d5469b30fe9903a37a4966df75609e88aad9ef55) [fixing pandoc issue 1940](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/1940) whereby data URIs not prefixed with "text/" are encoded is responsible since rmarkdown base64 encodes when self_contained is true but the [base64 tags](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/3d46213d750fd4ebb83e73d0df357f081c73f49f/R/base64.R) don't include "text/" and the [pandoc self contained data URI handling](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/05d238cd397c2a2720089a643192c1f1c7bad0df/src/Text/Pandoc/SelfContained.hs) doesn't look like it checks if something is already encoded' it is causing a double encoding.

title: unused argument error depending on output format
description:
I have an RMarkdown file with leading YAML:

```
title: "empty"
output:
  pdf_document: {}
```

I have some generic code that is attempting to render a document. That code blindly specifies `self_contained=TRUE` which produces the error:

```
> rmarkdown::render("empty.Rmd", output_options=list(self_contained=TRUE))
Error in (function (toc = FALSE, toc_depth = 2, number_sections = FALSE,  : 
  unused argument (self_contained = TRUE)
```

If I change to `output: html_document` there is no error, as one would expect.

If I specify multiple outputs and have `html_document` first, there is no error:

```
output:
  html_document: {}
  pdf_document: {}
```

If, however, I reverse the order of the output formats, we see the error again:

```
output:
  pdf_document: {}
  html_document: {}
```

The `self_contained` option does not apply to PDFs; is there a way to give `output_options` which will only apply to specific output formats (or _not_ apply to specific output formats)? Alternatively, could the fact that the `output_options` value is not used be an information (or warning) message instead of a hard error?

The example below is a bit difficult, but I have had real life examples where there's actually overlap of the legend names and legend boxes (see below).
